During the 1971 Liberation War, Ziaur Rahman played a pivotal role, famously broadcasting the declaration of independence from Chittagong on March 27th, earning him the title “Announcer of the Liberation”. He commanded sectors within the Bangladesh Forces, ultimately leading ‘Z Force’, a conventional brigade. After independence, he rose through the ranks of the Bangladesh Army, becoming Chief of Army Staff in 1975. Following the assassination of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in August 1975, a period of political instability ensued, marked by coups and counter-coups. Ziaur Rahman was briefly removed from his position but regained power through the November 1975 Sipahi–Janata Revolution led by Abu Taher, becoming the de facto head of government under Justice Sayem. He consolidated his power, suppressing dissent and executing those involved in previous coups. He officially became President in 1977, retiring from the army as a Lieutenant General in 1978.

As President, Ziaur Rahman founded the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) in 1978, ushering in a return to multi-party politics and civil liberties, including freedom of the press and speech. He focused on economic development, initiating programs to boost irrigation and food production. He also pursued improved relations with Western countries and China, shifting away from the close alignment with India favored by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman. He worked to establish regional cooperation, laying the groundwork for the creation of SAARC. However, his rule was marked by numerous coup attempts, leading to the establishment of military tribunals and the execution of at least 200 soldiers and air force personnel, giving him a reputation for strictness.

Ziaur Rahman was assassinated in 1981 in Chittagong during an attempted coup. His death sparked a divided legacy in Bangladeshi politics. He is credited with restoring order after the turbulent years following independence and establishing a democratic framework by abolishing the one-party BAKSAL system. However, he is also criticized for suppressing opposition. His economic reforms are seen as contributing to the rebuilding of the nation's economy and his adoption of certain Islamic policies garnered popular support. The BNP, founded by him, remains a significant political force in Bangladesh, with his widow, Khaleda Zia, later becoming a three-time Prime Minister.

title: Jessie Mae Brown Beavers
text:
Jessie Mae Brown Beavers was a Los Angeles-based journalist who dedicated her career to community service and advocacy. Born on March 18, 1923, she spent her entire life in Los Angeles and passed away on September 6, 1989, at the age of 66. Her mother, Arnetta Hoyt Brown, was a Baptist deaconess. Beavers received a bachelor’s degree in sociology from the University of California, Los Angeles. 

Beavers began her journalism career in 1944 as an editor of the family section of the *California Eagle*. In 1949, she transitioned to the *Los Angeles Sentinel*, where she remained an editor for the next four decades until her death. Throughout her career, she was a prominent figure in media organizations, notably being a founder and leader of the Los Angeles chapter of the National Association of Media Women in 1966. She received the Outstanding Woman in Journalism Award from the University of Southern California chapter of Theta Sigma Phi in 1969.

Beyond her work with the *Los Angeles Sentinel*, Beavers was heavily involved in civic duties. She served for sixteen years on the Los Angeles Human Relations Commission, beginning with her appointment by mayor Tom Bradley in 1973. During her time on the commission, she collaborated with Toshiko S. Yoshida, particularly during the American bicentennial, and led the affirmative action subcommittee. In 1982, she spearheaded hearings addressing racial bias within the entertainment industry. She also contributed to the Los Angeles County Music and Performing Arts Commission. Demonstrating her ambition for broader political representation, Beavers ran for a seat on the Los Angeles City Council in 1987.

Beavers was actively involved in several community organizations, including Jack and Jill and the Lullaby Guild. She was recognized for her contributions at various times; in 1968, she received recognition from the President's Youth Council, and in 1972, she was honored alongside notable figures like Quincy Jones and Ruth Washington by the Committee of Women for Good Government. A tribute event was held in her honor in 1973 at the Beverly Wilshire Hotel, attended by prominent individuals such as Mayor Bradley, judge Vaino Spencer, columnist Gertrude Gipson, and clubwoman Leontyne Butler King, with singer Thelma Houston hosting the event.

In 1947, Jessie Mae Brown married Leroy A. Beavers Jr., an insurance executive and nephew of businessman George A. Beavers Jr. Actress Dorothy Dandridge served as a bridesmaid at their wedding. The couple had three children together. Later in life, in 1979, Beavers was the victim of an assault and robbery at her home. She is buried at Forest Lawn Cemetery in Glendale, California.

title: Guillermo Rigondeaux
text:
Guillermo Rigondeaux Ortiz, born September 30, 1980, is a Cuban professional boxer who achieved significant success both as an amateur and a professional. As an amateur, Rigondeaux excelled, winning gold medals in the bantamweight division at both the 2000 and 2004 Summer Olympics. He was also a seven-time Cuban national champion at bantamweight between 2000 and 2006, compiling a record of roughly 475 fights with only 12 losses. Boxing trainer Freddie Roach considers Rigondeaux “probably the greatest talent I've ever seen”, praising his speed, power, counter-punching, athleticism, reflexes and footwork. He is highly regarded as one of the greatest defensive boxers in history.

Rigondeaux’s amateur career included detailed victories in both Olympic games. In 2000, he defeated opponents from Tunisia, Japan, Azerbaijan, the United States and Russia to claim gold. In 2004, he progressed through the tournament defeating boxers from China, Pakistan, Russia, Uzbekistan and finally Thailand in the gold medal match. He was also successful in numerous other amateur tournaments, winning championships in Belfast, Northern Ireland, Astana, Kazakhstan, Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, Mianyang, PR China, Moscow, Russia and Cartagena, Colombia. 

He defected from Cuba in 2007, initially intending to turn professional alongside other Cuban Olympians, but briefly attempted to return home before ultimately re-defecting in 2009 via Mexico City to Miami. He signed with Arena Box-Promotion and began his professional career in May 2009 with a TKO victory over Juan Noriega. He quickly accumulated wins, including capturing the NABA super bantamweight title in September 2009 and signing with Top Rank promotions in 2010.

Rigondeaux won the interim WBA super bantamweight title in November 2010 with a controversial split decision over Ricardo Cordoba, and then secured the full WBA title in January 2012 by knocking out Rico Ramos in the sixth round. He unified the super bantamweight division in April 2013 with a unanimous decision victory over Nonito Donaire, adding the WBO and *The Ring* titles to his collection. Despite holding multiple championships, Rigondeaux struggled to secure fights with other top boxers in the division. He defended his titles against Teon Kennedy, Roberto Marroquin, Sod Kokietgym and Hisashi Amagasa, though some of these bouts were criticized for being uncompetitive.  



He later fought Drian Francisco in November 2015, winning by unanimous decision. Throughout his career, Rigondeaux has been known for his technical skill and defensive prowess, but also for the difficulties in securing high-profile fights. His amateur and professional records demonstrate a consistent pattern of victory, establishing him as a highly skilled and accomplished boxer.

title: Lennie Hayton
text:
Lennie Hayton, born Leonard George Hayton in New York City in 1908, was a versatile American musician known for his work as a composer, conductor, and arranger. He was instantly recognizable for his signature captain’s hat, worn at a distinctive angle. Growing up in a Jewish family where his parents appreciated classical music, Hayton developed an early interest in the piano, learning from player piano rolls. Though his parents initially discouraged jazz, he discovered it at age sixteen and soon left school to play piano with the Broadway Hotel Orchestra.

His career gained momentum when Paul Whiteman hired him in 1928 as a pianist and arranger. During his time with Whiteman, he collaborated with prominent musicians like Frankie Trumbauer and Bing Crosby. Following a reduction in the Whiteman orchestra due to economic conditions in 1930, Hayton joined the Charles Previn Orchestra before reuniting with Bing Crosby in 1932. He became Crosby’s musical director, leading orchestras for recordings and radio broadcasts, including the hit song “Brother, Can You Spare a Dime?” in 1932. He continued as Crosby’s musical director for radio and film, notably for *Going Hollywood* in 1933, marking the start of his Hollywood career.

Hayton eventually became a musical director at Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer in 1940, a position he held until 1953, overseeing the studio’s prolific output of movie musicals. He received four Academy Award nominations for his work on *The Harvey Girls* and *The Pirate*, and won an Oscar for *On the Town* in 1950, alongside Roger Edens. He also arranged the music for *Singin’ in the Rain* and received further nominations for *Star!* and *Hello, Dolly!*. Later in his career, he arranged Frank Sinatra’s initial recording of “Something” by George Harrison. He also composed pieces like “Apple Blossoms” with several contemporaries, and co-arranged Hoagy Carmichael’s “Stardust” with Artie Shaw.

Hayton’s personal life included two marriages. His first wife, Helen Maude Gifford, died in 1943. He married Lena Horne in 1947, also acting as her musical director. Their marriage, though initially strategic for Horne’s career advancement, developed into genuine affection but was strained by the challenges of an interracial relationship and eventually led to separation. A lifelong smoker and drinker, Hayton died of a heart attack in Palm Springs, California, in 1971 and is buried in Hollywood Forever Cemetery.

title: Richard Burton
text:
Richard Burton was a Welsh actor born Richard Walter Jenkins Jr. in 1925, renowned for his distinctive baritone voice and celebrated as a significant Shakespearean performer. While often hailed as a potential successor to Laurence Olivier, some critics felt he never fully realized that potential, a perception sometimes linked to his well-documented struggles with alcohol. Despite seven Academy Award nominations, he never won, though he received numerous other accolades including a BAFTA, a Golden Globe, a Grammy, and a Tony Award for his role as King Arthur in *Camelot*. He reached peak box-office success in the mid-1960s, becoming one of the highest-paid actors globally, earning substantial fees and percentages of film grosses. His personal life, particularly his two marriages and divorces from Elizabeth Taylor, generated consistent public attention.

Burton’s early life was marked by hardship. He was one of thirteen children born to a Welsh-speaking family; his father was a coal miner, and his mother worked as a barmaid. He lost his mother to postpartum infections at the age of two, and was subsequently raised by his elder sister, Cecilia, and her husband. He grew up in a tough steel town and was deeply affected by his family's experiences with the dangers of coal mining. Despite the challenging circumstances, his family prioritized his education, making him the first to attend secondary school. He displayed a talent for both academics and performance, winning prizes for his singing and showing an aptitude for literature.

A pivotal figure in his early development was Philip Burton, a schoolmaster who took a strong interest in the young Richard, eventually becoming his legal guardian and providing intensive tutoring. Philip encouraged Richard's acting ambitions and ultimately facilitated a change of surname to Burton via deed poll. Burton's formal education was interrupted by service in the Royal Air Force during World War II, where he was deemed unfit for pilot training and served primarily in an administrative role. 

Burton began his acting career with small roles in the theatre and film, gaining recognition for his performance in Emlyn Williams' *The Last Days of Dolwyn* in 1949. This led to a contract with Alexander Korda, allowing him to work on various film projects. He steadily gained experience through a series of roles in British films, establishing a reputation for his intelligence and presence.  Early roles included parts in *Now Barabbas* and *The Woman with No Name*. Throughout this period, he continued to hone his craft, receiving guidance and encouragement from key figures in the theatre and film industries, setting the stage for his later rise to international stardom.

title: Xi Jinping
text:
Xi Jinping was born in Beijing in 1953, the son of prominent communist leader Xi Zhongxun. His early life was significantly impacted by the Cultural Revolution; his father was purged, leading to the family’s exile to rural Shaanxi province, where Xi experienced hardship and lived among the peasantry for seven years. He repeatedly applied to join the Communist Party during this time, eventually succeeding in 1974. He received his education at Tsinghua University, studying chemical engineering as part of a program for workers, peasants, and soldiers. 

Xi’s political career began in Hebei province, where he worked to address issues impacting local farmers, and then moved through Fujian and Zhejiang provinces, steadily rising through the ranks. In Fujian, he served as vice governor and focused on economic development, promoting concepts like the “Golden Triangle” and attracting investment. As Party Secretary of Zhejiang, he oversaw significant economic growth and cultivated a reputation for tackling corruption. A brief but important posting followed in Shanghai in 2007, where he was Party Secretary for seven months.

In 2007, Xi joined the Politburo Standing Committee, the highest decision-making body in China, and was designated as Hu Jintao’s presumed successor. He became Vice President and Vice Chairman of the Central Military Commission in 2008, solidifying his position. He officially became the paramount leader of China in 2012 as General Secretary of the CCP and Chairman of the CMC, and in 2013, he assumed the presidency. In 2016, he was formally recognized as the “core” leader of the party, and in 2018, term limits for the presidency were removed, enabling him to seek further terms. He was re-elected state president in March 2023, securing an unprecedented third term.

As leader, Xi has implemented extensive policies to strengthen party discipline and unity, most notably through a sweeping anti-corruption campaign that targeted both current and retired officials. He has also focused on “common prosperity,” introducing policies aimed at reducing inequality and alleviating poverty. He’s overseen significant economic reforms, expanding support for state-owned enterprises and promoting technological advancement. His response to the COVID-19 pandemic initially involved a strict “zero-COVID” policy, which was later abandoned following widespread protests.

Xi’s foreign policy has been characterized by a more assertive approach, particularly in relation to the United States, the South China Sea, and the Sino-Indian border. He has championed the Belt and Road Initiative to expand China's global influence, particularly in Africa and Eurasia. Relations with Taiwan have deteriorated under his leadership, culminating in the passage of a national security law in Hong Kong that curtailed political opposition.

Since assuming power, Xi’s tenure has seen increased censorship, mass surveillance, and concerns about human rights, particularly regarding the treatment of Uyghurs in Xinjiang. He has also fostered a cult of personality around himself, and his political ideology, “Xi Jinping Thought,” has been incorporated into the party and national constitutions. He has centralized power by taking on multiple leadership roles and establishing new CCP committees focused on national security, economic development, and military modernization.

title: Ahmed Mumin Warfa
text:
Ahmed Mumin Warfa was a Somali botanist who dedicated his life to both scientific research and peacebuilding within his country. He is best known for co-discovering the plant species *Cyclamen somalense* alongside Mats Thulin. Prior to the Somali civil war, Warfa was a professor of biology and agriculture at the Somali National University, where he also engaged in research, specifically focusing on identifying endemic species, particularly in the northeastern Bari region of Somalia. 

The outbreak of the civil war in 1991 dramatically altered Warfa’s work. With the closure of the Somali National University, he transitioned into a role focused on reconciliation. He worked as a translator for the United Nations and actively participated in establishing councils aimed at bringing about peace in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. This work, however, placed him in danger, and in 1994 he survived an assassination attempt, highlighting the risks associated with his peace efforts and the opposition he faced from various militia leaders.

Following the escalating conflict, Warfa emigrated from Somalia, initially residing in Nairobi, Kenya, before ultimately settling in the United States. There, he continued his academic career, teaching biology at both Salt Lake Community College and Brigham Young University in Utah. Despite his relocation, he maintained his connection to the field of botany, regularly attending and contributing to herbology conferences as a speaker.

Throughout his time in the United States, Warfa remained engaged with Somali affairs. He continued to work as a reconciliator, collaborating with both the United Nations and the Somali President, and also became involved in fundraising initiatives for Somali institutions, such as Hiiraan University. 

In 2020, Warfa returned to Somalia, accepting the position of rector – or president – of Zamzam University of Science and Technology in Mogadishu. He continued in this role until his death on March 15, 2021, succumbing to complications arising from COVID-19. He is survived by his twelve children: Sumaya Mumin, Ismail Mumin, Daud Ahmed Mumin, Hibo Mumin, Farah Mumin, Mohamed Mumin, Aisha Mumin, Yusuf Mumin, Dahir Mumin, Halima Mumin, Fadumo Mumin, and another daughter also named Fadumo Mumin.

title: Alf Garland
text:
Alfred Barrett Garland, born on March 19, 1932, and passing away on March 9, 2002, was a prominent figure in both the Australian Army and the Returned and Services League of Australia (RSL). He served as the National President of the RSL from 1988 until 1993, and was known for his direct and often controversial views, which frequently put him at odds with the Keating government of the time.

Garland dedicated 35 years to a career in the Australian Army, demonstrating considerable leadership and skill. A significant early command came in 1965 when he led the 1st Special Air Service squadron during operations against Indonesian forces in Borneo. His service extended to the Vietnam War, where he held the position of second-in-command of the 7th Battalion, Royal Australian Regiment. He also served as Australia’s chief liaison officer to United States forces during the conflict, a role requiring strong diplomatic and operational capabilities. 

Prior to his national role, Garland was President of the RSL branch in the Australian Capital Territory. As National President, he became a public voice on a range of issues, often sparking debate with his strong opinions. Beyond veteran’s affairs, Garland actively engaged in political and social commentary. He was a staunch monarchist, and in 1998, represented New South Wales as a delegate for the Australian Monarchist League at the Australian Constitutional Convention. There, alongside Bruce Ruxton, he vigorously opposed the movement towards Australia becoming a republic. Their consistent opposition to republican arguments, including a deliberate attempt to prolong debate by recounting his family's historical ties to the British Crown, proved disruptive and frustrating to those advocating for a republic. He also held leadership positions within the Australian Monarchist League, serving as chairman for both the NSW and ACT branches.

Garland’s concerns extended to economic and immigration policy. He actively campaigned against the Multifunction Polis (MFP), a technology city project funded by Japan. Furthermore, he publicly expressed concerns about the level of Asian immigration to Australia. In 1988, he advocated for changes to immigration selection policies, stating the need to maintain Australia as a “predominantly European” nation, and famously declaring “We want to retain Australia for Australians.” 

After a prolonged illness, Garland died at the age of 69 from motor neurone disease, leaving behind a legacy as a dedicated military officer and a vocal, sometimes divisive, advocate for his beliefs.

title: Rachel Bilson
text:
Rachel Bilson, born August 25, 1981, in Los Angeles, is an American actress who comes from a family deeply rooted in the entertainment industry. Her father, Danny Bilson, is a writer, director, and producer, and her mother, Janice Stango, is a therapist. She has an older half-brother and two younger half-sisters. Her family background includes Jewish and Catholic heritage, resulting in a “Chrismukkah” upbringing. Her great-grandfather worked in the movie trailer department for RKO Pictures, and her great-grandmother was a screenwriter.

Bilson began her acting career with appearances in commercials for brands like Subway, Raisin Bran, and Pepto-Bismol. She made her television debut in 2003 with small roles in *Buffy the Vampire Slayer* and *8 Simple Rules for Dating My Teenage Daughter*. Her breakthrough role came with the series *The O.C.*, where she was initially cast for a few episodes but became a regular due to the popularity of her character, Summer Roberts, and her romantic storyline with Seth Cohen, played by Adam Brody. During her time on *The O.C.*, she received several accolades including three awards at the 2005 Teen Choice Awards and was featured in *Maxim* and *FHM* magazines, though she previously turned down opportunities for seminude photoshoots, believing her body was private.

She transitioned to film with *The Last Kiss* in 2006 and then starred in the action film *Jumper* in 2008, where she met her future partner, Hayden Christensen. Bilson continued to appear in television, including guest spots on *Chuck* and *How I Met Your Mother*. From 2011 to 2015, she led *Hart of Dixie* as Dr. Zoe Hart, a series executive produced by *The O.C.* creator Josh Schwartz. She later joined the cast of *Nashville* in 2017 and starred in the short-lived ABC drama *Take Two* in 2018. More recently, she co-launched the podcasts *Welcome to the OC, Bitches!* with Melinda Clarke, revisiting *The O.C.*, and *Broad Ideas with Rachel Bilson* with Olivia Allen, featuring interviews with entertainment industry figures.

Beyond acting, Bilson has a strong interest in fashion. She’s described as a “fashion junkie” with a vintage style, and in 2008 launched a clothing line, Edie Rose, with DKNY Jeans, aiming for affordable fashion. She later collaborated with Steve Madden to launch the online shoe platform ShoeMint in 2011, and designed a shirt for Invisible Children in 2013. She was unfortunately the target of burglaries by the "Bling Ring" which resulted in the loss of much of her fashion collection.

Bilson dated *The O.C.* co-star Adam Brody from 2003 to 2006. She then began a relationship with Hayden Christensen in 2007 and, after a brief period where an engagement was called off, the couple reconciled and had a daughter in 2014 before separating in 2017. Both Bilson and Christensen are advocates for the No Kids Policy, protecting celebrity children from unwanted paparazzi attention.

title: Abdul Ilah Khatib
text:
Abdul Ilah Mohammad Khatib, born on March 31, 1953, is a Jordanian politician and diplomat who has held several prominent positions within the Jordanian government and with the United Nations. He is perhaps best known for his multiple terms serving as Jordan’s Minister of Foreign Affairs. He was appointed as the UN Special Envoy to Libya on March 7, 2011, a role reflecting his extensive experience in international affairs.

Khatib’s educational background is substantial, demonstrating a focus on international studies and economics. He earned a Master’s degree in International Economics from Johns Hopkins School of Advanced International Studies. He furthered his education with a Master’s degree in International Communications from the American University in Washington, D.C., and completed a Bachelor’s degree in Political Science from the School of Political Science in Athens, Greece. 

His career in public service began in 1984 as a diplomat at the Jordanian Embassy in Washington, D.C., a position he held for four years. He then moved to a role within the Jordanian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, serving as Head of the Private Office from 1988 to 1993. During this period, he was also involved in the Arab-Israeli peace talks, overseeing Jordan’s contributions from 1992 to 1993. 

Khatib transitioned to the private sector briefly, becoming General Manager of Dammam Investment Company in 1994 and holding that position until 1995. He also served on the board of directors for several investment, industrial, and financial corporations during 1993-1994. He returned to government service in January 1995 as the Minister of Tourism and Antiquities under Zaid ibn Shaker, a role he held until February 1996.  Following this, he was Managing Director of Jordan Cement Factories Company from 1996 to 1998.

He then embarked on a series of appointments as Minister of Foreign Affairs under different prime ministers. He first served in this capacity from August 1998 to June 2000 under Abdelraouf al-Rawabdeh. He briefly held the position again in March 1999, for a single month, under Fayez al-Tarawneh. A more extended period as Minister of Foreign Affairs followed under Ali Abu al-Ragheb, from June 2000 to January 2002, and then again under Marouf al-Bakhit from November 2005 to November 2007. 

Beyond his governmental and corporate roles, Khatib has also been involved with academic institutions, serving as a member of the board of trustees of the American Center of Oriental Research. He is married and has three children.

title: Raúl Esparza
text:
Raúl Eduardo Esparza, born October 24, 1970, is an American actor widely recognized for his work on Broadway and television. He has become a prominent figure in the theatre world since the 2000s, earning acclaim and numerous award nominations for his stage performances. He is also known for his role as ADA Rafael Barba on *Law & Order: Special Victims Unit*, joining the show in a recurring capacity in its fourteenth season before becoming a series regular for seasons fifteen through nineteen. 

Esparza's theatrical career began with his 2000 Broadway debut in a revival of *The Rocky Horror Show*, for which he won a Theatre World Award. He quickly followed this with roles in *Cabaret*, *Taboo*—earning his first Tony Award nomination—*Chitty Chitty Bang Bang*, and the acclaimed 2006 revival of *Company*, which garnered him a second Tony nomination. He continued to demonstrate his versatility with performances in plays by Pinter and Mamet, receiving Tony nominations for both *The Homecoming* (2008) and *Speed-the-Plow* (2009). Notably, he is one of only two performers to have been nominated for a Tony Award in all four acting categories. His stage work extends beyond Broadway, including productions of *Evita*, *Twelfth Night* with Anne Hathaway, and more recent appearances in *Road Show* and *Oliver!*.

Beyond the stage, Esparza has appeared in films like Sidney Lumet's *Find Me Guilty* and Wes Craven’s *My Soul to Take*. He has also had television roles in shows like *Pushing Daisies*, *Medium*, *Hannibal*, and *The Path*. He lent his voice as a narrator for Stephen King’s audiobook *Under the Dome* and has performed in concerts across the country.

Esparza’s family history is rooted in Cuba; his parents fled Fidel Castro’s regime in the 1960s. His father and grandmother escaped by boat, while his paternal grandfather defected through Spain. His maternal lineage traces back to Catalonia, Spain. He was raised in Miami, Florida, and attended Belen Jesuit, graduating in 1988 with a Silver Knight Award in Drama. He later earned degrees in Drama and English from New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts in 1992. He explored his ancestry on the genealogy program *Finding Your Roots*, discovering a long history of family business ownership and deep roots in Catalonia. 

His role on *Law & Order: SVU* saw him portray ADA Rafael Barba, becoming the first series regular ADA in several seasons and the first male ADA in the show's history. Despite leaving the show in 2018 to return to stage work, he has made guest appearances in later seasons, demonstrating the character's enduring impact. Esparza is openly bisexual, a fact he revealed in a 2006 New York Times profile, and was married to Michele Marie Perez from 1994 to 2008.

title: Kevin Anderson (tennis)
text:
Kevin Anderson, born in 1986, is a South African former professional tennis player who reached a career-high ranking of world No. 5 in July 2018, becoming the first South African to achieve this since Kevin Curren in 1985. He began playing tennis at age six and demonstrated athletic ability in running alongside his tennis pursuits. He first competed professionally at 17, quickly gaining a ranking and showing early promise.

Anderson’s collegiate career was spent at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, where he earned All-American honors in both singles and doubles, winning the national doubles championship in 2005-06 with partner Ryan Rowe. He led Illinois to a national runner-up finish in 2007, facing future ATP star John Isner in the championship match.

Turning professional, Anderson steadily climbed the ranks, achieving his first ATP Tour title at the South African Open in Johannesburg in February 2011, defeating Somdev Devvarman in the final. He continued to improve, reaching his first major final at the 2017 US Open, ultimately losing to Rafael Nadal. Interestingly, as a 12-year-old, he regularly competed against Nadal on the junior circuit. 

His most notable achievement came at the 2018 Wimbledon Championships. He reached the final after an epic semi-final victory over John Isner, a match lasting six hours and 36 minutes – the second-longest in major tournament history. He then lost the final to Novak Djokovic. Throughout his career, Anderson consistently demonstrated an ability to defeat top players, including a win over Novak Djokovic in 2008 and Andy Murray at the 2015 US Open.

Anderson experienced periods of injury, notably in 2016 with knee, shoulder and ankle issues, which impacted his performance. He achieved a career milestone in 2015, breaking into the top 10 of the ATP rankings. He enjoyed several strong runs in Masters 1000 events, reaching quarterfinals in Indian Wells, Madrid, Toronto and Cincinnati. 

He retired in May 2022 at the age of 35, but announced a comeback in July 2023. His career included multiple Challenger titles and consistent performances at Grand Slam level, reaching the fourth round or better in all four majors. He was known for his powerful serve and aggressive baseline game, making him a formidable opponent on all surfaces. He faced some of the biggest names in tennis repeatedly, often achieving notable victories against them.

title: Philippe Coutinho
text:
Philippe Coutinho, born in Rio de Janeiro in 1992, is a Brazilian professional footballer currently playing for Vasco da Gama. He’s renowned for his vision, passing ability, dribbling skills, and talent for scoring from long range. Coutinho developed through Vasco da Gama’s youth system and signed with Inter Milan in 2008 at age 16, although he remained on loan with Vasco until he turned 18, becoming a key player during his time there and helping them achieve promotion to the top tier.

He officially joined Inter Milan in 2010, making his debut in the UEFA Super Cup, and later contributing to a crucial Champions League victory against Bayern Munich. Despite scoring a couple of goals for Inter, he struggled for consistent playing time and was loaned to Espanyol in 2012, where he impressed by scoring five goals in 16 appearances. He returned to Inter, but continued to find opportunities limited.

Coutinho’s career took off when he joined Liverpool in January 2013. He quickly became a fan favourite, earning accolades such as being named to the PFA Team of the Year in 2015 and winning Liverpool’s Player of the Year awards in both 2015 and 2016. He established himself as a crucial part of the team, demonstrating impressive skill and playmaking ability. 

In January 2018, he made a high-profile move to Barcelona for a substantial fee. While at Barcelona, he secured two La Liga titles and various domestic trophies. Following a period where he wasn't a regular starter, he was loaned to Bayern Munich for the 2019–20 season, where he was part of the team that achieved a treble win – the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and UEFA Champions League. He then spent a loan spell at Aston Villa, which later became a permanent transfer.

On the international stage, Coutinho made his debut for Brazil in 2010 and has represented his country in several major tournaments, including the Copa América in 2015 and 2016, and the FIFA World Cup in 2018, where he scored two goals. He was also part of the Brazil squad that won the 2019 Copa América.

Coutinho’s early life was spent in Rio de Janeiro, where he was a shy child who discovered his passion for football through his older brothers. Starting with futsal, he honed his skills on the streets before joining a local academy, eventually being scouted by Vasco da Gama. His journey reflects a rise from humble beginnings to becoming a prominent figure in the world of professional football.

title: Dewi Sartika
text:
Dewi Sartika, born on December 4th, 1884, in Cicalengka, was a prominent figure in Indonesian history, recognized as a pioneer in women’s education and later honored as a National Hero. She was the daughter of Sundanese nobility, R. Rangga Somanagara and R. A. Rajapermas. Following her father’s death, she was raised by her uncle, receiving a traditional Sundanese upbringing alongside exposure to Western culture through the wife of a local resident assistant. Even as a child, she demonstrated a passion for teaching, often simulating classroom scenarios during play.

In 1904, Dewi Sartika established Sakola Istri in Bandung, marking the founding of the first school specifically for women in the Dutch East Indies. Initially located at the Pendopo in Bandung Regency, the school later moved to Jalan Ciguriang and was renamed Sakola Kaoetamaan Isteri (School of Excellence for Women) in 1910. Her dedication and the importance of her mission quickly led to expansion; by 1912, nine similar schools were operating across West Java, and by 1920, every city and regency in the region had its own establishment. In 1929, the school underwent another name change, becoming known as Sakola Raden Dewi. 

Dewi Sartika’s personal life included marriage to Raden Kanduruan Agah Soeriawinata, a teacher at Sakola Karang Pamulang, in 1906. Her contributions to education were formally acknowledged during her lifetime with the Order of Orange-Nassau, awarded on the 35th anniversary of Sekolah Kaoetamaan Isteri.

Sadly, Dewi Sartika did not live to see Indonesian independence. She passed away on September 11th, 1947, in Cineam, Tasikmalaya, while evacuating Bandung amidst the fighting of the Indonesian independence war. Her remains were later moved from Cineam to Makam Para Boepati Bandung. 

Her legacy endures in Indonesia today. Streets have been named in her honor, including the street where her school was located, and her name is recognized in various cities throughout the country. Furthermore, in 2016, Google commemorated her 132nd birthday with a Google Doodle, demonstrating her continued significance. In 1966, she was officially bestowed the title of Heroine of the National Movement, solidifying her place as a crucial figure in Indonesia’s history.

title: Jennifer Maia
text:
Jennifer Maia, born in Curitiba, Brazil in 1988, is a professional mixed martial artist currently competing in the bantamweight division of Invicta FC, where she is the reigning champion. Her combat sports journey began with soccer, transitioning to Muay Thai at age 15 where she earned national titles, before adding boxing and ultimately mixed martial arts to her skillset. She began her professional MMA career in 2009, quickly winning her first four fights by finish.

Early in her career, Maia faced both setbacks and successes, including a loss to Vanessa Porto and a quick knockout loss to Sheila Gaff. She scored a notable victory over Jéssica Andrade before joining Invicta Fighting Championships in 2013. Within Invicta, she competed for the flyweight title, eventually capturing the interim title in 2016 with a win over Porto in a rematch of their earlier encounter. She was later crowned the undisputed champion when the original titleholder was stripped, and successfully defended the flyweight championship twice before vacating it in 2018. 

Maia then signed with the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC), where she competed in the women’s flyweight division for twelve bouts. While in the UFC, she faced several top contenders including Liz Carmouche, Roxanne Modafferi (whom she defeated twice), and Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC Flyweight Championship, ultimately losing to Shevchenko via unanimous decision. She also had rematches with Katlyn Chookagian and faced opponents like Jessica Eye and Manon Fiorot. A positive drug test in 2019 resulted in a six-month suspension. She earned a Performance of the Night bonus for her submission win over Joanne Calderwood. After her contract with the UFC expired, she was not re-signed.

In 2024, Maia returned to Invicta FC, immediately challenging for and winning the bantamweight championship against Talita Bernardo, adding to her previous reign as the Invicta flyweight champion. She also participated in a professional grappling match against Beatriz Mesquita, which she lost by submission. Prior to her MMA career, Maia also had a professional boxing career, winning all three of her bouts by decision or TKO. Throughout her career, Maia has earned multiple accolades, including being tied for fourth in the UFC’s women’s flyweight division for the number of bouts competed in and ranking highly in several statistical categories. She is also a WGP Kickboxing Lightweight Champion with one successful title defense.

title: Valerie Harper
text:
Valerie Harper, born August 22, 1939, in Suffern, New York, was a celebrated American actress whose career spanned Broadway, television, and film. She began her performing journey as a dancer, debuting on Broadway in *Li'l Abner* and continuing with roles in productions like *Wildcat* and *Take Me Along*. Her early film work included small parts in *Rock, Rock, Rock!* and the film adaptation of *Li’l Abner*.

Harper achieved widespread recognition for her portrayal of Rhoda Morgenstern, initially on *The Mary Tyler Moore Show* from 1970 to 1974, and then as the star of her own spinoff series, *Rhoda*, which ran from 1974 to 1978. This role earned her four Emmy Awards, including one for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series, as well as a Golden Globe Award. She received further Golden Globe nominations for her performances in the films *Freebie and the Bean* (1974) and *Chapter Two* (1979). 

Her television career continued with the sitcom *Valerie* (1986-1987), but she was controversially fired after two seasons following a salary dispute. The show continued as *Valerie’s Family* and then *The Hogan Family*, with her character written out. She successfully sued the production company, Lorimar, and was awarded $1.4 million plus a percentage of the show’s profits.

Later in her career, Harper returned to the stage, earning a Tony Award nomination in 2010 for her performance as Tallulah Bankhead in *Looped*. She also toured with the play *Golda’s Balcony*, portraying Golda Meir, and made guest appearances on television shows like *Touched by an Angel*, *Sex and the City*, and *Desperate Housewives*. In 2013, she appeared as a contestant on *Dancing with the Stars*.

Harper's personal life included a marriage to Richard Schaal from 1964 to 1978, and a later marriage to Tony Cacciotti in 1987, with whom she adopted a daughter, Cristina. She was actively involved in the women’s liberation movement and co-founded the charity L.I.F.E. (Love Is Feeding Everyone) with Dennis Weaver.

In 2009, Harper was diagnosed with lung cancer, and in 2013, she revealed she had leptomeningeal carcinomatosis. Despite this prognosis, she continued to work and fight the disease for several years. She died on August 30, 2019, in Los Angeles, and is buried at Hollywood Forever Cemetery. Before her death, she famously participated in a pact with magician and mentalist Oz Pearlman, revealing a secret code word to be used after her death to test the validity of psychic claims.

title: Pogo (musician)
text:
Christopher Nicholas Bertke, known professionally as Pogo, is an electronic musician born in South Africa and now based in Australia. He is recognized for his unique style of music creation, often described as plunderphonics, where he constructs tracks almost entirely from pre-existing sounds – quotes, melodies, and effects – sourced from films, television programs, and other media. His work frequently features minimal additional musical elements beyond these sampled sounds.

Pogo’s musical projects include utilizing samples from well-known films like *Pulp Fiction* and a more expansive project called “Remix the World,” which incorporated original footage and sounds captured during travels to Kenya, South Africa, Bhutan, and Perth. He is particularly well-known for his visually-driven music videos on YouTube, with “Alice,” a track built from Disney’s *Alice in Wonderland*, exceeding 30 million views as of 2017. Another video, “Gardyn,” featuring his mother gardening, was showcased at the Guggenheim Museum in New York City in 2010. More recent video releases include “Trumpular,” based on quotes from Donald Trump in 2016, “Homarge” based on *The Simpsons* in 2019, “Strangerous” sampling *Stranger Things* in 2021, and “Cabin Fever” using sounds from *Muppet Treasure Island* also in 2021.

Beyond his individual projects, Pogo’s music has found a place as bumper music on the conservative talk show *Louder with Crowder*. His career has not been without its challenges; in 2011, he was detained in the United States for three weeks due to a lack of a valid work visa and was banned from re-entry until 2021. He also experienced a significant setback in 2020 when his YouTube channel was hacked and used for a cryptocurrency scam, though it was later restored by YouTube, retaining his subscriber base and view counts.

Pogo has faced considerable controversy due to content he posted online. In 2015, he released a video criticized for making misogynistic arguments, which he later defended as an attempt to impersonate the radical right.  Further controversy arose in 2016 when a livestream revealed statements expressing dislike for homosexuals and a seemingly supportive stance regarding violence against them, made in the context of the Orlando nightclub shooting. He subsequently attributed these views to Asperger syndrome and bipolar disorder, and again claimed he was attempting to portray extremist viewpoints, a claim met with skepticism by some sources. 

Throughout his career, Pogo has released a substantial discography, including eleven studio albums, starting with *Twilight Sessions* in 2006 and continuing through *Cosmoluxe* in 2022, along with numerous EPs.

title: Michael Folorunsho
text:
Michael Folorunsho, born on February 7, 1998, is an Italian professional footballer currently playing as a midfielder on loan to Cagliari from Napoli. He is also a member of the Italy national team. Folorunsho began his youth career with Lazio, progressing to play for their Under-19 team before turning professional. His initial professional experience came with Virtus Francavilla in Serie C, where he played for two seasons, accumulating 60 appearances. 

In July 2019, he was signed by Serie A club Napoli, though he was immediately loaned out for a two-year period to Bari, also in Serie C. Following this, Napoli continued to loan him to various Serie B clubs to gain experience. These loan spells included stints with Reggina in the 2020–21 season, then with both Pordenone and Reggina during the 2021–22 season, and a return to Bari for the 2022–23 season. 

Further loan moves followed in the 2023–24 season, first to Hellas Verona in August 2023, and then to Fiorentina in January 2025, with an option for a permanent transfer. Most recently, on July 24, 2025, he was loaned to Cagliari, again with an option to buy.

Folorunsho’s international career began with a call-up to the Italian senior squad in March 2024 by coach Luciano Spalletti. Although initially an unused substitute in friendly matches against Venezuela and Ecuador, he eventually earned his first cap for Italy on June 9 of the same year. This debut came in a friendly against Bosnia and Herzegovina, where he entered the game as a 76th-minute substitute for Davide Frattesi, with Italy winning 1–0. He was subsequently included in the Italian squad for the UEFA Euro 2024 tournament. 

Throughout his career, Folorunsho has been recognized for his performances, earning the Serie A Goal of the Month award for February 2024. He is of Nigerian descent. Statistics regarding his club and international appearances are available as of May 11, 2025, and June 15, 2024, respectively. Further information about his career can be found on Soccerway.

title: Fuerza Guerrera
text:
Fuerza Guerrera, born December 13, 1953, is a veteran Mexican *luchador* (professional wrestler) who debuted in 1977 and continues to wrestle today. He is known for wearing a mask throughout his career, a common practice in Mexican wrestling where a wrestler’s identity is often kept private. His real name is unknown, though it's established his paternal surname is González, the same as his son, Juventud Guerrera.

Guerrera began training in 1977 under Dick Angelo and several other trainers, initially wrestling as “Cachorro González” before adopting the name Fuerza Guerrera – meaning “Warrior Strength” – in 1979. He quickly established himself as a *rudo* (villain) character, a role that suited his personality and wrestling style. He found early success in Empresa Mexicana de Lucha Libre (EMLL, later CMLL), debuting on a major show in 1981 and winning the Mexican National Lightweight Championship in 1983. He later moved up in weight class, capturing the Mexican National Welterweight Championship in 1985 and eventually the NWA World Welterweight Championship in 1988, holding it for a significant period with numerous defenses.

Throughout the 1990s, Fuerza Guerrera became a central figure in the rivalry between CMLL and the newly formed Asistencia Asesoría y Administración (AAA). He followed Antonio Peña, the founder of AAA, when he left CMLL, bringing the intense feud with Octagón with him.  He became the first CMLL World Welterweight Champion in 1992 before moving to AAA. In AAA, he teamed with his son, Juventud Guerrera, achieving success including winning the Mexican National Tag Team Championship. He also held various titles in AAA and the World Wrestling Association (WWA), including WWA Tag Team and Trios Championships. 

A defining aspect of his career involved *Luchas de Apuesta* (bet matches), where wrestlers risk their masks. Fuerza Guerrera participated in several high-stakes matches, most notably a three-way round robin with Octagón and Huracán Ramírez in 1990, ultimately forcing Ramírez to unmask. He also famously avoided losing his own mask in a tag team match against El Hijo del Santo and Black Shadow Jr. 

In later years, Guerrera returned to CMLL briefly in 2001, winning the CMLL World Trios Championship. He eventually settled with the International Wrestling Revolution Group (IWRG) in 2007, where he continues to wrestle. He has held the IWRG Intercontinental Welterweight Championship multiple times.  He's also helped his son establish a new promotion, Gran Prix Championship Wrestling Super-X.  Despite a strained relationship with his son, and a one-time match against him in 2007, both have expressed a desire for a *Luchas de Apuesta* match before retirement. Fuerza Guerrera has also expanded his family's presence in wrestling, presenting his other children as professional wrestlers in 2018.

title: Mukesh (actor)
text:
Mukesh, born Mukesh Babu on March 5, 1957, is a prominent Indian actor, producer, television personality, and politician primarily known for his work in Malayalam cinema. Over a four-decade career, he has appeared in over 275 films, alongside occasional roles in Tamil productions. He comes from a family steeped in acting; his parents, O. Madhavan and Vijayakumari, were both actors, and his sister Sandhya Rajendran, along with her husband, are also performers.

Mukesh’s education includes a Bachelor of Science degree from Sree Narayana College, Kollam, and a law degree from The Kerala Law Academy Law College, Thiruvananthapuram. Before entering films, he was involved in stage dramas. He debuted on screen in 1982 with *Balloon*, quickly following with a leading role in *Ithu Njangalude Katha*, a remake of a Tamil film. He gained recognition through comedic roles in films directed by Priyadarshan during the mid-1980s, often in supporting capacities. *Mutharamkunnu P.O.* (1985) gained cult status over time, while *Boeing Boeing* (1985) marked his first major commercial success and his initial collaboration with Mohanlal, leading to numerous joint projects. He also worked alongside Mammootty in several popular films of the late 1980s, including *Snehamulla Simham* and *Oru CBI Diary Kurippu*, reprising his role in subsequent installments of the CBI series. *Ramji Rao Speaking* (1989) proved to be a breakthrough role, becoming a major box office hit and cementing his position in the industry.

The 1990s saw Mukesh taking on more leading roles. He starred in *In Harihar Nagar*, a defining film of Malayalam cinema's golden age of comedy, and formed a successful pairing with Jayaram in films like *Thoovalsparsham* and *Malayogom*. He also achieved solo success with films like *Gajakesariyogam* and *Champion Thomas*.  He was part of the hugely successful *Godfather* (1991) which ran for a record-breaking 417 days in theatres. He continued to deliver hits such as *Mannar Mathai Speaking* and *Kanakkinavu*, which won the Nargis Dutt Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration at the IFFI.

In more recent years, Mukesh ventured into film production, co-producing *Kadha Parayumbol* (2007) which won the Kerala State Film Award, and *Thattathin Marayathu* (2012), considered a key film in the Malayalam New Wave. He has also hosted television shows, including a Malayalam version of *Deal or No Deal* and the comedy talk show *Badai bungalow*. 

Beyond acting and production, Mukesh is actively involved in politics as a member of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI-M). He was first elected to the Kerala Legislative Assembly in 2016, representing the Kollam constituency, and was re-elected in 2021, though with a reduced margin. He unsuccessfully contested for a Lok Sabha seat in 2024. His public life has also faced controversy, including allegations of inappropriate phone calls and, more seriously, accusations of sexual harassment, leading to his arrest in September 2024. He authored two books, *Mukesh Kathakal* and *Mukesh Babu and Party in Dubai*. He served as chairman of the Kerala Sangeetha Nataka Academy.

title: Phife Dawg
text:
Malik Izaak Taylor, professionally known as Phife Dawg, was a Trinidadian-American rapper best known as a member of the influential hip-hop group A Tribe Called Quest. Born on November 20, 1970, in Queens, New York City, to Trinidadian immigrant parents, he tragically passed away on March 22, 2016, at the age of 45 due to complications from diabetes. He earned the nicknames “Five-Foot Assassin” and “Five-Footer” due to his height of 5 feet 3 inches. Phife grew up in the St. Albans neighborhood of Queens, and experienced the early loss of his twin brother, Mikal, shortly after birth. He first met Q-Tip at age two, and the pair began rapping together at age nine after being inspired by the Sugarhill Gang.

Phife Dawg formed A Tribe Called Quest in 1985 with Q-Tip and Ali Shaheed Muhammad, later adding Jarobi White. The group became associated with De La Soul and Jungle Brothers as part of the Native Tongues collective. They initially signed with Jive Records in 1990, releasing their debut album, *People's Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm*. Phife’s lyrical contributions grew significantly with the critically acclaimed *The Low End Theory* in 1991, where he addressed social and political issues. The group continued to release successful albums throughout the 1990s – *Midnight Marauders*, *Beats, Rhymes and Life*, and *The Love Movement* – before disbanding due to internal conflicts and issues with their record label. Their story was documented in the 2011 film *Beats, Rhymes & Life: The Travels of A Tribe Called Quest*.

Beyond his work with A Tribe Called Quest, Phife collaborated with artists like Fu-Schnickens, Diamond D, and Chi-Ali. He released his debut solo album, *Ventilation: Da LP*, in 2000 and was working on a second, *MUTTYmorPHosis*, at the time of his death. Singles from this posthumous album, “Sole Men” and “Nutshell,” were released shortly after his passing. Remarkably, A Tribe Called Quest reunited in 2015, deciding to record a final album, *We Got It from Here... Thank You 4 Your Service*, which was released in November 2016, just months after Phife’s death. His second solo album, *Forever*, was released on the sixth anniversary of his death, March 22, 2022.

Phife was married to Deisha Head-Taylor and had two children. He was a dedicated fan of the New York Knicks and even appeared as a playable character in the *NBA 2K7* and *NBA 2K9* video games. He was diagnosed with diabetes in 1990, a condition he openly discussed and used as inspiration for his music, even calling himself a "funky diabetic." He received a kidney transplant from his wife in 2008, but it was unsuccessful, requiring another transplant. 

Phife Dawg’s legacy is one of challenging conventions in hip-hop with his self-deprecating style. He influenced artists like Kanye West and Jill Scott. In 2016, a section of Linden Boulevard in Queens was renamed “Malik ‘Phife Dawg’ Taylor Way” in his honor, and in 2024, he was posthumously inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a member of A Tribe Called Quest.

title: Dominique Blake
text:
Dominique Blake, born February 15, 1987, in Bronx, New York, is a track and field athlete who competes for Jamaica. Her athletic career began in 2002 with indoor track, expanding to outdoor events in 2003. She attended Penn State University from 2004, earning a communications degree while competing for their track team. 

During her time with Penn State, Blake achieved notable results in the 4x400 meter relay at the NCAA Division I Indoor Track and Field Championships, placing 12th in 2006, 4th in 2007, and 5th in 2008. She also competed in the distance medley relay in 2007, finishing 13th, and participated in the individual 400 meters in 2008, but didn’t advance past the heats.

Blake faced early setbacks, including a disqualification at the 2006 USA Outdoor Track and Field Championships for testing positive for ephedrine, resulting in a nine-month ban. She competed at the 2008 United States Olympic Trials, finishing 23rd in the 400 meters. Representing Jamaica, she won a gold medal in the 4x400 meter relay at the 2010 Central American and Caribbean Games. At the 2010 Commonwealth Games, she finished 12th in the 4x400 meter relay and 18th in the individual 400 meters, reaching the semi-finals. She also competed at the 2012 IAAF World Indoor Championships without medaling.

A controversial moment occurred at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London. Although Blake was part of the Jamaican team that qualified, she did not actually run in the women’s 4x400 meter event. However, she was mistakenly awarded a bronze medal by the Jamaica Olympic Association, which she initially kept. Later, a more significant suspension came in 2013 after testing positive for methylhexanamine, initially resulting in a six-year ban. 

She appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and successfully had her ban reduced to four and a half years in 2014. Blake returned to competition in January 2017 and, in accordance with IAAF rules, eventually returned the Olympic bronze medal to the Jamaica Olympic Association that same year. In 2018, she competed at the IAAF World Indoor Championships, helping Jamaica qualify for the 4x400 meter final, though she wasn’t a runner in the final race where the team was later disqualified. She also participated in the 2018 National Relay Championships, finishing sixth in the 400 meters and not completing the 800 meters final, and she placed fourth in the 400 meters at the 2019 National Relay Championships.

title: Lina Marulanda
text:
Lina Marulanda, born Lina María Marulanda Cuartas on May 15, 1980, was a Colombian television personality and model who tragically died on April 22, 2010. She was originally from Medellín, Colombia, and began her career in modeling at the young age of twelve. Her early life involved balancing her education with the demands of a burgeoning modeling career, a situation she later expressed regret about in a 2004 interview. 

Marulanda initially attended Santa María del Rosario de Medellín High School, but transferred to Parra Paris High School after experiencing difficulties with the school's administration and nuns. Following her graduation from high school, she pursued higher education at Jorge Tadeo Lozano University in Bogotá, studying advertising. 

Her career in television began in 2002 when she started presenting for CM& News. She then became a prominent figure at Caracol News, working there for six years. During her time at Caracol News, she presented the 0700 edition and covered international news. She also co-hosted the entertainment segment of the evening news, first with actress Margarita Ortega and later with model Adriana Arboleda, starting in 2003. In December 2005, she took the lead role in presenting the entertainment portion of Caracol News at 12:30, alongside journalist Ivan Lalinde. 

Beyond news presentation, Marulanda expanded her television work to include hosting the reality show *Challenge 20-07* on Canal Caracol in early 2007. That same year, she returned to CM& News to provide special coverage of Colombiamoda 2007, and also reported on the event for W Radio.  She then joined the W Radio team for *La hora del Regreso* on July 24, 2007, replacing Marcela Sarmiento. 

In addition to her work in television, Marulanda was a successful spokesmodel for several major clothing brands and graced the pages of popular magazines such as *SoHo*, *Don Juan*, *Cromos*, and *G*.

Marulanda’s life was cut short when she died after falling from the balcony of her sixth-floor apartment. Authorities determined her death to be a suicide. At the time of her death, she was undergoing divorce proceedings from her second husband, Carlos Oñate, after a marriage of only three months. She was surrounded by family and a doctor when the incident occurred, with her parents, ex-husband, and a physician present.

title: Bif Naked
text:
Bif Naked, born Beth Nicole Torbert on June 15, 1971, is a Canadian singer who achieved significant success between 1996 and 2016, ranking among the top 150 best-selling Canadian artists. She gained prominence with the #1 Billboard Canada hit “Spaceman” and the MTV TRL-played video for “Moment of Weakness,” and her album *I Bificus* achieved platinum status internationally. 

Born in New Delhi, India, to teenage missionary parents, she was adopted and spent her childhood moving between locations including Lexington, Kentucky, and various towns in Manitoba, Canada, eventually settling in Winnipeg. She graduated from John Taylor Collegiate and studied theatre at the University of Winnipeg before embarking on a career as a stand-up comic. The name “Bif” originated as a mispronunciation of her given name, Beth.

Bif Naked began her musical journey singing with underground bands before independently releasing her first self-titled album in 1994, followed by *I Bificus* in 1998 and a subsequent Canadian tour. She released further albums, including *Purge* in 2001, a spoken word album *Okenspay Ordway: Things I Forgot To Tell Mommy*, *Superbeautifulmonster* in 2005, and *The Promise* in 2009, the latter recorded during her battle with breast cancer and dedicated to her fans. In 2012, she released *BIF NAKED FOREVER: Acoustic Hits and Other Delights* featuring acoustic versions of her songs and new material.  She has also been involved in the side project Jakkarta.

Throughout her career, Bif Naked has toured extensively across Europe, the United States, and Canada, sharing stages with numerous prominent artists including Snoop Dogg, Billy Idol, and Foo Fighters. Her music has been featured in television shows like *Buffy the Vampire Slayer* and *The West Wing* and films such as *American Psycho 2*. She contributed covers to soundtracks, including Twisted Sister’s “We’re Not Gonna Take It” for *Ready to Rumble* which was used as David Arquette’s entrance theme in WCW. 

Beyond her solo work, Bif has collaborated with other artists, appearing on albums by Strapping Young Lad, SNFU, and Dead Celebrity Status, and recording a duet with Will Blunderfield. She has also appeared in music videos for bands like Moist and Liveonrelease.  

Bif Naked’s interests extend to acting, with roles in films like *Archangel* and *Crossing*, television series including *Once a Thief*, *The L Word*, and *Buffy the Vampire Slayer*, and video games like *SSX*. She also hosted the CBC series *ZeD* and the reality show *Bif Naked Bride* documenting her marriage to Ian Walker. She is known for her extensive tattoos which include imagery from various religions and philosophies.

Bif identifies as polyamorous and pansexual and has been married and divorced three times. She was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2008, undergoing treatment and becoming an advocate for cancer awareness. She received an honorary doctorate from the University of the Fraser Valley in 2013.  Her memoir, *I Bificus*, was published in 2016. She continues to perform with her current band consisting of herself, Doug Fury, Chiko Misomali, and Peter Karroll.

title: Naz Mitrou-Long
text:
Nazareth Jersey Mitrou-Long, born in Mississauga, Ontario, Canada on August 3, 1993, is a professional basketball player currently with AEK Athens of the Greek Basketball League and Basketball Champions League. His father is of Trinidadian descent and his mother is a Greek Canadian, born in Sparta, Greece, and immigrated to Canada as a child. He has a large family, with three siblings and six half-siblings, including brother Elijah, who also played college basketball. Mitrou-Long began his basketball journey playing high school ball at Father Michael Goetz, followed by stints at Montrose Christian, Findlay Prep, and REDA Red before committing to Iowa State University in 2012.

At Iowa State, Mitrou-Long played college basketball for five seasons, experiencing setbacks due to hip injuries. As a freshman, he saw limited action, averaging 1.4 points. He developed into a key player in his sophomore year, becoming a reliable three-point shooter and averaging 7.1 points while shooting 40% from beyond the arc. His junior season saw increased responsibility, averaging 10.1 points and hitting a team-high 77 three-pointers, despite suffering labral tears in both hips that required surgery. He sat out his senior season to rehab, receiving a medical redshirt. Returning for a fifth year as a redshirt senior, he was named to the All-Big 12 Second Team after averaging 12.0 points and showcasing strong offensive performances, including a career-high 37 points in a game against Drake.

After going undrafted in the 2017 NBA draft, Mitrou-Long played in the NBA Summer League for the Sacramento Kings and signed a two-way contract with the Utah Jazz, splitting time between the Jazz and their G League affiliate, the Salt Lake City Stars. He briefly played 20 regular-season games for the Jazz and Indiana Pacers before continuing his career primarily in the G League with the Salt Lake City Stars and Fort Wayne Mad Ants.

Mitrou-Long’s professional career took him to Europe, with stints at Basket Brescia Leonessa in Italy’s Lega Basket Serie A, where he averaged 17.5 points, and Olimpia Milano, the Italian champions. He also played for Žalgiris Kaunas in Lithuania and Olympiacos Piraeus in Greece. He obtained Greek citizenship and a passport in December 2023, allowing him to play as a domestic player for Olympiacos. He has also represented the senior men’s Greek national team, making his debut in November 2024. Throughout his career, Mitrou-Long has been recognized for his three-point shooting ability and work ethic. He began displaying his full last name on his jersey in 2015 to honor his mother.

title: Julie Bishop
text:
Julie Bishop was born in Lobethal, South Australia in 1956, the third of four children. Her parents were both involved in local politics, and she grew up on an apple and cherry orchard. She was educated at Basket Range Primary School and St Peter's Collegiate Girls’ School, where she was head prefect, before studying law at the University of Adelaide, graduating in 1978. After a brief stint at an Adelaide law firm, she moved to Perth in 1983 after marrying property developer Neil Gillon, and became a partner at Robinson Cox, later Clayton Utz, eventually becoming managing partner of the Perth office. Prior to entering politics, she held positions with the Special Broadcasting Service and the senate of Murdoch University.

Bishop entered federal parliament in 1998, representing the Division of Curtin in Western Australia. In the Howard government, she held portfolios including Minister for Ageing, Education and Science, and Women. Following the Coalition’s loss in the 2007 election, she was elected as the first female Deputy Leader of the Liberal Party, a position she held for eleven years under three different leaders: Brendan Nelson, Malcolm Turnbull, and Tony Abbott. 

When the Coalition regained power in 2013, Bishop became Australia’s first female Minister for Foreign Affairs. During her tenure, she oversaw changes to the foreign aid program, including integrating AusAID into the Department of Foreign Affairs and implementing significant budget cuts. She also navigated complex international issues such as the military intervention against ISIL, the downing of Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, and the execution of Australian citizens in Indonesia. She also initiated the New Colombo Plan, providing funding for Australian students to study in the Indo-Pacific region.

In 2018, a leadership spill within the Liberal Party saw Scott Morrison elected as party leader and Prime Minister, defeating both Peter Dutton and Bishop. Bishop declined to remain as Foreign Minister and moved to the backbench, subsequently announcing her retirement from politics in February 2019, taking effect after the federal election was called. 

Since leaving parliament, Bishop has continued to serve in public life. In January 2020, she became the first female chancellor of the Australian National University. In April 2024, she was appointed as a United Nations special envoy for Myanmar. Before entering politics, Bishop was involved in a significant legal case defending CSR Limited against compensation claims from asbestos mining workers, an involvement that later drew scrutiny after she became a public figure, though she maintained she acted ethically and professionally. Her early political involvement included serving as a delegate to the 1998 constitutional convention, where she advocated for a minimalist approach to republicanism.

title: Haruto Takahashi
text:
Haruto Takahashi, born November 7, 1995, is a Japanese professional baseball pitcher currently playing for the Hanshin Tigers in Nippon Professional Baseball. His baseball journey began with softball, influenced by his older brother, before transitioning to little league with the Nishina Shonen Baseball Club in Shizuoka. He initially played both pitcher and right field at Tokoha University Tachibana Integrated High School, contributing to a national junior high softball championship. While he participated in the 2012 Summer Koshien as a reliever, his team lost in the first round, and he went undrafted after high school, leading him to enroll at Asia University in Tokyo. 

At Asia University, Takahashi became a regular starting pitcher, culminating in a Best 8 finish at the 2016 Japan National Collegiate Baseball Championship Tournament, with a record of 5 wins, 7 losses, and a 3.57 ERA across 31 appearances. He was drafted by the Hanshin Tigers in the 2nd round of the 2017 NPB draft, signing a 70 million yen contract with an annual salary of 12 million yen and receiving jersey number 29.

Takahashi made a strong debut in 2018, pitching seven shutout innings with only two hits allowed against the Carps, earning his first win – the first by a Hanshin rookie at Koshien Stadium in 60 years. However, a weak pitching arm limited his starts, and the season concluded with a 2–3 record and a 3.63 ERA, earning him a 1 million yen raise. The 2019 season involved time in the farm system to strengthen his arm. He ultimately achieved a 3–9 record with a 3.78 ERA, and contributed to the team’s progress in the Climax Series, resulting in a 9 million yen salary increase to 22 million yen.

In the shortened 2020 season, Takahashi excelled, particularly against the Giants, posting a 2.03 ERA against them. He recorded a career-high 14 strikeouts and completed his first game, finishing the season with a personal best 2.49 ERA in 12 starts and a 5-4 record. This performance, along with a strong home record at Koshien, led to a substantial 7 million yen raise, bringing his annual salary to 29 million yen. His success was partly attributed to a strong battery partnership with catcher Seishiro Sakamoto, who effectively called pitches to leverage Takahashi’s strengths.

Takahashi is a 5’11” left-handed pitcher who utilizes a three-quarters delivery. His primary pitch is a four-seam fastball, complemented by a cutter, two-seamer and occasional curveball and slider, reaching speeds up to 152 km/h (94 mph).

title: Fahadh Faasil
text:
Fahadh Faasil, born Abdul Hameed Mohammed Fahad Fazil on August 8, 1982, is a highly acclaimed and popular Indian actor and producer working primarily in Malayalam cinema. The son of filmmaker Fazil, he began his career in 2002 with his father’s film *Kaiyethum Doorath* under the name Shaanu, but the film was a commercial failure. Following this, he took a seven-year break, pursuing studies – including a Master’s in Philosophy from the University of Miami – before returning to acting in 2009 with a role in the anthology film *Kerala Cafe*.

His breakthrough came with the thrillers *Chaappa Kurishu* and *Akam* in 2011, earning him his first Kerala State Film Awards for Second Best Actor for both. He continued to gain recognition with a string of successful films in 2012 and 2013, including *22 Female Kottayam*, *Diamond Necklace*, *Annayum Rasoolum*, *Amen*, *North 24 Kaatham*, *Artist*, and *Oru Indian Pranayakadha*. *22 Female Kottayam* and *North 24 Kaatham* brought him Filmfare Awards for Best Actor, while *Artist* and *North 24 Kaatham* earned him Kerala State Film Awards for Best Actor. The film *Bangalore Days* in 2014 became one of the highest-grossing Malayalam films of all time.

Throughout his career, Fahadh has consistently received praise for his diverse portrayals. He continued to deliver acclaimed performances in films like *Maheshinte Prathikaaram* (2016), *Take Off* (2017), *Thondimuthalum Driksakshiyum* (2017) – for which he won a National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor and a Filmfare Award – *Njan Prakashan* (2018), *Varathan* (2018), and *Joji* (2021). He gained national recognition with roles in *Kumbalangi Nights* (2019), *Malik* (2021), *Vikram* (2022), and *Aavesham* (2024).

Beyond acting, Fahadh is a brand endorser and a philanthropist. He is married to actress Nazriya Nazim and co-owns the production company Fahadh Faasil and Friends with her. He is also a co-partner in the digital entertainment company Bhavana Studios, alongside Dileesh Pothan and Syam Pushkaran. His career has been marked by a willingness to experiment with roles and genres, establishing him as one of the leading and most respected actors in Malayalam cinema.

title: Quincy Jones
text:
Quincy Jones Jr., born in Chicago in 1933 and passing away in 2024, was a prolific American musician and producer with a career spanning seven decades. He achieved remarkable success in various facets of the music industry, earning 28 Grammy Awards, an Emmy, and a Tony Award, alongside nominations for numerous other prestigious accolades. Jones initially gained recognition in the 1950s as a jazz arranger and conductor, later transitioning to producing pop hits, notably for Lesley Gore, including the iconic “It’s My Party.” He also collaborated extensively with Frank Sinatra and Count Basie, contributing arrangements and conducting for their joint projects.

His work reached new heights with Michael Jackson, producing the groundbreaking albums *Off the Wall*, *Thriller*, and *Bad*, all of which achieved massive commercial success. Jones demonstrated his humanitarian side by producing and conducting the charity single "We Are the World" in 1985, raising funds for famine relief in Ethiopia. Beyond record production, Jones was a prolific composer for film, creating scores for films like *The Pawnbroker*, *In the Heat of the Night*, *The Wiz*, and *The Color Purple*, for which he later won a Tony Award for its revival in 2016, and an Emmy for work on the miniseries *Roots*.

Jones’s lineage is complex, revealing a mixed heritage. His paternal grandmother was an ex-slave, while his paternal grandfather was Welsh. Genealogical research uncovered French Huguenot ancestry linked to the family of Tennessee Williams, which Jones believed contributed to his musical talent. DNA testing revealed approximately 34% European ancestry alongside his predominantly African roots, including English, French, Italian, and Welsh heritage. Notably, he was a distant relative of George Washington. 

His early life was marked by a move to Washington state during the Great Migration and a childhood impacted by his mother’s mental health struggles. He developed his musical skills as a trumpeter and arranger in Seattle, inspired by musicians like Ray Charles and benefiting from the supportive environment of a smaller city. He pursued formal music education at Seattle University and later the Berklee College of Music in Boston.

Throughout his career, Jones demonstrated a keen business acumen, becoming the first African American vice-president at Mercury Records. He founded Qwest Productions and later Qwest Entertainment, expanding into film and television production. He consistently emphasized the importance of collaboration and humility, famously requesting artists to “check their ego at the door” during the recording of “We Are the World.” Jones received numerous honorary awards throughout his lifetime, including the Grammy Legend Award, the Kennedy Center Honors, and the National Medal of the Arts, culminating in an Academy Honorary Award in 2024. Time magazine recognized him as one of the most influential jazz musicians of the 20th century.

title: Diafra Sakho
text:
Diafra Sakho, born in Senegal in 1989, was a professional footballer who primarily played as a striker. He began his career in the French football system, starting with Génération Foot, a feeder club for FC Metz, before joining Metz directly in 2007. After initially playing for Metz’s reserve team where he scored 17 goals in 22 games, he earned a place in the first team in 2010, scoring his first goal against Nantes. A loan spell at Boulogne followed in 2012, but he returned to Metz and played a key role in their promotion back to Ligue 2, scoring 19 goals in 33 appearances. He then led Metz to the Ligue 2 title with another impressive goal-scoring season, netting 20 goals in 36 games, earning him the Ligue 2 Player of the Year award for the 2013–14 season.

In August 2014, Sakho moved to West Ham United in England, fulfilling a long-held dream. He quickly made an impact, scoring his first goal for the club against Sheffield United in the League Cup. He then became known for a remarkable run of scoring in his first six Premier League starts, matching a record previously held by Micky Quinn, and was awarded the Premier League Player of the Month for October 2014. However, his first season was disrupted by injury, sustained in a match against West Bromwich Albion, which also led to a dispute with the Senegal national team who wanted him to participate in the 2015 Africa Cup of Nations. FIFA ultimately fined West Ham for playing him in an FA Cup match during the tournament.

Sakho continued with West Ham for several more seasons, although injuries continued to hamper his progress. He scored in both the Europa League and Premier League in the 2015-16 season, and after a transfer request and a failed medical at West Bromwich Albion, he remained with the club. The 2016–17 season saw limited appearances due to injury, and in January 2018, he moved to French side Rennes. He then had a loan spell with Turkish club Bursaspor before joining Swiss side Neuchâtel Xamax in 2020, where he failed to score in eight appearances. He later signed for Nancy in 2022, eventually retiring from playing in July 2023.

Sakho also represented the Senegal national team, making his debut in 2014 and scoring his first international goal against Kosovo. He played a part in Senegal's qualification for the 2018 FIFA World Cup, their first appearance in the tournament since 2002. Throughout his career, he achieved honors including a Ligue 2 title with Metz and individual accolades such as the Ligue 2 Player of the Year award.
