He also had a period of legal trouble in 2015, being arrested on suspicion of assault, but was later cleared of any wrongdoing.

title: W. Clark Still
text:
William Clark Still, born in 1946, is a distinguished American organic chemist renowned for his work at Columbia University. His research has profoundly impacted areas like natural product synthesis, reaction development, conformational analysis, macrocyclic stereocontrol, and computational chemistry. He is perhaps best known for co-developing flash column chromatography, a widely used purification technique for organic compounds.

Still achieved a landmark in 1979 with the first total synthesis of periplanone B, a sex pheromone of the American cockroach. This synthesis not only confirmed the compound’s structure but also demonstrated a key anionic oxy-Cope rearrangement for forming the molecule’s 10-membered ring. He followed this in 1980 with the total synthesis of monensin, a complex ionophore, utilizing a diastereoselective aldol reaction to unite two advanced fragments. This reaction exemplified the Cram-Felkin-Anh model for predicting stereochemical outcomes.

Beyond total synthesis, Still significantly advanced chemical methodology. He developed the Wittig-Still rearrangement in 1978, improving the scope of the 2,3-Wittig rearrangement by using organotin compounds to generate alkoxy-substituted carbanions.  He also co-developed the Still-Gennari modification of the Horner-Wadsworth-Emmons reaction in 1983, which altered reaction conditions to favor the formation of Z-alkenes, a previously challenging outcome.

His development of flash column chromatography in 1978 revolutionized purification in organic chemistry labs. By applying pressure to speed solvent elution, it dramatically reduced purification times and improved separation quality, becoming a standard technique, particularly for small-scale work.  His publication on the method remains highly cited and frequently accessed. 

Recognizing the need for computational tools, Still pioneered the application of computational methods to organic chemistry. He created a Monte Carlo method for conformational analysis, searching for the lowest energy conformations of molecules. This led to the development of the MacroModel software program in 1986, designed to be accessible to both novice and experienced chemists. MacroModel incorporated a novel implicit solvation model, GB/SA, to simulate solvent effects, and was later acquired by Schrodinger, Inc.

title: Patrick Merrill
text:
Patrick Merrill, born February 22, 1979, is a Canadian who formerly played professional lacrosse and currently serves as the head coach and general manager of the San Diego Seals in the National Lacrosse League (NLL). His professional playing career encompassed stints in both the NLL and Major League Lacrosse (MLL).

Merrill began his NLL career after being selected in the first round of the 2002 draft by the Toronto Rock. He played four seasons with the Rock before becoming a focal point of the 2008 expansion draft, where he was chosen first overall by the Boston Blazers. However, the 2008 NLL season faced initial cancellation and then reinstatement, leading to complications for the newly formed Blazers and the Arizona Sting, both of whom ultimately opted out of participating in that season. Consequently, a dispersal draft was held, and Merrill was then selected second overall by the Titans. 

Throughout his career, Merrill played alongside his brother, Brodie Merrill, who currently plays for the same San Diego Seals team that Patrick now leads as coach and general manager. 

The article provides detailed key statistics breakdowns for his play in the NLL, MLL, and MSL, though specific numbers are not included. The NLL statistics tracked games played, goals, assists, points, loose balls, penalty minutes, points per game, loose balls per game, and penalty minutes per game. MLL statistics included games played, goals, two-point goals, assists, points, shots, ground balls, penalties, penalty minutes, faceoffs won, and faceoffs attempted.  The Major Series Lacrosse (MSL) statistics mirrored those of the NLL, tracking games played, goals, assists, points, loose balls, penalty minutes, points per game, loose balls per game, and penalty minutes per game. 

Beyond his playing career, the article notes Merrill’s current role in coaching, specifically mentioning his position with the San Diego Seals, but does not provide details on his coaching record or accomplishments. It also references coaching statistics for both the NLL and the Ontario Junior Lacrosse League (OJLL), though no data is provided.

title: Camille Paulus
text:
Camille Paulus, born on April 24, 1943, is a Belgian figure known for his dual career in law and liberal politics. He is a qualified lawyer, having earned a doctorate in law from the Vrije Universiteit Brussel, or VUB, in 1966. This academic background would later inform his professional life in multiple ways. 

Paulus transitioned from legal studies into a prominent position in local government, becoming the mayor of Aartselaar in 1989. He took over this role from Frans Van den Eynde, and served as mayor concurrently with other significant roles. Beyond his mayoral duties, Paulus also held a position as a Law Professor at the Vrije Universiteit Brussel, demonstrating a continued commitment to the academic sphere. 

His influence extended beyond Aartselaar and the university, as he also served as President of the Liberaal Vlaams Verbond, a liberal organization, for a substantial period spanning from 1982 to 1993. This leadership role within the liberal movement signifies his commitment to liberal political ideals and his capacity to guide a significant political organization.

In 1993, Paulus moved into provincial government, becoming the governor of the Belgian province of Antwerp. This was a considerable step up in responsibility and influence. He held this position for over fifteen years, serving until April 30, 2008. As governor, he was responsible for the administration and oversight of the entire province, a role demanding considerable administrative and political skill. 

Throughout his career, Paulus balanced roles in academia, local politics, and regional administration, showcasing a versatile and sustained engagement with Belgian public life. Information regarding his career is documented in the “Geschiedenis van de provincie Antwerpen. Een politieke biografie,” published in 2005, and within the Liberal Archive dedicated to him.

title: Salt Bae
text:
Nusret Gökçe, globally known as Salt Bae, was born in 1983 in a village in eastern Turkey to a Kurdish family. His father worked as a mineworker, and financial hardship forced Nusret to leave school at the age of eleven or twelve to begin an apprenticeship as a butcher in Istanbul. Driven to improve his culinary skills, he spent several years between 2007 and 2010 travelling and working in restaurants in Argentina and the United States, often without pay, to gain experience. He opened his first restaurant in Istanbul in 2010, followed by a Dubai location in 2014, laying the foundation for what would become the Nusr-Et chain. The name, meaning “my meat” in Turkish, reflects his focus.

Gökçe rose to international fame in January 2017 through viral videos showcasing his distinctive meat preparation and seasoning technique. His dramatic sprinkling of salt, dropping it from his fingertips down his forearm and onto the meat, earned him the nickname “Salt Bae” and generated millions of views online. This exposure led to patronage from numerous celebrities and political figures.  Nusr-Et now boasts locations in Turkey, Greece, the United States, the United Kingdom, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Saudi Arabia.

Despite his fame, early critical reviews of his New York City steakhouse in 2018 were largely negative, with some describing the food as overpriced, over-salted, tough, and lacking flavor. However, the theatrical aspect of his tableside service, personally performed by Gökçe, was often praised as a unique dining experience. His Manhattan burger bar ultimately closed in 2023.

Gökçe’s career hasn’t been without controversy. He faced criticism for a 2016 photo mimicking Fidel Castro, and for serving Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro amidst widespread food shortages in Venezuela, prompting protests.  He also settled a lawsuit with former employees in New York who accused him of unfairly retaining a portion of their tips, paying them $230,000.  Further issues included a fire at his Istanbul restaurant caused by a show, and temporary closures of his Boston restaurant for violating COVID-19 safety regulations.  A large bill at his UK restaurant also drew media attention.  Most recently, he was investigated by FIFA for disruptive behavior following the 2022 FIFA World Cup final, where he gained unauthorized access to the field and interacted with players and the trophy. Financial reports from his London restaurant show fluctuating revenues and profits, alongside accusations of tip theft and discrimination against former staff. 

Beyond his restaurants, Gökçe has engaged in philanthropic endeavors, funding the construction of a school, library, guest house, mosque, English education center, and computer laboratory in his hometown of Erzurum.

title: Charley Boorman
text:
Charley Boorman, born in 1966, is a British television presenter, travel writer, and actor with a lifelong passion for motorbikes. He is perhaps best known for his four long-distance motorcycle journeys undertaken with his friend Ewan McGregor, documented in the popular series *Long Way Round* (2004), *Long Way Down* (2007), *Long Way Up* (2020) and the upcoming *Long Way Home* (2025). 

Boorman’s early life was split between Wimbledon, London and County Wicklow, Ireland. He comes from a film industry background; his mother is costume designer Christel Kruse and his father is film director Sir John Boorman. Actor Lee Marvin served as his godfather. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in his father’s films, including *Deliverance* in 1972 and *Excalibur* in 1981, alongside his sister Katrine Boorman. He continued acting into adulthood, with roles in *The Emerald Forest* (1985), *Hope and Glory* (1987), *The Serpent's Kiss* (1997) and *The Bunker* (2001).

Beyond acting, Boorman developed a successful presenting career. Following *Long Way Round*, he participated in the 2006 Dakar Rally, an experience documented in *Race to Dakar*, though he was forced to retire due to injury. He followed this with *Long Way Down*, travelling from Scotland to South Africa. Subsequent travel series included *By Any Means* (2008), travelling from Ireland to Sydney using local transport, and *Right to the Edge* (2009), from Sydney to Tokyo. He also presented *Charley Boorman's Extreme Frontiers* for Channel 5 in 2011, and further series in South Africa and the US. More recently, he began presenting *Motorbike TV* for Motorsport.TV in 2022.

Boorman is also involved in charitable work, having supported UNICEF since 2004 and serving as president of Dyslexia Action from 2009 – he himself is dyslexic and actively raises awareness of the condition. He has also visited troops in Afghanistan and presented Gold Duke of Edinburgh’s Awards. 

In 2016, Boorman suffered serious leg injuries in a motorbike accident in Portugal, requiring surgery and a period of wheelchair use. He continues to ride, although he now walks with a limp. He has written several books detailing his adventures, including *Long Way Round*, *Race to Dakar*, *Long Way Down*, *Extreme Frontiers* and his autobiography *Long Way Back* (2017).

title: Radja Nainggolan
text:
Radja Nainggolan, born in Antwerp, Belgium in 1988, is a professional footballer currently playing for Lokeren-Temse. Throughout his extensive career, he has primarily played as a central midfielder, notably spending a significant portion of his time in Italy with clubs like Piacenza, Cagliari, Roma, and Inter Milan, accumulating 367 Serie A appearances and 48 goals. He was recognized for his consistent performance with four consecutive selections to the Serie A Team of the Year. He also represented Belgium internationally 30 times, scoring six goals, and participated in Euro 2016.

Nainggolan’s upbringing was marked by his mother raising him and his siblings after his Indonesian father left the family. The loss of his mother in 2010 deeply affected him, prompting a commemorative tattoo. He is fluent in Dutch, English, French, and Italian, and was raised Catholic.

His professional journey began with Tubantia Borgerhout before moving to Germinal Beerschot’s youth system. He debuted with Piacenza in 2006, becoming a regular starter by the 2008-09 season, helping the team avoid relegation. A loan move to Cagliari in 2010 proved pivotal, eventually leading to a permanent transfer where he became a fan favorite, even being included in a list of the club’s all-time best players.

In 2014, Nainggolan joined Roma on loan, then permanently in 2015. He played a key role in securing Champions League qualification for the club and was a consistent performer, renewing his contract multiple times.  A significant transfer to Inter Milan followed in 2018 for a reported €38 million, where he became the first Belgian to score for the club in the Champions League. Loan spells back at Cagliari followed, where he was even named Serie A’s MVP for November 2019.

Further moves saw him join Royal Antwerp in 2021, where a suspension due to off-field incidents led to a mutual termination of his contract. He then had a brief stint with SPAL in Italy, coached by former teammate Daniele De Rossi, before moving to Indonesia to play for Bhayangkara, motivated by a substantial contract.  He scored one goal during his time there. He returned to Belgium with Lokeren-Temse in early 2025, scoring on his debut.

Internationally, Nainggolan represented Belgium at the U23 level and earned his first senior cap in 2009. He was part of the Euro 2016 squad, scoring a crucial goal against Sweden. He initially retired from international football in 2017, later reversing his decision, only to retire again in 2018.

Known as “Il Ninja,” Nainggolan is a versatile and dynamic midfielder, praised for his physicality, technique, and ability to contribute both defensively and offensively. He has been deployed in various midfield roles, including as a playmaker, box-to-box midfielder, and even as a winger.  He has faced controversy throughout his career, including incidents involving smoking and alcohol, and a recent arrest related to a cocaine-smuggling investigation. He has also served as an ambassador for the FIFA U-17 World Cup and has a wife and two daughters.

title: Dr. Dre
text:
Andre Young, known professionally as Dr. Dre, was born in Compton, California, in 1965. His early life was marked by his parents’ separation and frequent moves throughout the Los Angeles area. He was largely raised by his grandmother and later developed a strong family connection through his stepfather’s children, including future rapper Warren G. He initially pursued an apprenticeship but turned towards music, influenced by artists like Grandmaster Flash, and began DJing under the name “Dr. J” before adopting “Dr. Dre.”

Dre’s musical career began in 1984 with the group World Class Wreckin’ Cru, finding initial success in the electro-hop scene. In 1987, he co-founded the groundbreaking group N.W.A alongside Eazy-E, Ice Cube, and Arabian Prince. N.W.A revolutionized hip-hop with their explicit lyrics detailing the realities of street life, and their 1989 debut album, *Straight Outta Compton*, became a cornerstone of West Coast hip-hop and popularized gangsta rap. Following Ice Cube’s departure, Dre pioneered the subgenre of G-funk, characterized by its synthesizer-heavy production and slower tempos.

After N.W.A disbanded in 1991, Dre launched a successful solo career with his debut album, *The Chronic* (1992), released on Death Row Records. The album, featuring the hit single “Nuthin’ but a ‘G’ Thang” with Snoop Dogg, catapulted him to mainstream success and earned him a Grammy Award. He also mentored and produced for other artists on Death Row, including Snoop Dogg, Warren G, and Daz Dillinger, helping launch their careers. However, disputes led Dre to leave Death Row in 1996 and establish Aftermath Entertainment. 

Aftermath released several projects, including a compilation album and Dre’s second studio album, *2001* (1999), which reaffirmed his influence. In the 2000s, Dre increasingly focused on producing for other artists, most notably signing and launching the careers of Eminem and 50 Cent. Aftermath later signed artists like Kendrick Lamar, Anderson .Paak, and Busta Rhymes, continuing Dre’s influence in the music industry. He has garnered seven Grammy Awards, including Producer of the Year, and was ranked by *Rolling Stone* as one of the greatest artists of all time. 

Outside of music, Dre has appeared in several films, including *Set It Off* and *Training Day*. However, his career has also been shadowed by accusations of violence against women, including a no-contest plea in an assault case in 1991 and more recent allegations from former partners. Following the release of his 2015 album, *Compton*, he issued a public apology related to these accusations. Despite the controversy, Dr. Dre remains a pivotal figure in hip-hop history, known for his innovative production, artist development, and lasting impact on the genre.

title: Michael Douglas
text:
Michael Douglas is a highly acclaimed American actor and film producer with a career spanning several decades. Born in 1944 to actors Kirk and Diana Douglas, he received a Bachelor of Arts degree in drama from the University of California, Santa Barbara. He began his career in the late 1960s with smaller film roles and gained early television exposure in *The Streets of San Francisco* (1972-1976), earning three Emmy nominations and eventually winning one in 2013 for his portrayal of Liberace in *Behind the Candelabra*.

A pivotal moment in his career came with producing *One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest* (1975), a film he acquired the rights to from his father, ultimately winning an Academy Award for Best Picture. He continued to produce films while also building his acting profile, appearing in movies like *The China Syndrome* (1979), *Romancing the Stone* (1984) and its sequel, *The Jewel of the Nile* (1985). Douglas achieved significant success in the 1980s with roles in *Fatal Attraction* (1987) and, most notably, as Gordon Gekko in *Wall Street* (1987), for which he won the Academy Award for Best Actor and later reprised in *Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps* (2010). 

Throughout the 1990s and 2000s, Douglas remained a prominent figure in Hollywood, starring in films such as *The War of the Roses* (1989), *Basic Instinct* (1992), *The American President* (1995), *Traffic* (2000), and *The Game* (1997). He also ventured into television again, winning a Golden Globe for his performance in *The Kominsky Method* (2018-2021). More recently, he played Hank Pym in several Marvel Cinematic Universe films from 2015 to 2023 and portrayed Benjamin Franklin in the 2024 miniseries *Franklin*.

Beyond his work in entertainment, Douglas has been involved in humanitarian and political activism, serving on the board of the Nuclear Threat Initiative and as a United Nations Messenger of Peace. He has received numerous honors throughout his career, including two Academy Awards, five Golden Globes, a Primetime Emmy, the Cecil B. DeMille Award, and the AFI Life Achievement Award. He has been married to Catherine Zeta-Jones since 2000. Douglas announced in 2025 his plans for semi-retirement, citing his age and a desire to spend more time with his family.

title: Caitlin Lowe
text:
Caitlin Faith Lowe-Nagy, born February 6, 1985, is currently the head coach of the Arizona Wildcats softball team. Her career began with significant success at Foothill High School in California, where she was a four-time All-American and led her team to multiple championships between 2000 and 2003, earning Orange County “Player of the Year” in 2003. She continued her athletic accomplishments at the University of Arizona, playing softball and achieving First Team All-American status in each of her four years – a feat only shared by one other Wildcat player. 

During her time at Arizona, Lowe led the team to back-to-back Women’s College World Series championships in 2006 and 2007. She consistently ranked among the program’s leaders in stolen bases, runs, and batting average, and her career included impressive single-game performances, such as a four-hit game against Louisiana Tech and driving in four RBIs against Louisiana-Lafayette. She accumulated over 300 hits, 200 runs, and 100 stolen bases while maintaining a .400 batting average, and was named to the Greatest College Softball Team All-Time in the outfield.  She also earned the inaugural Lowe's Senior CLASS Softball Award, recognizing her excellence both on and off the field.

Following her collegiate career, Lowe competed internationally, winning a silver medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics. She was a member of the U.S. Women’s National Softball Team from 2005, contributing to World Cup wins in 2006 and 2007, and a gold medal at the 2007 Pan American Games. She was known for her exceptional speed and base running, even hitting the first-ever inside-the-park home run in Olympic Games history. 

Lowe then spent six seasons playing professionally with the USSSA Pride in National Pro Fastpitch, winning three titles and being named Player of the Year in 2012. She retired from professional play in 2015, after which the Pride inducted her into their Hall of Fame and retired her jersey number 26.

After her playing career, Lowe transitioned into coaching. She began as a volunteer assistant coach at Arizona in 2013, becoming the associate head coach by 2018. In June 2021, she was named the head coach of the Wildcats, following the retirement of long-time coach Mike Candrea. 

Lowe graduated from Arizona with a degree in psychology and a minor in communications. She comes from an athletic family, with her sister and another sister also playing softball at Oregon State University. She is married to Paul Nagy, an assistant soccer coach at the University of Arizona, and they have two children, Harper and Beckham.

title: Douglas Wood (engineer)
text:
Douglas Wood was an Australian construction engineer born in Whyalla, South Australia, in 1941. He received his education at Geelong College and the Gordon Institute of TAFE, where he qualified as a mechanical engineer. In 1973, Wood relocated to the United States, settling in Alamo, California with his wife and daughter. For 25 years, he worked for the Bechtel Corporation, contributing to large-scale projects like the Palo Verde Nuclear Generating Station in Arizona, before establishing his own company and moving to Iraq for work related to project management and nuclear plant construction.

In May 2005, while in Baghdad attempting to finalize a business deal, Wood was kidnapped alongside two Iraqi colleagues. The Shura Council of the Mujahideen of Iraq claimed responsibility, and footage of Wood pleading for his life was broadcast by Al-Jazeera, with demands for the withdrawal of Australian and US troops from Iraq. The Australian government, led by Prime Minister John Howard and Foreign Minister Alexander Downer, firmly refused to negotiate with the captors, rejecting both troop withdrawal and ransom payments. Wood’s family launched a public relations campaign appealing to his captors, emphasizing his personal values and potential sympathy with their cause. 

After a six-week ordeal, Wood was rescued by Iraqi army troops, aided by U.S. forces, during a raid on a house in Ghazaliya. The rescue occurred during a routine search for weapons, and a brief firefight ensued, though no one was injured. Tragically, it was later revealed that Wood’s two Iraqi business associates had been killed approximately a month prior to his rescue.

Following his liberation, Wood disputed claims made by Sheikh Taj al-Din Alhilali, who asserted he had played a role in securing Wood’s release and that Wood had spoken with him during his captivity. Wood denied ever having any contact with Alhilali. In 2009, Wood expressed concerns to Prime Minister Kevin Rudd about the safety of the Iraqi soldiers involved in his rescue, claiming seven had been targeted and murdered for providing evidence against his kidnappers. Consequently, two Iraqi service personnel were granted humanitarian visas to relocate to Australia. 

Prior to the kidnapping, Wood had been involved with a feasibility study for the Jervis Bay Nuclear Power Plant. He later publicly supported the development of a nuclear energy industry in Australia, stating he would be comfortable living near a nuclear plant, but voiced reservations about the qualifications of Australian engineers and suppliers to undertake such a project. Wood passed away on December 31, 2019.

title: Zubaira Tukhugov
text:
Zubaira Tukhugov, born January 15, 1991, is a Russian mixed martial artist who competed in the Lightweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). He began his professional MMA career in 2010, initially gaining experience by winning a Pankration Atrium Cup eight-man tournament. Before joining the UFC in 2014, Tukhugov built a record of 10-3, fighting for promotions including Cage Warriors, ProFC, and Fight Nights, where he won three consecutive bouts against Romano De Los Reyes, Harun Kina, and Vaso Bakocevic. He also secured a victory over Denys Pidnebesnyi while competing in Cage Warriors.

Tukhugov debuted in the UFC in February 2014 with a unanimous decision win over Douglas Silva de Andrade, after his original opponent, Thiago Tavares, withdrew due to injury. He followed this with a first-round technical knockout victory over Ernest Chavez in October of the same year. A scheduled rematch with Tavares in 2015 was cancelled due to a rib injury sustained by Tukhugov. He later won a split decision against Phillipe Nover in December 2015.

His UFC career has been marked by both successes and setbacks. A controversial split decision loss to Renato Moicano in May 2016 followed two disputed decisions regarding strikes to the groin. In 2016, he was pulled from a fight after a potential anti-doping violation, eventually resulting in a two-year USADA suspension and a $10,000 fine for testing positive for ostarine. He was also removed from a scheduled fight in 2018 due to his involvement in the post-fight melee at UFC 229 following the Khabib Nurmagomedov vs. Conor McGregor event, receiving a one-year suspension and a $25,000 fine, later reduced by 35 days.  

Following his suspension, Tukhugov returned in 2019, fighting to a split draw against Lerone Murphy. He secured another first-round TKO victory over Kevin Aguilar in 2020, but lost a split decision to Hakeem Dawodu at UFC 253, having missed the featherweight limit. Further fights saw a unanimous decision win over Ricardo Ramos in 2021, and scheduled bouts against Nate Landwehr and Lucas Almeida both fall through due to visa issues and weight management problems, respectively. His final UFC fight in February 2023, against Elves Brenner, ended in a split decision loss after he again missed weight. Subsequently, on February 28, 2023, he was released from the UFC roster.

title: Riccardo Tisci
text:
Riccardo Tisci, born in Taranto, Italy in 1974 and raised in Como, is an Italian fashion designer who rose to prominence through his innovative and often gothic-infused designs. He initially studied at the Design Istituto d’Arte Applicata in Cantù until age 17 before completing his education at London’s Central Saint Martins College of Art and Design, graduating in 1999. Following graduation, he gained experience working with companies like Puma, Antonio Berardi, and Coccapani, and spent three years with Ruffo Research, a company known for launching designer careers.

A turning point came in 2005 when Tisci was appointed creative director of Givenchy’s haute couture, ready-to-wear, and accessories lines. He was brought in by LVMH and Givenchy leadership who recognized his unique blend of elegance, modernity and romanticism. During his twelve-year tenure at Givenchy, he significantly increased the brand’s haute couture client base from five to twenty-nine customers. He also designed costumes for Madonna’s Sticky & Sweet Tour in 2008, further establishing his profile. Tisci stepped down from Givenchy in 2017, citing a desire to focus on personal interests.

In 2018, Tisci moved to Burberry as chief creative officer, succeeding Christopher Bailey. His vision for Burberry centered on blending tradition with a darkly gothic aesthetic. He initiated a collaboration with Vivienne Westwood for the Winter 2018 collection and continued to collaborate extensively throughout his career. However, his time at Burberry ended in September 2022 with the appointment of Daniel Lee as his replacement.

Tisci is known for his highly stylized runway presentations and a melancholic, romantic approach to design. He championed inclusivity, notably featuring Lea T, a transgender model from Brazil, in his Givenchy Fall–Winter 2010 collection. Throughout his career, Tisci’s strong network fostered numerous collaborations with artists, musicians, and other creatives. These included projects with Marina Abramović, Jay-Z and Kanye West (designing album artwork and tour costumes), Beyoncé, Nike (producing multiple sportswear collections including one intended for the 2016 Olympics), and even virtual pop idol Hatsune Miku. He also contributed costume design to ballet, specifically Maurice Ravel’s *Boléro*.  Italian model Mariacarla Boscono has been a frequent collaborator and friend. 

Tisci is openly gay and, in 2025, was involved in a lawsuit alleging sexual assault in New York.

title: Billy Snedden
text:
Billy Snedden was born in Perth, Western Australia, in 1926, the youngest of six children to Scottish immigrant parents. His father worked as a stonemason and had a somewhat troubled past, and the family moved to Perth after a fire destroyed their home in a mining town. Snedden’s early life was marked by his father’s absence and the need for family members to contribute to the household income. He attended local schools and began working part-time from a young age, displaying an aptitude for sport as well. He briefly attended university before enlisting in the Royal Australian Air Force in 1945, though his service coincided with the end of World War II and involved mainly non-combat duties.

Following the war, Snedden completed his law degree at the University of Western Australia and began practicing law. He became involved in the Young Liberals, eventually becoming its federal chairman. He then worked for the Department of Immigration, serving in Italy and England, gaining fluency in Italian during his time abroad. Returning to Australia in 1955, he moved to Melbourne and successfully entered Federal Parliament as the member for Bruce.

Snedden steadily rose through the ranks of the Liberal Party, holding various ministerial portfolios under multiple Prime Ministers from 1964 to 1972, including Attorney-General, Minister for Immigration, Minister for Labour and National Service, and finally Treasurer. He became Deputy Leader in 1971. Following the Liberal Party’s defeat in the 1972 election, he assumed the leadership, promising a more liberal approach. However, his leadership was fraught with challenges, notably his controversial decision to block the Labor government’s budget in 1974, leading to a double dissolution election. 

Despite campaigning on the slogan "Oh no, not Snedden!", Whitlam was re-elected. Snedden faced internal challenges from Malcolm Fraser, eventually losing the leadership in 1975. He then surprised many by accepting the position of Speaker of the House of Representatives in 1976, a role he held until his retirement from Parliament in 1983. As Speaker, he championed parliamentary independence and sought to restore dignity to the office, even reinstating the traditional wig and gown. 

After leaving Parliament, Snedden remained active in public life, serving as chairman of the Melbourne Football Club and on the board of the Victorian Football League. His death in 1987 was notable due to the unusual circumstances surrounding it, involving the ex-girlfriend of his son. Throughout his career, Snedden was known for his pragmatism and commitment to parliamentary procedure, leaving a significant mark on Australian political life.

title: Esteban Espíndola
text:
Esteban Ezequiel Espíndola López, born on March 22, 1992, is an Argentine professional footballer who plays as a centre-back. He began his professional career with River Plate, though his opportunities were limited initially, appearing only on the bench twice in the Argentine Primera División. He did make his debut for the club in the 2012–13 Copa Argentina against Estudiantes.

In July 2013, Espíndola was loaned to Atlético de Rafaela, also a Primera División team, but only featured in three league matches during the 2013–14 season. He then moved to Nueva Chicago in Primera B Nacional in 2014, but his time there was brief, as he departed without making a single appearance. A move to Belgrano, another Primera División side, followed in February 2015. He spent three seasons with Belgrano, accumulating twenty appearances across all competitions. 

In August 2017, Espíndola was loaned to San Martín, a Primera B Nacional team. This proved a successful move, as he helped the club achieve promotion to the top division.  He then ventured abroad, joining Olimpia in the Liga Nacional of Honduras in August 2018. He played in fourteen games for Olimpia before leaving in December of the same year by mutually terminating his contract. He returned to Argentina in January 2019, signing with Racing de Córdoba in the Torneo Federal A, but experienced relegation with the team. 

Espíndola subsequently returned to Honduras, joining Marathón, where he found goal-scoring form. He scored his first senior career goal on August 11, 2019, in a 1–1 draw against his former club, Olimpia, and went on to score against Honduras Progreso and Real Sociedad.  In July 2020, he moved again, this time to Costa Rica, signing a one-year contract with Saprissa and being assigned the number five shirt.

Before turning professional, Espíndola represented Argentina at the youth level, playing for both the U15 and U17 teams. He participated in the 2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup in Nigeria, making three appearances for the U17 squad and even scoring a goal – a penalty kick – during a group stage match against Germany. 

Throughout his career, Espíndola has achieved some team honours. He was part of the River Plate squad that won the U-20 Copa Libertadores in 2012 and later celebrated a Liga FPD Clausura title with Saprissa in 2021.

title: Franck Ribéry
text:
Franck Ribéry, born in Boulogne-sur-Mer, France in 1983, was a professional footballer renowned for his speed, skill, and precise passing, widely considered one of the best players of his generation. His football journey began at age six with FC Conti Boulogne, followed by a spell at Lille where difficulties adjusting led to his departure. He then returned to US Boulogne, spending two years there before moving through the amateur divisions with Alès and Brest. 

Ribéry’s breakthrough came in 2004 with Metz, where his impressive performances earned him a transfer to Galatasaray in Turkey in January 2005. He won the Turkish Cup with Galatasaray, but his time there was cut short due to disputes over wages and controversial circumstances surrounding his move to Marseille later that year. At Marseille, he flourished, helping the team reach consecutive Coupe de France finals, though they ultimately lost both.

In 2007, Ribéry joined Bayern Munich for a then club-record fee of €25 million. This marked the most successful period of his career, where he won nine Bundesliga titles, six DFB-Pokal trophies, a Champions League title, and a FIFA Club World Cup, accumulating a total of 24 titles over twelve seasons. His exceptional form during the 2012–13 season earned him a nomination for the FIFA Ballon d’Or, alongside Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo. During his time at Bayern, he formed a celebrated attacking partnership with Arjen Robben, affectionately known as “Robbery.” 

After leaving Bayern in 2019, Ribéry continued his career with Fiorentina in Italy for two years, before finishing his playing days with Salernitana in 2022. He also served as a technical collaborator for Salernitana following his retirement. 

Ribéry represented the France national team 81 times, participating in the 2006 and 2010 FIFA World Cups, and the 2008 and 2012 UEFA European Championships. He received numerous individual accolades, including three French Player of the Year awards and the German Footballer of the Year award, becoming the first player to win both. He was also named to the UEFA Team of the Year, awarded the Young Player of the Year in France, and won the UEFA Best Player in Europe Award in 2013.

Beyond his on-field achievements, Ribéry’s early life was marked by a serious car accident at age two, leaving him with prominent facial scars. Before becoming a professional footballer, he worked as a construction worker with his father, an experience he described as valuable. His path to success was not without challenges, facing setbacks and trials throughout his early career before ultimately establishing himself as a world-class player.

title: Gretl Braun
text:
Margarete Berta “Gretl” Braun was the younger sister of Eva Braun, and through her sister’s marriage, became sister-in-law to Adolf Hitler. Born in 1915, she spent much of her life within Hitler’s inner circle, particularly at his retreat, the Berghof, in the Bavarian Alps. She worked as a clerk for the photographer Heinrich Hoffmann, who was the official photographer for the Nazi Party, following in the footsteps of her sister Eva. Hitler provided the Braun sisters with comfortable housing, initially an apartment and later a villa.

Gretl’s personality was described as lively and somewhat rebellious, contrasting with the formality of the Berghof. She enjoyed smoking despite Hitler’s disapproval and even attracted the attention of Hitler’s SS adjutant, Fritz Darges, though their potential relationship was abruptly ended when he was transferred. In 1944, Gretl married SS-Gruppenführer Hermann Fegelein, a liaison officer for Heinrich Himmler who worked on Hitler’s staff. The wedding, a lavish three-day event, was attended by Hitler, Himmler, and Martin Bormann, and served to solidify a formal connection between Hitler and Eva. 

The closing days of the war brought tragedy for Gretl. Shortly after her wedding, the Normandy Landings occurred, signaling a turning point. Her husband, Fegelein, was arrested for desertion and executed by Hitler just days before Hitler and Eva Braun committed suicide in the Führerbunker, a decision influenced by Hitler’s anger at Himmler’s attempts to negotiate a surrender. While heavily connected to the Nazi regime, Gretl survived the war. She was pregnant at the time of Fegelein's death and gave birth to a daughter, Eva Barbara, in May 1945, naming her in memory of her sister.

After the war, Gretl changed her name and remarried in 1954 to Kurt Berlinghoff.  She lived a quiet life until her death in 1987 in Bavaria, identified on her tombstone as Gretl Berlinghoff. Tragically, her daughter, Eva Barbara, also died young, by suicide in 1971 following the death of her boyfriend. Gretl, her daughter, her second husband, and another sister, Ilse Braun, are all buried together. Despite the extensive documentation surrounding Hitler and his inner circle, Eva Braun’s business papers, requested to be destroyed by her in a final letter to Gretl, were never found, nor was any of her personal correspondence.

title: Jamie Dornan
text:
Jamie Dornan is a Northern Irish actor, model, and musician who has garnered recognition with two Irish Film and Television Awards and nominations for a BAFTA Television Award and a Golden Globe Award. Born in 1982, he began his career as a model in 2001, quickly gaining attention and being dubbed “the Golden Torso” by *The New York Times*, and later being named one of the “25 Biggest Male Models of All Time” by *Vogue*. Prior to acting, he was also a member of the folk band Sons of Jim, releasing music until 2008.

Dornan’s acting debut came in 2006 with a role in Sofia Coppola’s *Marie Antoinette*. He followed this with smaller parts in independent films and television, including a recurring role in *Once Upon a Time* from 2011 to 2013. A breakthrough came with his portrayal of serial killer Paul Spector in the crime drama *The Fall* (2013-2016), earning him critical acclaim and a BAFTA nomination. This role significantly broadened his professional opportunities.

He gained international prominence playing Christian Grey in the *Fifty Shades* film trilogy (2015-2018), which, despite critical panning, proved a commercial success, grossing $1.32 billion. Dornan has stated the franchise opened doors for other roles he desired. Subsequent film work includes appearances in *Anthropoid* (2016), *Barb and Star Go to Vista Del Mar* (2021), and *Belfast* (2021), for which he received a Golden Globe nomination. He also starred as the lead in the thriller drama *The Tourist* (2022-2024).

Dornan’s personal life has been marked by loss, with his mother passing away when he was 16 and his father succumbing to COVID-19 complications in 2021. He credits his father with consistent support throughout his career. He has two older sisters, one working at Disney in London and the other a fashion designer. He attended Methodist College Belfast, where he participated in rugby and the drama department, laying the groundwork for his later career. He briefly attended Teesside University before moving to London to pursue acting training, although he never formally enrolled in drama school. 

Throughout his modelling career, he worked with prominent fashion houses like Dior Homme, Hugo Boss, and Calvin Klein, appearing in numerous advertising campaigns and collaborating with renowned photographers. While successful as a model, he initially hesitated to embrace the profession, but was encouraged by his sisters. He has consistently returned to modelling, becoming a global brand ambassador for Loewe in 2024. His recent film roles include *Heart of Stone* (2023) and *A Haunting in Venice* (2023), continuing to demonstrate his versatility as an actor. In 2020, *The Irish Times* recognized him as one of Ireland’s greatest film actors.

title: Ushoshi Sengupta
text:
Ushoshi Sengupta is an Indian actress, model, and beauty pageant winner recognized for representing India on an international stage. She achieved national recognition by winning the inaugural “I Am She – Miss Universe India” title, a pageant organized by Tantra Entertainment Private Limited in collaboration with former Miss Universe, Sushmita Sen. This victory led to her participation in the Miss Universe 2010 competition, held in Las Vegas, Nevada, on August 23, 2010. She competed against 83 other delegates, ultimately finishing among them as the crown went to Ximena Navarrete of Mexico.

Born in Kolkata, Sengupta comes from a family with a military background, being the daughter of an officer in the Indian Air Force. Her early education took place at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Ballygunje, also in Kolkata, where she demonstrated a particular aptitude for mathematics. Her academic success in mathematics led to a scholarship offer for further study in engineering. However, Sengupta chose a different path, opting to pursue a degree in liberal arts and a career in professional modeling instead. 

She ultimately earned a Bachelor of Humanities degree from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata, which is affiliated with the University of Calcutta. Prior to her success in the Miss Universe India pageant, Sengupta already had experience working as a model. 

Following her participation in the Miss Universe competition, Sengupta transitioned into acting, making her debut in the Bengali film industry with the movie *Egoler Chokh*. Directed by Arindam Sil, the film was released in August 2016, marking her entry into the world of cinema. While the article focuses primarily on her pageant background, it signals a career shift toward acting following her time as a beauty queen.

title: Patricia Cladis
text:
Patricia Cladis was a Canadian-American physicist who dedicated her career to the study of liquid crystals. Born in Shanghai in 1937, she received her early education at Little Flower Academy in Vancouver, British Columbia, graduating in 1955. She continued her education at the University of British Columbia, earning a Bachelor of Arts degree in combined Honours Mathematics and Physics in 1959. Following this, she obtained a Master of Arts degree in physics from the University of Toronto in 1960, and a PhD in physics, specializing in superconductivity, from the University of Rochester in 1968.

Before focusing solely on physics research, Cladis held diverse roles. After her master’s degree, she worked as a meteorologist for Transport Canada and later as a programmer-analyst at KCS Ltd. in 1962. She began her academic career as an assistant professor of physics at Western Connecticut State University in 1963, concurrently working as a research assistant at the University of Rochester while completing her doctoral studies. 

A pivotal period in her research occurred from 1968 to 1972, when she conducted research at the University of Paris (Orsay), focusing on liquid crystals and collaborating with the Orsay Liquid Crystal Group, led by Professor Pierre-Gilles de Gennes, who later won the Nobel Prize for his work in the field. In 1972, she joined Bell Labs as a research physicist, continuing her exploration of liquid crystals for 25 years. She then transitioned to the private sector, founding Advanced Liquid Crystal Technologies in Summit, New Jersey, in 1997. This company focused on both physical and biological research.

Throughout her career, Cladis was recognized for her significant contributions to physics. She was named a fellow of the American Physical Society in 1983 and received a Guggenheim Fellowship in 1993. She also earned the Humboldt Prize, acknowledging her lifetime achievements and promoting international scientific collaboration.  She served on the Editorial Board of *Liquid Crystals* from 1986 to 1993 and was a board member of the International Liquid Crystal Society. She also held visiting appointments at numerous universities, including Northwestern University where she received the Edith Kreeger Wolf Distinguished Professor award, University of Paris (Orsay), École Pratique des Hautes Études, École Normale Supérieure, Weizmann Institute of Science, University of Duisburg-Essen, and University of Bayreuth. 

Her research centered on the material properties and processing of liquid crystals, specifically focusing on defects, the reentrant nematic phase, and phase transitions and pattern formation. Later in her career, she expanded her interests to patterns in complex fluids, including polymers, culminating in the publication of a book on patterns in complex systems in 1995.  She authored or co-authored over 130 publications and edited several books, with *Spatio-temporal patterns in nonequilibrium complex systems* being her most well-known edited work. Patricia Cladis passed away in Summit, New Jersey, on July 3, 2017.

title: Idris Elba
text:
Idrissa Akuna Elba, known professionally as Idris Elba, is a highly successful English actor and musician born in London in 1972. He has achieved significant recognition for his work, including a Golden Globe Award and numerous nominations for BAFTA and Emmy Awards. In 2016, *Time* magazine included him on its list of the 100 Most Influential People in the World. His films have collectively grossed over $9.8 billion worldwide, placing him among the top 20 highest-grossing actors of all time.

Elba’s acting journey began with studies at the National Youth Music Theatre and early roles in television productions like *Crimewatch* and *The Boot Street Band*. He gained prominence playing Stringer Bell in the acclaimed HBO series *The Wire* (2002-2004) and later as DCI John Luther in the BBC One series *Luther* (2010-2019), a role which earned him a Golden Globe. He’s also appeared in notable television shows like *The Office* and *The Big C*, and more recently in the Apple TV+ thriller *Hijack*. 

His film career is extensive, including roles in *American Gangster*, *Prometheus*, *Star Trek Beyond*, and *The Suicide Squad*. He portrayed Nelson Mandela in *Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom*, earning another Golden Globe nomination. Notably, he received a Screen Actors Guild Award for his performance in the Netflix drama *Beasts of No Nation*. Elba has also lent his voice to animated films such as *Zootopia*, *The Jungle Book*, *Finding Dory*, and the *Sonic the Hedgehog* franchise, voicing Knuckles the Echidna. He made his directorial debut with the film *Yardie* in 2018.

Elba’s early life was spent in Hackney and East Ham, London, where he shortened his name from Idrissa to Idris while at school. He comes from a Sierra Leonean and Ghanaian heritage, with his parents having immigrated to London from Sierra Leone. He supported himself through various jobs while pursuing acting, including DJing, tyre-fitting, and working at the Ford Dagenham plant. He began DJing professionally in his teens under the name DJ Big Driis.

Beyond acting, Elba is a successful DJ and R&B singer, performing under the monikers DJ Big Driis and Idris. He is also a co-owner of the Formula E racing team, Kiro Race Co. He has established his own production company, Green Door Pictures, with Apple, and more recently 22Summers, focusing on developing original content. He is currently involved in projects including an Afrofuturist animated series and a film studio in Zanzibar, as well as a documentary on knife crime in the UK.

title: Daniel Ek
text:
Daniel Ek, born in Stockholm, Sweden in 1983, is a businessman and technologist best known as the co-founder and CEO of the music streaming service Spotify. As of May 2025, Forbes estimates his net worth to be $9.2 billion. He grew up in the Rågsved district and briefly attended the KTH Royal Institute of Technology before dropping out to pursue a career in IT.

Ek’s early career involved building websites and working with open-source technologies from a young age. He held positions at companies like Jajja, Tradera (later acquired by eBay), and Stardoll, serving as CTO for the latter. He also founded Advertigo, an online advertising company, which he sold to TradeDoubler in 2006. Following this, he briefly led μTorrent before its sale to BitTorrent, and Ludvig Strigeus, a developer from μTorrent, later joined him at Spotify.

The idea for Spotify arose in 2002, observing the difficulties in combating music piracy after the shutdown of Napster. Ek envisioned a legal streaming service that would offer a superior alternative to piracy while providing compensation to the music industry. He co-founded Spotify AB with Martin Lorentzon in 2006, launching the service in 2008. Originally utilizing a peer-to-peer model, Spotify transitioned to a server-client system in 2014. Lorentzon stepped down as chairman in 2016, with Ek assuming the role alongside his duties as CEO. By 2017, Spotify had over 217 million active users and had garnered over $2.5 billion in funding. Ek was named the most powerful person in the music industry by Billboard that same year, and in 2022, he personally invested $50 million in Spotify stock.

Beyond Spotify, Ek co-founded Neko Health in 2018, a medical technology company focused on non-invasive full-body scanning using AI, which launched in 2023. He also established Prima Materia in 2021, an investment firm with a $1 billion pledge to support European technology “moonshots,” and serves as chairman of German defense technology company Helsing, a recipient of significant investment from Prima Materia.

Ek has been vocal about the challenges facing startups in Sweden, co-authoring an open letter in 2016 advocating for changes to laws concerning housing, taxation, and education to prevent companies like Spotify from relocating. He has also offered insights into the evolving music industry, suggesting artists need to focus on continuous engagement with fans rather than infrequent album releases. Recent comments regarding the “shelf life” of content sparked criticism from musicians, leading to clarifications from Ek emphasizing his support for creative expression. 

Personally, Ek is married to Sofia Levander and has two daughters. He's a supporter of Arsenal Football Club and made an unsuccessful bid to purchase the team in 2021. His story was depicted in the 2022 Netflix series *The Playlist*, where he was portrayed by Edvin Endre. His views and Spotify’s business practices have faced criticism from artists concerned about fair compensation and the impact on the music industry, prompting Spotify to release annual artist remuneration reports. Some artists have even removed their music from Spotify in protest of Prima Materia’s investments in defense technology.

title: Joseph Michael Linsner
text:
Joseph Michael Linsner, born December 13, 1968, is an American comic book writer and artist, best known for creating the character Dawn, a mature-audiences, supernatural figure, and for his depictions of female characters. He’s established himself as a prominent cover artist within the comics industry. Growing up in Queens, New York, Linsner was influenced early on by titles like Batman and X-Men, as well as the work of Alberto Vargas, and later by creators such as Alan Moore, Pat Mills, and David Cronenberg. His father’s death when he was 14 had a significant impact on his life.

Linsner began his career by self-publishing *Cry for Dawn* in 1989 through Cry for Dawn Productions, co-founded with Joseph M. Monks, which ran for nine issues. After the production company dissolved in 1993, he continued to publish Dawn through Sirius Entertainment with various limited series and one-shots until 2000. He entered mainstream comics by providing a cover for *Justice League Quarterly* #13 in 1993. He subsequently worked with Marvel Comics on projects like *Killraven* #1, covers for *Mystique*, and the *Wolverine-Black Cat* limited series, *Claws*, and its sequel in 2011. 

Beyond his character-driven work, Linsner is also known for his benefit work. In 2002, he self-published *I Love New York*, a comic intended as a fundraiser for the American Red Cross following the September 11th attacks, reflecting his personal experience as a New Yorker.  He has also provided illustrations for the book *Our Gods Wear Spandex* and contributed cover art to titles from Topps Comics, Dark Horse Comics, and Dynamite Entertainment, becoming a prolific cover artist for the latter, particularly for licensed characters like Red Sonja and Vampirella starting in 2012. Linsner is a long-time supporter of The Hero Initiative, an organization providing assistance to comic book creators.

Linsner’s career has been marked by some controversy. In 2013, he publicly accused his former assistant, Eva Hopkins, of selling his original artwork without his permission, leading to a public dispute. He is married to Kristina Deak-Linsner.

Throughout his career, Linsner has received recognition for his work. He was nominated for an Eisner Award for Best Painter/Digital Artist in 1997 and was awarded an Inkpot Award at the 2007 San Diego Comic-Con. He was also a guest of honor at the 2008 Toronto Comic Con alongside Herb Trimpe and Greg Land. He has an extensive bibliography including numerous *Dawn* series, *Dark Ivory*, and contributions to titles like *Harley Quinn*.

title: Julian Jarrold
text:
Julian Jarrold, born in Norwich in 1961, is a British film and television director who has received a BAFTA nomination and an Emmy nomination for his work. He comes from a distinguished family background, being a descendant of the Huguenot founders of Jarrolds of Norwich, a department store established in 1823, and the only son of Peter Jarrold and Juliet Pollard. He was educated at Gresham’s School in Holt and later at Trinity & All Saints College in Leeds. He is married to Jo Higgins and currently resides in Primrose Hill, London.

Jarrold’s directorial career began with the 1999 adaptation of *Great Expectations*, praised for its understated character portrayals. He followed this with the widely popular 2006 television film *Kinky Boots*, described as enjoyable and well-made, though relatively lightweight. In 2007, he directed *Becoming Jane*, a film noted for its witty and visually appealing direction, employing techniques like tracking shots and clever focus.

A significant undertaking was his 2008 adaptation of Evelyn Waugh’s *Brideshead Revisited*, a novel considered a classic and previously unfilmed. Jarrold acknowledged the pressure of adapting such a beloved work but also saw an opportunity to introduce it to a new generation unfamiliar with the story. The film was commended for its period detail while avoiding excessive spectacle. 

He directed the HBO film *The Girl* in 2013, earning him his first Emmy nomination. Subsequently, he took on the serial killer film *Exit 147* and *A Royal Night Out*, released in 2015. His work on *Red Riding 1974*, part of a trilogy, was particularly lauded, with critics praising its film noir aesthetic and the performances of its cast, including Andrew Garfield and Sean Bean. The film utilized Super 16 millimeter film to create a gritty and atmospheric visual style. 

More recently, in 2023, Jarrold’s *The Good Mothers* received the best series award at the Berlin International Festival. Beyond directing, Jarrold served as a judge for the Norwich Film Festival in 2016 and was appointed its patron in 2017. Earlier in his career, in 1988, he worked as a producer on the TV mini-series *The Other Side of Midnight*.

title: Kari Matchett
text:
Kari Matchett is a Canadian actress with a diverse career spanning television and film. Born in Spalding, Saskatchewan, she received her education at Lethbridge Collegiate Institute in Alberta before pursuing theatre training at the National Theatre School in Montreal and the Moscow Theatre School. She honed her stage skills with three years at the Stratford Shakespeare Festival in Ontario.

Matchett’s early television work in Canada included roles in *The Rez* and a breakthrough starring role as Colleen Blessed in *Power Play* from 1998 to 2000. She then appeared in *A Nero Wolfe Mystery* playing various characters, including a recurring role as Lily Rowan, alongside Timothy Hutton. She also took on the role of Beth in *Wonderfalls*, portraying the love interest of a lesbian character. 

Her film career began with roles in *Apartment Hunting* (2000) and *Angel Eyes* (2001), followed by *Cube 2: Hypercube* (2002) and *Men with Brooms* (2002). She continued to work steadily in both film and television, appearing in *Cypher* (2002), *Five Days to Midnight* (2003), and *Blue Murder*, for which she won a Gemini Award after a guest appearance in 2001. 

Throughout the 2000s, Matchett took on roles in several television series including *Invasion* (2005), *Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip*, *Shark*, *Wild Card*, and *Intimate Stranger*. She also had parts in *Civic Duty* (2006) with Peter Krause, and *24* (2007), as well as recurring roles in *Heartland* (2007), *ER* (2007-2008), and *Crash* (2008-2009), the latter playing the daughter of Dennis Hopper’s character. A reunion with Timothy Hutton occurred on *Leverage*, where she played Maggie Collins, the ex-wife of his character.

From 2010 to 2014, Matchett played a significant role as Joan Campbell in the USA Network series *Covert Affairs*. She also appeared in supporting roles in critically acclaimed films, including Terrence Malick’s *The Tree of Life* (2011), which won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival, and *Maudie* (2016) alongside Ethan Hawke. More recently, in 2023, she joined the cast of the Netflix series *The Night Agent* as U.S. president Michelle Travers.

title: Belisarius
text:
Belisarius, a military commander of the Byzantine Empire under Justinian I, lived around 500-565 AD and is renowned as one of history’s greatest generals, particularly for his success despite often limited resources. He was instrumental in reclaiming much of the Mediterranean territory once held by the Western Roman Empire. Born likely in Germania (modern Sapareva Banya, Bulgaria) to potentially Illyro-Roman or Thraco-Roman parents, he rose through the ranks to become a senior guardsman to Justinian by 526, though the specifics of his early advancement are unknown. He was granted permission to form the *bucellarii*, an elite cavalry regiment of 7,000 men equipped with lances, composite bows and swords, that served as the core of his future armies.

Belisarius’ early military career was marked by both defeats and successes. He participated in the Iberian War against the Sasanian Persians, experiencing setbacks at battles like Tanurin and Mindouos, though he also led successful raids. Despite these initial failures, he was appointed to command a Roman army in the east by Justinian, and in 530, achieved a decisive victory at the Battle of Dara, forcing the Persians into peace negotiations. A subsequent defeat at Callinicum, however, nearly derailed the peace process, and he was briefly charged with incompetence, though ultimately exonerated. He also successfully repelled a Hunnic incursion at Melantias and employed deception to thwart a Persian invasion and lift a siege at Ariminum.

Following the Nika riots in Constantinople in 532, where riots nearly toppled Justinian, Belisarius, alongside other commanders, brutally suppressed the rebellion, resulting in a massive loss of life. This demonstrated his loyalty and military prowess to the emperor. In 533, Justinian tasked Belisarius with conquering the Vandal Kingdom in North Africa, citing religious persecution and political instability as justification.

The Vandalic War was launched with an army of around 17,000 soldiers, supported by a substantial naval force.  Factors contributing to the campaign's feasibility included Vandal weaknesses – recent Berber defeats, internal revolts, and a lack of preparedness – and Belisarius’ experience and leadership.  The voyage to Africa was fraught with challenges, including spoiled supplies and unfavorable weather, but Belisarius maintained discipline and organization. He quickly seized the opportunity presented by the Vandal’s lack of coastal defenses, initiating a swift and successful campaign that culminated in the defeat of the Vandal king Gelimer and the conquest of the Vandal kingdom within nine months.  While initial intentions may have been limited to securing Tripolitania, Belisarius’ actions at Sicily set in motion Justinian's broader reconquest plans.

title: Johann Christian von Engel
text:
Johann Christian von Engel was a historian born in 1770 in Leutschau, a town now known as Levoča, which was then part of the Kingdom of Hungary under the rule of the Habsburg monarchy. He passed away in 1814, leaving behind a legacy as a significant scholar of Central and Eastern European history. Engel’s education took place at the University of Göttingen, where he studied under prominent academics Heyne and Schlözer, figures who undoubtedly influenced his approach to historical research. 

Throughout his career, Engel dedicated himself to writing detailed historical accounts. His work was considered remarkably comprehensive and scholarly for its time, representing a substantial accumulation of knowledge on the regions he studied. He is particularly noted for being a pioneer in establishing a firm, academic foundation for the histories of Hungary, Ukraine, and the Danubian principalities – areas whose historical narratives had previously lacked rigorous scholarly treatment. 

Engel authored several major works that cemented his reputation. His most significant publication was “Die Geschichte der Ukraine und der ukrainische Kosaken, wie auch der Königreiche Halitsch-Wladimir” (History of Ukraine and the Ukrainian Cossacks, along with the Kingdom of Halych-Volodymyr), published in Halle in 1796. This work provided a detailed examination of Ukrainian history, including the role of the Cossacks and the Kingdom of Halych-Volodymyr. 

Following this, he produced “Geschichte des ungarischen Reiches und seine Nebenländer” (History of imperial Hungary and neighboring lands), a five-volume series completed between 1797 and 1804. This extensive work offered a broad overview of Hungarian history and the surrounding territories. In 1804, he published “Geschichte der Moldau und Walachey” (History of Moldavia and Wallachia), focusing on the historical development of these Danubian principalities. Finally, he completed another five-volume work, “Geschichte des Königreichs Ungarn” (History of the Kingdom of Hungary) in 1814, shortly before his death.

In recognition of his contributions to scholarship, Engel was ennobled in 1812, adding “von” to his name, a title reflecting his elevated status within the Austrian Empire. His works remained valuable resources for historians for years, and continue to be referenced as important early scholarly contributions to the understanding of Central and Eastern European history.

title: Grant Bowler
text:
Grant Bowler is a New Zealand-born, Australia-raised actor and television presenter with a diverse career spanning film, television, and theatre in multiple countries. Born in 1968, he began his television career with a role as Constable Wayne Patterson on the Australian police drama *Blue Heelers* from 1993 to 1996. He subsequently appeared in *Pacific Drive*, *Medivac*, *Always Greener*, *Stingers*, and the adaptation of *On the Beach*, along with a year-long stint on the ABC series *Something in the Air* and a role in the miniseries *Through My Eyes*. He also had a recurring role on *All Saints* between 2004 and 2005.

Beyond acting, Bowler is well-known as a presenter, notably hosting the Australian versions of *The Mole* from 2000 to 2003 and *The Amazing Race Australia* for three seasons beginning in 2010. He stepped down from *The Amazing Race* in 2019. For nearly two decades, since 2004, he has been the voiceover narrator for *Border Security: Australia*, and also narrates the Canadian and American versions of the show when they air in Australia and New Zealand as *Border Security: International*.

Bowler has also taken on significant roles in international productions. He played Wolfgang West in the New Zealand series *Outrageous Fortune*, and guest starred as Captain Gault on the American show *Lost*. He portrayed Connor Owens, a character described as having "evil secrets," in *Ugly Betty* and appeared as a werewolf named Cooter in *True Blood*. He also took on the role of Hank Rearden in the film *Atlas Shrugged: Part I* and Richard Burton in the TV movie *Liz & Dick*. More recently, he had a recurring role in *The Baker and the Beauty*. 

A graduate of the National Institute of Dramatic Art, Bowler’s early career included extensive work with the Bell Shakespeare Company. He has also appeared in films such as *Killer Elite*, *Gallipoli*, *Swelter*, *400 Days*, *Lucky Dog*, and *Zooey to the Max*. He separated from his wife, actress Roxane Wilson, in 2011, after nine years of marriage and they share two children.

title: Robert Jennings (rugby league)
text:
Robert Jennings, born in Blacktown, New South Wales in 1996, is a rugby league footballer of Tongan international calibre. He comes from a strong sporting family, with his brother Michael playing for the Sydney Roosters and another brother, George, for the Melbourne Storm. He is also the nephew of former All Black Arthur Jennings. His early football development took place with the Western City Tigers and Minchinbury Jets before he was signed by the Penrith Panthers.

Jennings began his National Rugby League (NRL) career with the Penrith Panthers, making his debut in round 7 of the 2015 season against the Gold Coast Titans. He also represented the Junior Kangaroos and the New South Wales Under-20s that year. Despite being contracted with Penrith until the end of 2016, he saw limited game time in 2016 and subsequently signed a one-year deal with the South Sydney Rabbitohs.

His time with the Rabbitohs proved more fruitful. He debuted in 2017 and in 2018 enjoyed a breakout season, scoring a hat-trick against Manly and later a remarkable four tries in a game against Parramatta. He finished the 2018 season with an impressive 19 tries. 

In 2019, Jennings moved to the Wests Tigers on a two-year contract, making 18 appearances in his first season, although the team missed out on finals contention. He was released from the Tigers in September 2020. He then returned to the Penrith Panthers for the 2021 and 2022 seasons, primarily as cover during State of Origin periods, and was part of their NSW Cup Grand Final winning team in 2022, also featuring in their NRL State Championship victory.

Most recently, Jennings signed a two-year contract with the newly established Dolphins in May 2022, debuting for the club in 2023. After his contract expired at the end of the 2023 NRL season, he transitioned away from the NRL, and in 2025 joined the Stanley River Wolves, a local Queensland rugby league club, where he now plays in the second row, continuing his rugby league career at a community level. As of round 11, 2025, he has scored six tries for the Wolves.

title: Leo Kokubo
text:
Leo Kokubo, born on January 23, 2001, is a professional footballer who currently plays as a goalkeeper for Sint-Truiden, a Belgian team. He is of mixed heritage, with a Nigerian father and a Japanese mother, and was born in Japan. Kokubo has represented Japan at various youth levels, including the U16, U18, and U23 national teams.

His involvement with the Japan U23 squad culminated in a significant achievement in April 2024 when he was selected for the 2024 AFC U-23 Asian Cup. During the final match of this tournament against Uzbekistan, Kokubo played a crucial role in securing a 1–0 victory for Japan. Late in the game, during stoppage time, he successfully saved a penalty kick taken by Umarali Rakhmonaliev. This pivotal save directly contributed to Japan winning the AFC U-23 Asian Cup for the second time in the nation’s history. 

As a direct result of his outstanding performance in the final, Kokubo was awarded the “Man of the match” honor. This recognition highlighted his key contribution to the team's success and his individual skill as a goalkeeper.

Beyond his national team achievements, Kokubo has also experienced club-level success. He was part of the Benfica team that won the Supertaça Cândido de Oliveira in 2023, a Portuguese Super Cup competition. As of February 15, 2025, his career statistics are recorded, though specific details of those statistics are not provided in the available information. 

In summary, Leo Kokubo has established himself as a promising goalkeeper, demonstrating his abilities both at the youth international level for Japan and with his club, Benfica. His performance in the 2024 AFC U-23 Asian Cup final, marked by a crucial penalty save and a “Man of the match” award, stands as a highlight of his career thus far.

title: Carol Dweck
text:
Carol Dweck, born in New York in 1946, is a prominent American psychologist currently holding the Lewis and Virginia Eaton Professorship of Psychology at Stanford University. Her career has included faculty positions at the University of Illinois, Harvard, and Columbia University before arriving at Stanford in 2004. Throughout her career, she has received numerous accolades including being named a James McKeen Cattell Fellow, a Mentor Awardee, and a William James Fellow by the Association for Psychological Science (APS), as well as election to the National Academy of Sciences in 2012. 

Dweck’s upbringing included an experience in sixth grade where students were ranked by IQ, leading her to become hesitant to risk appearing less intelligent. She graduated from Barnard College in 1967 and earned her Ph.D. in psychology from Yale University in 1972. Her academic journey led her through various universities before establishing herself at Stanford.

Dweck’s research is centered on motivation and mindset, particularly the concept of implicit theories of intelligence. Introduced in a 1988 paper, these “implicit theories” – also known as implicit beliefs, self-theories, or mindsets – represent core assumptions about whether personal attributes are malleable or fixed. This work gained broader public attention with the publication of her 2006 book, *Mindset: The New Psychology of Success*. 

According to Dweck, individuals operate on a continuum between a “fixed mindset,” believing abilities are innate and unchangeable, and a “growth mindset,” believing abilities can be developed through dedication and hard work.  Those with a fixed mindset prioritize appearing intelligent, fearing failure as a reflection of their inherent limitations. Conversely, a growth mindset embraces challenges, views failure as a learning opportunity, and fosters a belief in continuous improvement. Dweck emphasizes that mindset isn’t always consciously recognized but is evident in reactions to setbacks. She argues that adopting a growth mindset leads to a less stressful and more successful life.  She cautions against simply praising effort, emphasizing the importance of acknowledging current achievement levels while working towards improvement.  She also cautions against praising intelligence, as this can inadvertently encourage a fixed mindset.

More recently, Dweck has been developing a broader theory connecting motivation and mindset to social and personality development, published in 2017. However, her research has faced criticism.  Some researchers have found it difficult to replicate her findings, with concerns raised about the fragility of the effects and the challenges of implementing mindset interventions in real-world settings like classrooms. A large-scale trial in England in 2019, involving over 5000 pupils, found no significant impact of growth mindset training on literacy or numeracy. Despite this, Dweck has been praised for her openness to addressing methodological concerns. 

Dweck is married to David Goldman, a theatre director and critic. Her work continues to be highly influential, and she received the Yidan Prize for Education Research in 2017, along with substantial funding for future projects.  She has authored and co-authored numerous academic papers and books, solidifying her position as a leading figure in the field of psychology.

title: Ted Thompson
text:
Ted Thompson, born January 17, 1953, and passing away January 20, 2021, enjoyed a lengthy career in professional football as both a player and an executive. He spent ten years as a linebacker and special teams player for the Houston Oilers from 1975 to 1984, starting nine games over that period and proving remarkably durable, appearing in 146 of 147 games. Undrafted out of Southern Methodist University where he was a three-year starter at linebacker and team captain, Thompson initially found a role with the Oilers thanks to a prior connection with coach Bum Phillips. He even filled in as an emergency kicker in one game, successfully converting four extra points.

Thompson transitioned to team management with the Green Bay Packers in 1992, hired by Ron Wolf as a scout. He steadily rose through the ranks, becoming director of pro personnel in 1993, and later director of player personnel in 1997. During his initial tenure with the Packers, the team reached the playoffs six times and won Super Bowl XXXI in 1997. He left the Packers in 1999, recruited by former Packers coach Mike Holmgren to join the Seattle Seahawks as their vice president of operations and head of scouting.

In Seattle, Thompson worked alongside Holmgren, contributing to a team that reached the playoffs twice and ultimately the Super Bowl in 2005 following his departure. Several key players on that Seahawks Super Bowl team, including Shaun Alexander, Darrell Jackson, and Steve Hutchinson, were acquired during Thompson’s time there. Holmgren credited Thompson with helping the team make “good decisions” during that period. 

Thompson returned to Green Bay as general manager in 2005, inheriting a team over the salary cap. He made difficult initial decisions, releasing several veteran players, and focused on building through the draft, notably selecting Aaron Rodgers in the first round. He prioritized low-cost free agents to fill gaps.  The Packers ultimately had a difficult 2005 season, finishing with a 4–12 record. He then hired Mike McCarthy as head coach in 2006, and oversaw a period of sustained success. 

Over the next decade, Thompson continued to emphasize drafting and developing players. He oversaw the Packers’ Super Bowl XLV victory in 2011.  He was known for his patience and long-term vision, often prioritizing character and potential over immediate impact. He was recognized for his work with the Sporting News NFL Executive of the Year award in 2008. Thompson’s tenure also included navigating the complexities of Brett Favre’s retirement and eventual trade to the New York Jets.  He revealed in 2019 that he was battling an autonomic disorder.

title: Mark Murphy (singer)
text:
Mark Murphy, a highly respected jazz singer, was born in Syracuse, New York, in 1932 and passed away in 2015. He built a career spanning over six decades, recording 51 albums under his own name and becoming known for his innovative vocal improvisations. His talent was recognized with four Down Beat magazine awards for Best Male Vocalist between 1996 and 2001, and he received five Grammy nominations for Best Vocal Jazz Performance. Beyond performing, Murphy also wrote lyrics to well-known jazz tunes, including “Stolen Moments” and “Red Clay.”

Murphy’s musical upbringing was steeped in tradition, with his parents involved in church choir direction and his grandmother and aunt serving as church organists. He began piano lessons at age seven and in his teens, joined his brother’s jazz dance band, drawing early influence from singers like Peggy Lee, Nat “King” Cole, and Ella Fitzgerald, as well as pianist Art Tatum. He studied Music and Drama at Syracuse University, graduating in 1953 after being discovered by Sammy Davis Jr. who helped connect him with opportunities in New York City.

After moving to New York, Murphy pursued both acting and singing, performing with the Gilbert and Sullivan Light Opera Company and appearing on television, while also twice placing second in amateur singing contests at the Apollo Theatre.
