His recording career began with Decca Records in 1956, but after modest success, he moved to Los Angeles in 1958, recording for Capitol Records and achieving a minor hit with “This Could Be the Start of Something.”  Returning to New York in the early 1960s, he recorded for Riverside Records, including the album *Rah* featuring accompaniment from jazz greats like Bill Evans and Clark Terry, and *That’s How I Love the Blues*, which became a personal favorite. His 1963 single “Fly Me to the Moon” achieved chart success and earned him a "New Star of the Year" award from *Down Beat*.

In 1963, Murphy relocated to London, establishing himself in the jazz scene at Ronnie Scott's Club and gaining regular airplay on BBC Radio. This period included recordings in London and Germany, including the acclaimed *Midnight Mood*. He also worked on Dutch radio and appeared in British film and television productions, and it was during this time he met his long-time partner, Eddie O'Sullivan. 

Returning to the United States in 1972, Murphy embarked on a prolific period with the Muse label, releasing an album per year for over fourteen years. These albums included Grammy-nominated works like *Satisfaction Guaranteed* and *Bop for Kerouac*, the latter reflecting his admiration for writer Jack Kerouac. He later explored Brazilian music, collaborating with the band Viva Brasil and incorporating the music of Antonio Carlos Jobim and Milton Nascimento into his repertoire. 

His career continued with recordings on Milestone and HighNote Records, as well as collaborations with artists in the acid jazz and hip-hop genres, including UFO. Throughout his later years, he released numerous anthologies and continued touring internationally, performing in the U.S., Europe, Australia, and Japan until shortly before his death in 2015. He was the first recipient of the Jazz Foundation of America’s “Words and Music Award” in 2009, cementing his legacy as “a major name in vocal jazz.”

title: Rigoberto Torres
text:
Rigoberto Torres, born in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico in 1960, is a sculptor currently living and working in Florida. His early artistic experience involved working in a factory that produced cast religious figures, a skill that would later inform his artistic practice. He also identifies as a community-based artist, a description reflected in much of his work. Torres is particularly recognized for his collaborative sculptures with artist John Ahearn, created between 1981 and 1985. These pieces predominantly feature plaster and fiberglass depictions of the artists’ neighbors in the Bronx, New York City. 

Together, Torres and Ahearn created four significant murals: *We Are Family*, *Life on Dawson Street*, *Double Dutch*, and *Back to School*. *Double Dutch*, originally created in 1981 and restored in 2010, is now part of the collection at the Pérez Art Museum Miami. These sculptures weren’t confined to galleries; they were intentionally placed in public spaces – affixed to buildings, standing freely, and incorporated into street events as a form of performance art. Torres and Ahearn frequently moved their studio to the sidewalk to encourage neighborhood participation, with children often serving as both observers and models.

Torres’ work is characterized by a naturalistic approach to portraying people, resulting in accurate and compelling representations. His sculptures are described as demonstrating an instinctive ability to create scenes from individual figures, placing them within the tradition of humanistic naturalism. He first met Ahearn in 1980 while working at the religious statuary factory, and their partnership led to the creation of what is sometimes referred to as the “South Bronx Hall of Fame.” This body of work aimed to create monuments to everyday individuals, offering an alternative to the conventional practice of public monuments honoring only the famous or heroic.

Several of these collaborative sculptures remain installed throughout the Bronx. *Double Dutch* can be found at the intersection of Kelly Street and Intervale Avenue, while *Life on Dawson St.* is located on Longwood Avenue and Dawson Street. *We Are Family* faces 156th Street on Southern Boulevard, and additional casts are situated outside The POINT Community Development Corporation on Garrison Avenue. 

Beyond his work in the Bronx, Torres returned to his native Puerto Rico in 1990, where he created twenty-two pieces over a year, including a work titled *Ruth Fernandez* in 1991. His artistic output demonstrates a commitment to representing communities and individuals through accessible, public art.

title: Amr Diab
text:
Amr Diab, born on October 11, 1961, in Port Said, Egypt, is a highly successful singer, composer, and actor who has become a prominent figure in the Arabic music world and beyond. Coming from a middle-class background in Sharqia Governorate, he earned a bachelor's degree in music from the Cairo Academy of Arts in 1986. His musical career began in 1983 with the release of his first album, *Ya Tareeq*, and quickly gained momentum with subsequent albums like *Ghanny Men Albak* (1984), *Hala Hala* (1986), and *Mayyal* (1988) released through Delta Sound. 

Throughout the 1990s, Diab continued to release popular albums including *Habibi* (1991), *Ayyamna* (1992), and *Rag'een* (1995). He pioneered the use of high-tech music videos in the Middle East in 1992. A turning point came in 1996 with *Nour El Ain*, released through Alam El Phan, which earned him his first World Music Award and broadened his international recognition. He continued with Alam El Phan, releasing *Amarain* (1999) and collaborating with artists like Khaled and Angela Dimitriou. His style, particularly evident in “Nour El Ain”, has been described as “Mediterranean music,” a fusion of Western and Middle Eastern rhythms.

After leaving Alam El Phan, Diab signed with Rotana Records, releasing *Leily Nahary* (2004) and the highly successful *Kammel Kalamak* (2005), and *El Lilady* (2007).  He faced a challenge in 2009 when his album *Wayah* was leaked online, prompting fans to boycott illegal sites, but went on to win four African Music Awards that same year.  Further albums followed with Rotana, including *Banadeek Taala* (2011) and *Shoft El Ayam* (2014), the latter reaching number one on the Billboard World Albums chart – a first for a Middle Eastern artist.  

In 2016, he moved to Nay For Media, releasing *Ahla w Ahla*. Subsequent albums with Nay Records included *Maadi el Nas* (2017) and *Kol Hayaty* (2018), alongside mini-albums and a prolific release of singles between 2021 and 2023. His 30th album, *Sahran*, was released in February 2020, followed by *Ya Ana Ya La* later that year. In December 2023, he released *Makanak*. He also participated in promotional work, releasing singles for Vodafone Music and Hyde Park in March 2024.  Notably, his song "Tamally Maak" was named one of the Best Arabic Pop Songs of the 21st Century by Rolling Stone in April 2024.

Diab has also ventured into acting, appearing in the films *El Afareet* (1989), *Ice Cream in Gleam* (1992) – which was recognized by UCLA’s School of Theater, Film and Television – and *Deahk We La'ab* (1993), though his primary focus remained music.

Throughout his career, Diab has received numerous accolades, including seven World Music Awards, six African Music Awards, two All Africa Music Awards, and a Guinness World Record for being the best-selling Middle Eastern artist. He is known for composing over 97 of his own songs and is considered a pioneer in bringing music videos to the MENA region. He faced criticism during the 2011 Egyptian uprising for perceived silence, but responded with the patriotic song "Masr A'let".

title: Joel Edgerton
text:
Joel Edgerton, born in Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia in 1974, is a versatile actor and filmmaker with a substantial body of work spanning Australian and international productions. He began his career on the stage and in Australian television, gaining recognition for his role as Will McGill in the series *The Secret Life of Us*, for which he received an AACTA Award. He initially gained wider international attention playing Owen Lars in *Star Wars: Attack of the Clones* and *Revenge of the Sith*, a role he revisited in the Disney+ series *Obi-Wan Kenobi*.

Throughout his career, Edgerton has consistently appeared in a diverse range of films. Notable Australian contributions include *The Square*, *Animal Kingdom*—winning him another AACTA Award—*Wish You Were Here*, and *Felony*. He’s also featured in major international films like *King Arthur*, *Warrior*, *Zero Dark Thirty*, *The Great Gatsby*, *Black Mass*, *Bright*, *The Green Knight*, *Master Gardener*, and *The Boys in the Boat*. Beyond film, he’s appeared in television series such as *The Underground Railroad* and the science fiction series *Dark Matter*.

Edgerton’s talents extend beyond acting; he is a skilled filmmaker. He wrote, directed, and starred in the critically acclaimed thriller *The Gift* (2015), earning him a nomination for a DGA Award. He followed this success with *Boy Erased* (2018), which he also wrote and directed, and co-wrote *The King* the following year. He’s also lent his voice to animated projects, including *Legend of the Guardians: The Owls of Ga'Hoole* and a guest appearance voicing a character in the children’s show *Bluey*. 

His personal life includes a past relationship with Olympic athlete Cathy Freeman and a current relationship with Christine Centenera, editor-in-chief of Vogue Australia, with whom he has twins born in 2021. He comes from a creative family, with his brother Nash Edgerton working as a stuntman and filmmaker; the two have collaborated on several projects, including the film *Gringo*, and are both part of the Blue-Tongue Films collective. 

Edgerton is also committed to philanthropic work, serving as a distinguished ambassador for The Fred Hollows Foundation, an organization dedicated to restoring sight and improving eye health globally and within Australia. He views this work as a meaningful counterbalance to the demands of his profession. He received the Australians in Film Breakthrough Award in 2011, recognizing his accomplishments in international cinema.

title: Walter Model
text:
Otto Moritz Walter Model was a German Generalfeldmarschall during World War II, known for his aggressive early command of panzer divisions and later, his skill in defensive warfare. Born in 1891 to a non-military middle-class family, he joined the army in 1909 through the influence of an uncle. His early career was marked by ambition and outspokenness, though he was considered an unremarkable student at military school. He served with distinction in World War I, earning the Iron Cross First Class and receiving multiple wounds, which brought him to the attention of his superiors and led to his selection for General Staff training.

Between the wars, Model navigated the tumultuous political landscape of the Weimar Republic, developing a strong aversion to communism. He rose through the ranks of the reduced Reichswehr, benefiting from connections and demonstrating a dedication to military innovation and planning. He served in various staff and command positions, focusing on tactics and weapon development, and became close to fellow officers like Friedrich Paulus. By 1938, he was chief of staff of the IV Corps, and his support for the Nazi Party aided his advancement.

At the outbreak of World War II, Model commanded the 3rd Panzer Division during the invasion of Poland and France. Though initially lacking experience with armored units, he proved a capable commander, implementing unorthodox training methods that emphasized combined arms operations. He participated in the swift advance through France, playing a role in the encirclement of French forces. 

The invasion of the Soviet Union in 1941 marked a turning point in Model's career. He led his division with aggression, rapidly advancing into Soviet territory and reaching the Dnieper River. He implemented innovative tactics, preparing his troops for a fluid and combined arms approach. His successes on the Eastern Front brought him to the attention of Adolf Hitler, who recognized his tenacity and loyalty. Throughout the war, Hitler repeatedly tasked Model with stabilizing critical situations on the Eastern Front, appointing him to command Army Group North, Army Group North Ukraine, and Army Group Centre.

As the war turned against Germany, Model was transferred to the Western Front in August 1944 to command OB West and Army Group B. His relationship with Hitler deteriorated after the failed Battle of the Bulge. Following the encirclement of Army Group B in the Ruhr Pocket in April 1945, Model, facing defeat, took his own life on April 21st, 1945. He left behind a legacy as a hard-driving and effective, if often ruthless, commander who was deeply loyal to the Nazi regime. His decision to destroy his personal papers means much of his early life remains obscure.

title: Robbie Horgan
text:
Robbie Horgan, born on June 7, 1968, is a former Irish professional footballer who specialized as a goalkeeper. His professional career began with Shamrock Rovers, where he first appeared in a League of Ireland match on April 14, 1987. This game held particular significance as it was the final match played at Glenmalure Park (also known as Milltown) and determined the winner of the League of Ireland B Division, a title ultimately secured by Shamrock Rovers.

Horgan moved to Drogheda United in 1988, making his debut for the club on September 4th in a 2-1 victory against Bray Wanderers. He quickly established himself as a key player for Drogheda, achieving notable success during his time there. In the 1989 season, he maintained 12 clean sheets in 26 league matches, contributing to Drogheda United’s championship win in the League of Ireland First Division. He continued his strong form into the following season, 1990/1991, recording 15 clean sheets as Drogheda once again claimed the First Division title.

After spending four and a half years with Drogheda United at United Park, Horgan transferred to Shelbourne in November 1992. However, his time there was relatively brief, as he rejoined Shamrock Rovers in July 1994, remaining with the club for another eight years. During his second spell at Shamrock Rovers, Horgan gained European experience, playing in two UEFA Cup matches against Djurgårdens IF in the 2002–03 season. His final League of Ireland appearance as a player came at the end of the 2007 season.

Following his playing career, Horgan transitioned into coaching, serving as the goalkeeping coach at Sporting Fingal until the club ceased operations. In August 2009, he achieved a unique distinction, becoming the only player to have competed at both Milltown and Tallaght Stadium, marking a significant historical moment in Irish football.

Horgan returned to Drogheda United in February 2011, taking on the role of assistant to manager Mick Cooke. During their partnership, Drogheda United enjoyed success, winning the League of Ireland Cup in 2012. When Mick Cooke departed from Drogheda in November 2013, Horgan was promptly appointed as his replacement, stepping into the role of manager.

title: John Counter
text:
John Counter was a prominent Canadian businessman and politician born in 1799 who played a significant role in the development of Kingston, Ontario. He arrived in Canada with his parents in 1820 from Devonshire, England, and initially joined the family bakery business, eventually expanding into real estate, transportation, and industrial ventures. He aimed to establish Kingston as a key transportation hub between Canada and the United States.

Counter’s business interests were diverse. He invested heavily in the city’s commercial district, owning a foundry and sawmill, and was involved with the Calvin Company, proposing a ferry service to Cape Vincent, New York, anticipating the arrival of the Grand Trunk Railway. He held substantial waterfront property and shares in the Penny Bridge, now known as the La Salle Causeway, and even proposed the construction of a Wolfe Island Canal. He was a strong advocate for Kingston’s incorporation as a town, believing it would stimulate economic growth and increase property values, and signed the petition that led to its incorporation in 1838.

Politically, Counter was a highly influential figure, serving as Mayor of Kingston for five non-consecutive terms: 1841-43, 1846, 1850, 1852-53, and 1855. He was instrumental in establishing the city’s Board of Trade in 1839 and played a key role in accommodating government officials when Kingston briefly served as the capital of the Province of Canada in 1841, even offering his own home for their use. He also championed the construction of a new town hall and contributed to the donation of the first clock for the City Hall Clock Tower.

Despite his success, Counter's ambitious ventures were funded with substantial borrowing. He eventually faced financial ruin, declaring bankruptcy in 1855 due to difficulties meeting mortgage payments after resigning as mayor due to a conflict of interest involving his shares in the local gas company. He died in 1862 in relative poverty and obscurity at his son-in-law's home. 

An official portrait of Counter was painted in 1842 by American artist Alvah Bradish, commissioned by members of the town council. The portrait, depicting him with a Chain of Office and a scroll, is currently displayed in the John Counter meeting room at Kingston City Hall, having undergone restoration in the late 1970s.

title: Tanel Ingi
text:
Tanel Ingi, born on November 26, 1976, is an Estonian actor working primarily in stage and film. He is a long-standing performer at the Ugala theatre in Viljandi, where he has been a member of the company since 1998 and continues to perform. His career began while he was still a student, and he has since taken on roles in a remarkably diverse repertoire of plays, encompassing both classic and contemporary works. 

Ingi’s stage work includes performances in plays by internationally renowned authors such as William Shakespeare, Anton Chekhov, Leo Tolstoy, and Victor Hugo. He’s also performed in adaptations of works by A. A. Milne, Robert Louis Stevenson, Mark Twain, Jules Verne, Tom Stoppard, Friedrich Schiller and Estonian writers like August Gailit and Oskar Luts. This demonstrates a breadth of skill and a comfort across various dramatic styles.

Beyond the theatre, Ingi has built a substantial presence in Estonian film and television. His first film role was in the 1999 drama *Lurjus*, also known as *An Affair of Honour*, directed by Valentin Kuik and featuring Taavi Eelmaa. A particularly recognized role came in 2005 with his portrayal of Tõnu in the television film *August 1991*, directed by Ilmar Raag. This film is a dramatization of the events surrounding the failed Soviet attempt to quell the Singing Revolution, a pivotal moment in Estonia’s fight for independence.

Ingi’s television appearances are numerous and span different genres. He has been seen in the children’s series *Nöbinina*, the crime drama *Kelgukoerad* on Kanal 2, and the TV3 series *Kättemaksukontor*. He also participated in *Riigimehed*, an ETV political satire. More recently, he joined the cast of Kanal 2’s *Pilvene all* in 2015, playing the character of Andres Kroon. In 2017, he took on the role of Aivar in the ETV drama series *Pank*, a ten-part production focusing on the emergence and struggles of a new bank in Estonia during the 1990s. In 2020, he expanded his creative involvement in filmmaking by co-directing the comedy feature film *Asjad, millest me ei räägi* alongside Andrejs Ekis.

Tanel Ingi currently lives in Viljandi with his wife, Kätlin. They also maintain a summer residence located in Koeru Parish, near the village of Preedi in Järva County. His formal training began in 1995 at the Kopli-Tallinn Art School, and he later graduated from the Viljandi Culture Academy in 1999.

title: Stan Marple
text:
Stanislaus Henry Marple is a Canadian who enjoyed a lengthy career in professional ice hockey, both as a player and a coach, with a significant portion of his career spent in the United Kingdom. He played professionally for twelve seasons in various British leagues, achieving considerable recognition while with the Guildford Flames. His contributions to the Guildford Flames were so substantial that the team retired his jersey number, 3. 

Marple’s association with the Guildford Flames extended beyond his playing days; he later transitioned into a coaching role with the team, ultimately becoming their head coach. During his tenure as both head coach and general manager, the Guildford Flames secured an impressive ten titles. Specific details regarding the nature of these titles aren’t provided, but their number indicates a period of sustained success for the club under his leadership.

Prior to his extended time in the UK, Marple held a position as the general manager for the University of Alberta’s men’s hockey team, the Alberta Golden Bears, a role he fulfilled until 1994. Following his time in Alberta, he returned to ice hockey coaching in the United Kingdom, where he remained for the following thirteen years. 

While a prolific player, Marple’s playing career was curtailed after 2005 due to a league rule – specifically, the EPL’s four-import rule – which limited his regular playing time to situations where other imported players were injured. Despite this limitation, his impact on the game in the UK remained significant.

His coaching record at Guildford demonstrates a high level of success, amassing 396 wins against 174 losses and 42 ties and overtime losses. As a general manager, his record also reflects positively on his leadership, with 213 wins and 55 losses. These statistics, though not detailing specific league or season information, paint a picture of a consistently successful hockey executive and coach. Further biographical information and detailed career statistics are available through The Internet Hockey Database.

title: Wil Nieves
text:
Wil Nieves, born September 25, 1977, in Puerto Rico, enjoyed a lengthy professional baseball career primarily as a catcher, ultimately transitioning into a minor league coaching role. He played in Major League Baseball for seven different teams: the San Diego Padres, New York Yankees, Washington Nationals, Milwaukee Brewers, Colorado Rockies, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Philadelphia Phillies.

Nieves was initially drafted by the Padres in 1995 and debuted with them in 2002, appearing in 28 games. He was then selected off waivers by the Angels before being traded to the Yankees. With the Yankees in 2007, he served as a backup to Jorge Posada and was particularly valued as a personal catcher for pitcher Mike Mussina, assisting him through a difficult period. He even made a single appearance at first base due to a shortage of position players. Despite a brief, promising performance, he was designated for assignment and later played for the Yankees' Triple-A affiliate, Scranton/Wilkes-Barre, before becoming a free agent.

He continued his career with the Washington Nationals in 2008, where he hit his first major league home run – a walk-off against the Chicago Cubs. He filled a backup role for the Nationals in both 2009 and 2010, behind Jesus Flores and Iván Rodríguez respectively. Subsequent stints followed with the Milwaukee Brewers in 2010, the Atlanta Braves in 2011, and the Colorado Rockies in 2012. With the Rockies, he excelled in spring training, but was later called up to mentor younger players like Wilin Rosario and assist struggling pitchers.

Nieves also spent time with the Arizona Diamondbacks in 2012, making an immediate impact with a two-run home run in his debut. He then signed with the Philadelphia Phillies in 2013, serving as Carlos Ruiz’s backup until a leg injury sidelined him in 2014. A return to the San Diego Padres in 2015 saw him briefly make their opening day roster before being designated for assignment. He finished his playing career with a short stint in the Braves organization in 2015.

Following his playing days, Nieves transitioned into coaching. In 2019, he joined the Boston Red Sox organization as a coach for their Class A-Advanced affiliate, the Salem Red Sox, bringing his extensive baseball experience to player development. Throughout his career, Nieves was known as a solid defensive catcher and a respected teammate.

title: Vicky Kaushal
text:
Vicky Kaushal, born on May 16, 1988, in Mumbai, is a prominent Hindi film actor recognized for his numerous awards, including a National Film Award and three Filmfare Awards. He was listed in Forbes India’s Celebrity 100 in 2019. Despite coming from a film family – his father, Sham Kaushal, is an action director, and his younger brother, Sunny, is also an actor – he initially pursued a degree in electrical engineering from Rajiv Gandhi Institute of Technology, graduating in 2009, due to his father’s desire for a stable career. However, during an industrial visit, he realized his passion lay in filmmaking. He honed his skills at acting academies and through theatre, including work with Manav Kaul and Naseeruddin Shah, before beginning his film career.

Kaushal started as an assistant director to Anurag Kashyap on the film *Gangs of Wasseypur* in 2012, considering Kashyap a vital mentor. He followed this with minor roles in Kashyap’s subsequent films. His leading role debut came with the independent drama *Masaan* (2015), which garnered critical acclaim and several awards for Kaushal, including the IIFA and Screen Award for Best Male Debut. He continued to work in independent films, including *Zubaan*, where he researched stammering for a role and found it difficult to shake the habit even after filming concluded. *Raman Raghav 2.0* (2016) saw him portray a troubled police officer, requiring intense preparation and physical commitment.

A breakthrough arrived in 2018 with supporting roles in the commercially successful *Raazi* and *Sanju*. He won a Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor for his performance in *Sanju*, where he played a character inspired by one of Sanjay Dutt’s real-life friends.  His portrayal of an army officer in *Uri: The Surgical Strike* (2019) solidified his position as a leading actor, earning him a National Film Award for Best Actor. He followed this with *Sardar Udham* (2021), a biopic for which he underwent significant physical transformation, and won a Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor.

Recent successes include *Zara Hatke Zara Bachke* (2023), a romantic comedy, and the biopic *Sam Bahadur*, as well as *Dunki*, where he had a special appearance. His highest-grossing film to date is *Chhaava* (2025), a historical action film where he played Sambhaji, requiring extensive physical training and weight gain. Beyond acting, Kaushal endorses various brands and participates in award shows. He is married to actress Katrina Kaif, their wedding in 2021 receiving considerable media attention. While initially private about his relationships, he was previously linked to actress Harleen Sethi.

title: Klaudia Kaczorowska
text:
Klaudia Kaczorowska, born on December 20, 1988, is a Polish volleyball player who competes with both the Polish women's national team and the club PGE Atom Trefl Sopot. She has enjoyed a successful career, highlighted by a bronze medal at the 2009 European Championship and multiple Polish Championship titles.

Kaczorowska’s club career includes a significant period with PGE Atom Trefl Sopot, beginning in 2012. While playing for Sopot, she achieved victory in the Polish Cup in March of 2015 and subsequently signed a contract extension with the team in May of the same year. Prior to joining Sopot, she was a key player for PTPS Farmutil Piła, where she experienced a period of considerable success. With Piła, she won the Polish Cup in 2007/2008, and secured the Polish Championship title in the same season. This success continued into the 2008/2009 season with Piła, as she helped the team win both the Polish SuperCup and another Polish Championship. 

She then moved to Bank BPS Muszynianka Fakro Muszyna for the 2010/2011 season, contributing to their winning of both the Polish Cup and the Polish Championship. Before returning to Sopot, Kaczorowska also found success with them, winning the Polish Championship in both the 2012/2013 and 2013/2014 seasons, and adding another Polish Cup victory in 2014/2015. She also participated in the CEV Cup with PGE Atom Trefl Sopot in the 2014/2015 season.

Alongside her club achievements, Kaczorowska has represented Poland on the international stage, participating in the 2009 Universiade and the CEV European Championship in the same year, where the team won bronze. She also competed in the European League in 2014 as part of the national team. 

Kaczorowska has also been recognized for individual performances.  In 2008, playing in the Polish Cup, she was named Best Server. She repeated this achievement in 2015, again being awarded Best Server in the Polish Cup.  Notably, in 2015, she also received the Most Valuable Player award for the Polish Cup, further demonstrating her impact on the game. Information regarding her current status, beyond the dates provided in the article, is not included.

title: Jemima Goldsmith
text:
Jemima Marcelle Goldsmith, known professionally as Jemima Khan, is an English television and film producer and screenwriter. Born in London in 1974, she is the daughter of financier Sir James Goldsmith and Lady Annabel Goldsmith, and comes from both aristocratic and Jewish heritage. She has numerous half-siblings alongside her two younger brothers, Zac and Ben Goldsmith. She initially studied English at the University of Bristol but left to marry Imran Khan in 1995, later completing her degree and earning a master’s degree in Middle Eastern Studies from the University of London.

Khan founded Instinct Productions in 2015, a London-based production company. Through this, she has been an executive producer on several high-profile documentary series including *The Clinton Affair*, *The Case Against Adnan Syed*, and *Impeachment*, the third season of Ryan Murphy’s *American Crime Story*.  She also produced the feature film *What’s Love Got to Do with It?*, a romantic comedy which garnered several nominations and awards.  She has also worked on documentaries like *We Steal Secrets: The Story of WikiLeaks* and *As Far As They Can Run*. A planned TV series about the Rothschild banking dynasty, slated for production with Julian Fellowes, remains unproduced as of 2025.

Beyond production, Goldsmith has a significant background in journalism. She has contributed to numerous publications including *The Independent*, *The Sunday Times*, *Vanity Fair* (as European editor-at-large), and *The New Statesman*, which she guest-edited in 2011, receiving praise for the issue’s focus on freedom of speech. 

Goldsmith is also known for her philanthropic work. She launched a fashion label in 1998 employing Pakistani women and donating profits to her then-husband’s cancer hospital. She has been a UNICEF UK Ambassador since 2001, undertaking field work in multiple countries and supporting various campaigns. She also supports charities focused on Palestinian refugees and sustainable agriculture. 

Goldsmith’s marriage to Imran Khan, who later became Prime Minister of Pakistan, was a significant period in her life. Following the marriage, she converted to Islam and lived in Lahore, learning Urdu and adopting Pakistani customs. During this time, her Jewish heritage was exploited by Khan’s political opponents. The couple divorced in 2004, citing difficulties adapting to the demands of Pakistani political life. They have two sons together. 

Throughout her life, Goldsmith has been a vocal activist, campaigning against wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, advocating for freedom of information, and supporting Julian Assange. More recently, she has spoken out against antisemitism and Islamophobia and criticized the Pakistani government’s treatment of her sons in relation to her ex-husband. She has also been the subject of media scrutiny regarding her personal relationships, including those with Hugh Grant and Russell Brand.

title: Muhammad Alhamid
text:
Muhammad Alhamid, born in Makassar on September 17, 1971, is an Indonesian professor, academic, civil servant, and figure in electoral oversight. He comes from an Arab Indonesian family of the Ba’Alawi sada clan, the son of Sayyid Alhamid and Syarifah Aisyah Sadiq Alaydrus, and is married to Lubena Umar Alhaddad with whom he has five children: Fatimah Zahra, Jakfar Sodiq, Khadijah, Aisyah, and Umar Muchdar.

His educational background began in Makassar, completing elementary school in 1984, junior high in 1987, and high school in 1990. He then attended Hasanuddin University, earning a Sarjana Ilmu Pemerintahan (Bachelor of Science in Government) in 1994 and a Master of Science degree in 1999 from the same institution. He later pursued and completed his doctoral studies at Airlangga University in 2007, focusing his dissertation on leadership and innovation adoption within a South Sulawesi farming community. 

Alhamid’s academic career includes positions at Hasanuddin University, where he served as secretary of the Political Science Department from 2008 to 2010, and then as its chairman from 2010 to 2012. In 2015, he was confirmed as a professor in Sociology. He has also lectured at the University of West Sulawesi since 2008 and the Makassar Institute of Public Administration since 2010, teaching courses in Indonesian Political Systems, Political Geography, and National Unity and Political Development. He is a prolific publisher, with numerous journal articles covering topics from election accountability and Islamic perspectives on gender to the roles of Nahdlatul Ulama and Muhammadiyah in Indonesian political culture. He also authored a book in 2018 titled *Eksistensi DKPP RI dalam Mengawal Demokrasi dan Pemilu Bermartabat* (The Existence of the DKPP RI in Escorting Dignified Democracy and Elections).

His involvement in election oversight began in 2009 as chairman of the South Sulawesi Province Election Supervisory Committee. He was then appointed a commissioner of the Election Supervisory Board of the Republic of Indonesia (Bawaslu RI) in 2012, subsequently serving as its chairman from 2012 to 2017. Following his tenure at Bawaslu, he was appointed as a member of the Election Organization Ethics Council of the Republic of Indonesia (DKPP RI) in 2017 by President Joko Widodo, a position he held until 2022. 

Alhamid has received recognition for his service, including the Satyalancana Karya Satya award for 10 years of civil service in 2012 and the 1st Class of Star of the Defenders of Democracy award in 2015, presented by President Joko Widodo. This latter award acknowledged his contributions as Chairman of Bawaslu during the 70th anniversary of Indonesian independence.

title: Akbar Hossain
text:
Akbar Hossain, born on January 18, 1941, in Kashari Patty, Comilla District, was a prominent Bangladeshi politician and a decorated military officer. He served multiple terms as a government minister, holding portfolios including Shipping, Environment and Forests, and Petroleum and Mineral Resources, and was a long-standing figure within the Bangladesh National Party (BNP).

Hossain began his career in the military, joining the Kakul Military Academy in Pakistan in May 1966. He was commissioned into the 31 Baluch Regiment and simultaneously pursued a bachelor’s degree at the University of Dhaka, which he completed in 1969. He actively participated in the Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971, initially serving under Khaled Musharraf and later with Ziaur Rahman’s Z Force. His bravery and contributions during the war earned him the prestigious ‘Bir Protik’ award for gallantry. He voluntarily retired from the Bangladesh Army in December 1973, having reached the rank of lieutenant colonel.

Transitioning to politics, Hossain became involved in the formation of the United People’s Party (UPP) in January 1974 and rose to the position of its vice-president. He later left the UPP when it merged with the Jatiyatabadi Front, and became a founding member of the Bangladesh National Party (BNP). Within the BNP, he held several key positions, starting as special secretary, progressing to joint secretary general, and ultimately serving as one of the party’s vice-presidents until his death. 

His political career included a significant period of ministerial service. He first entered the government in 1978 as Minister for Petroleum and Mineral Resources under President Ziaur Rahman. He was first elected to the Bangladesh Parliament in 1979, representing the Comilla 8th constituency, and successfully defended this seat in four subsequent elections. During the period of military rule under General Hossain Mohammad Ershad, Hossain faced political opposition and was imprisoned five times. 

Following the end of the military dictatorship and the election of Khaleda Zia as Prime Minister, Akbar Hossain was appointed Minister for the Environment and Forests in October 1993. He again held a ministerial position after the BNP’s victory in the 8th Jatiyo Sangshad elections in October 2001, becoming Minister for Shipping in Khaleda Zia’s third term as Prime Minister. Akbar Hossain died in Dhaka on June 25, 2006, as a result of a heart attack.

title: Coco Chanel
text:
Gabrielle Bonheur “Coco” Chanel, born in 1883, was a French fashion designer and businesswoman who revolutionized feminine style in the post-World War I era. She is the only fashion designer to be named on *Time* magazine’s list of the 100 most influential people of the 20th century, and her influence extended beyond clothing to include jewelry, handbags, and fragrance, most famously Chanel No. 5 and the iconic interlocking-CC monogram. Chanel’s couture house closed in 1939 with the outbreak of World War II, but she remained in France during the German occupation, a period marked by controversial collaboration with the occupiers and the Vichy regime. Documents later revealed her direct involvement with Nazi intelligence, including a plan to act as a mediator between the Allies and Germany. She was questioned after the war due to her relationship with German diplomat Hans Günther von Dincklage, but was not charged, reportedly due to the intervention of Winston Churchill.  She eventually returned to Paris in 1954 to revive her fashion house.

Chanel’s early life was marked by hardship. Born to a laundrywoman and an itinerant vendor, she spent her early years in poverty, and her birth was initially registered incorrectly as “Chasnel.”  After her mother's death when she was eleven, she and her siblings were sent to the Aubazine convent, where she learned to sew.  She later worked as a seamstress and cabaret singer, acquiring the nickname “Coco” during her performances, though accounts of its origin vary. She began designing hats as a hobby while living with Étienne Balsan, a wealthy French officer, who provided her with financial support and access to a privileged social circle. 

Her relationship with Arthur ‘Boy’ Capel, another wealthy man, proved even more pivotal. Capel financed her first shops and his style influenced her designs. The design of Chanel No. 5’s bottle is believed to be inspired by items he possessed. Their nine-year affair ended with his death in 1919, an event that deeply affected Chanel.  She opened boutiques in Deauville in 1913 and Biarritz in 1915, introducing casual clothing made from previously unconventional materials like jersey.  These ventures proved successful, and in 1919, she established her couture house at 31 rue Cambon in Paris.

Throughout her career, Chanel cultivated relationships with prominent figures in the arts and aristocracy. She supported the Ballets Russes, financially backing productions and designing costumes. She also formed a close friendship with Misia Sert and had a brief affair with Igor Stravinsky.  Her association with Vera Bate Lombardi led to connections with British aristocracy, including an extended affair with the Duke of Westminster, who showered her with gifts and further solidified her social standing.  However, the Duke’s antisemitism seemingly reinforced existing prejudices within Chanel. Later in life, Chanel struggled with morphine addiction and was known for her sharp wit and sometimes destructive personality. She spent decades attempting to regain full control of her perfume business, Parfums Chanel, which she’d initially licensed to the Wertheimer brothers.

title: Tom Buk-Swienty
text:
Tom Buk-Swienty, born on July 19, 1966, in Eutin, is a Danish historian, journalist, and author who has become particularly known for his extensive research and writing on the Second Schleswig War. He grew up in Sønderborg, Denmark, and pursued higher education at both the University of Copenhagen and the University of California, earning degrees in history and American Studies. 

Buk-Swienty began his professional life combining journalism and academia. From 1994 to 2005, he worked as the American correspondent for the Danish periodical *Weekendavisen*. Simultaneously, he lectured at the University of Southern Denmark in Odense, a position he held until 2010. He now works as an independent author but maintains a connection to the University of Southern Denmark as an adjunct professor in history, starting in 2014.

His early writing focused on American subjects, stemming from his time living and studying in the United States. This resulted in books like *Amerika Maxima* (2002), a travel narrative, and *Den ideelle amerikaner* (2005), a biography of Jacob A. Riis. He continued to produce works relating to America, including *Det sidste hus på prærien* (2006). Upon returning to Denmark, Buk-Swienty shifted his focus to the 1864 Second Schleswig War, a significant conflict in Danish history. 

This interest culminated in a two-volume work on the war, the first volume, *Slagtebænk Dybbøl* (2008), receiving considerable acclaim and several awards. The success of the first book led to the publication of the second volume two years later, *Dommedag Als* (2010).  He also collaborated with Søren Mørch on *Købmændenes historie* (2007) and edited Jacob A. Riis’s diaries, *Ren kjærlighed kan jo aldrig dø* (2007).

Beyond the Schleswig War, Buk-Swienty has also turned his attention to biography. He authored a two-volume biography of Wilhelm Dinesen, the father of Karen Blixen. The first volume, *Kaptajn Dinesen - Ild og blod* (2013), and the second, *Kaptajn Dinesen - Til døden os skiller* (2014), explore the life of this complex figure.  

Buk-Swienty’s work has reached an international audience. *The Other Half: The Life of Jacob Riis and the World of Immigrant America* is an English translation of his work on Riis, published by W. W. Norton & Company in 2008.  Similarly, *1864: The Forgotten War that Shaped Modern Europe*, a translation of his work on the Second Schleswig War, was published by Profile Books in 2014. He also published *Det Ensomme Hjerte* in 2016. 

Throughout his career, Buk-Swienty's work has been recognized with numerous accolades, including “Årets historiske bog” (Historical Book of the Year) in 2008 for *Slagtebænk Dybbøl*, “Årets faglitterære pris” (Non-Fiction Book of the Year) in 2009, the Søren Gyldendal Prize in 2010, and the Læsernes Bogpris (Readers’ Book Prize) in 2011.

title: Abdelhamid Shabana
text:
Abdelhamid Shabana, born on October 2, 1985, is an Egyptian footballer who, as of the information available in April 2014, is without a club team, functioning as a free agent. He is described as an attacking midfielder with a dynamic playing style, possessing the versatility to also feature as a striker or winger. Shabana has gained recognition within Egyptian football for scoring notable goals against some of the country’s most prominent clubs, specifically naming Zamalek, Al-Ahly, and Ismaily as teams he has impacted with his goals.

Shabana’s involvement with Egyptian national teams extends to the youth levels. He was a consistent player for both the Egypt U20 and Egypt U23 squads.  His contributions included participation in qualifying matches for the African Games, indicating his role in attempting to secure national team advancement in this competition. Furthermore, he was part of the team that achieved success in the Qatar U23 Cup, winning the tournament.

Throughout his career, Shabana has achieved success at the club level, earning championship titles with two different teams. He was a member of the Al-Ahly team that won the Egyptian Premier League title during the 2010-2011 season. Later in his career, while playing for Churchill Brothers, he contributed to their victory in the 2014 Federation Cup. 

The information provided gives a snapshot of Shabana’s career as it stood on April 29, 2014. It highlights his position as a versatile attacking player who has demonstrably contributed to success for both club and country, particularly at the youth international level and with two established clubs in Egypt and India. However, the concluding note of being a free agent suggests that his career trajectory was ongoing at the time this information was recorded.

title: Enamul Haque (engineer)
text:
Enamul Haque was born on October 21, 1969, and is a politician affiliated with the Bangladesh Awami League. He served as a member of the Jatiya Sangsad, representing the Rajshahi-4 constituency for three consecutive terms, beginning in 2008 and concluding in 2024. His educational background includes an undergraduate degree in engineering, as well as the completion of an MBA program. 

Haque initially won his seat in the Jatiya Sangsad in the 2008 election as a candidate for the Bangladesh Awami League, and successfully defended that seat in the election held on January 5, 2014, again running under the Awami League banner. However, his political career has been marked by several controversies and accusations.

In September 2014, the Bangladesh Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) suggested that formal corruption charges be filed against him, relating to activities involving his company, Ena Enterprise. This recommendation signaled the beginning of scrutiny regarding his business dealings and potential financial misconduct. Later, in January 2017, Haque publicly criticized Iqbal Sobhan Chowdhury, the editor of *The Daily Observer*, following the publication of a newspaper report that alleged his involvement in the drug trade. He took issue with the report’s claims and responded with a public rebuke of the editor.

Internal party disputes also surfaced in September 2017 when local leaders of the Awami League in the Rajshahi region accused Haque of contributing to divisions within the party and instigating internal conflicts. These accusations suggest that his actions were perceived as disruptive to party unity.

A more serious and personal accusation arose in June 2020, when Ayesha Akter Liza, a woman estimated to be between 35 and 36 years old, accused Haque of deception and of having compelled her to undergo an abortion. Liza claimed that they had entered into a marriage on April 30, 2013, which was officially registered on May 11, 2018.  Haque acknowledged the marriage but stated that it had ended in divorce on April 23, 2020, presenting a differing account of the relationship’s status. 

Most recently, in September 2024, the ACC announced it would launch a full investigation into new allegations of corruption against Haque. These latest accusations center around claims of money laundering, irregularities in the implementation of development projects, and the illegal accumulation of wealth. This renewed investigation indicates that concerns regarding his financial conduct continue to persist, even after his term in the Jatiya Sangsad concluded.

title: Roxana Miranda
text:
Roxana del Pilar Miranda Meneses, born on April 24, 1967, is a Chilean activist and politician best known for her candidacy in the 2013 Chilean presidential election. She represented the Partido Igualdad, or Equality Party, in that race. Miranda was born in Buin to Francisco Miranda Araya, a municipal worker, and Orfilia de las Mercedes Meneses Roa, a seamstress. Her father passed away when she was six years old. She completed her secondary education at the Liceo Comercial de San Bernardo, where she was also an active student leader, holding a position on the student council.

Miranda’s involvement in political and social movements began with her work with the Asociación de Deudores Habitacionales, known as ANDHA Chile, an association of people with housing debt. She rose to become a national leader within the organization, which later rebranded as «ANDHA Chile a Luchar Democrático». Before running for president, Miranda pursued elected office at the local level. In 2008, she ran as an independent candidate for mayor of San Bernardo, receiving 3,558 votes, representing 4.24% of the total. She attempted to win the same position again in 2012, but garnered fewer votes, securing only 1,831, or 2.77% of the electorate. In 2009, she ran for a deputy seat in District No. 30, ultimately finishing seventh with 4,332 votes, which amounted to 2.85% of the votes cast.

Later, Miranda became the president of the Partido Igualdad and was officially proclaimed as the party's presidential candidate on January 20, 2013. During the campaign leading up to the election, there were discussions about potentially unifying her candidacy with that of Marcel Claude. However, Miranda publicly stated she would not withdraw from the race. On May 29, 2013, she successfully submitted the necessary signatures to the Electoral Service of Chile, formally validating both the Partido Igualdad and her presidential bid.

Miranda presented her detailed government program on November 5, 2013, making her the last presidential candidate to do so. The 125-page program focused on four key areas of social reform, which she described as a “plebeian program” aimed at transforming Chile. These areas were titled “Superación del capitalismo” (Overcoming capitalism), “Que el pueblo mande” (Let the people rule), “Recuperación de nuestros derechos” (recovering our rights), and “El buen vivir” (Good living). Ultimately, Miranda was unsuccessful in the presidential election. She is married to Iván Luis Vargas García, and the couple have four children.

title: Mattias Asper
text:
Nils Mattias Joacim Asper, born on March 20, 1974, is a Swedish football manager and former goalkeeper. He currently manages Kristianstad FC, a club in the Swedish Division 2. Asper began his professional playing career with Mjällby AIF during the mid-1990s, and later played in Spain, Turkey, and Norway before returning to Mjällby in 2008. He also represented the Sweden national team, earning three caps between 1999 and 2002, and was part of the squad for UEFA Euro 2000, though he didn’t play in the tournament itself.

Asper was a key player for Mjällby AIF for four seasons before joining AIK in 1998. Initially, Lee Baxter was the first-choice goalkeeper for AIK, but after a poor start to the season with only one win in seven games, Asper was brought in on June 8th against Östers IF. This change proved pivotal, as AIK went undefeated for the remainder of the season and ultimately won the Allsvenskan championship. In 1999, AIK qualified for the Champions League, reaching the group stage, and Asper set a new Allsvenskan record by maintaining a clean sheet for 797 consecutive minutes.

His strong performances with AIK attracted attention from Real Sociedad in Spain, leading to a transfer just before the 2000-01 season. However, his time in Spain was unsuccessful. He subsequently returned to Sweden, initially on loan to Beşiktaş J.K. in Turkey, before joining Malmö FF in 2002. With Malmö FF, he achieved another Allsvenskan title in 2004. 

Asper made his debut for the Swedish national team on November 27, 1999, in a friendly match against South Africa, coming on as a substitute for Magnus Kihlstedt. He earned a second cap in a friendly against Austria in March 2000. Despite being selected for the UEFA Euro 2000 squad, he remained third-choice goalkeeper behind Magnus Hedman and Magnus Kihlstedt. His final international appearance came in a friendly against Russia in August 2002.

Throughout his career, Asper achieved significant honours, including winning the Allsvenskan and Svenska Cupen with AIK in 1998 and 1999 respectively, and the Allsvenskan again with Malmö FF in 2004. He was also recognized individually, winning the Swedish Goalkeeper of the Year award in both 1998 and 1999. He announced his retirement from professional football on November 26, 2014.

title: Jefferson Thomas
text:
Jefferson Thomas was born in Little Rock, Arkansas, in 1942, the youngest of seven children and named after President Thomas Jefferson. He initially attended the segregated Horace Mann High School, where he participated in track and field. In 1957, as a sophomore, he volunteered to be one of the first African-American students to integrate Little Rock Central High School, becoming part of the group known as the Little Rock Nine.

The initial attempts to enter the school on September 4, 1957, were blocked by the Arkansas National Guard, acting under the governor’s orders, and a hostile crowd of approximately 400 people. A larger mob, around 1000 strong, again prevented their entry on September 23rd. President Dwight D. Eisenhower intervened, federalizing the National Guard and deploying federal troops to ensure the students' safety and allow them access to the school. Federal forces remained at Central High for the duration of the school year.

Despite enduring harassment, Thomas successfully graduated from Little Rock Central High School in 1960 and subsequently enrolled at Wayne State University in Detroit. He later moved to Los Angeles, California, in 1961, where he became involved in civil rights activism, serving as Treasurer of the NAACP Youth Council and State President of the Progressive Baptist Youth Convention. He continued his education at Los Angeles State College, becoming President of the Associated Engineers while earning a bachelor’s degree in Business Administration. Thomas also served in the U.S. Army during the Vietnam War as an infantryman in the 9th Infantry Division. 

He later narrated the 1964 United States Information Agency film *Nine from Little Rock*, reflecting on the experience and stating that challenges could lead to improvement. The film, intended to counter negative perceptions of American racial issues during the Cold War, was widely acclaimed and distributed internationally. 

Thomas spent his later years in Columbus, Ohio, with his wife, Mary, and dedicated himself to community service, mentoring youth through the Village to Child Program. He received an Honorary Doctor of Humane Letters from Ohio Dominican University in 2001. He was a frequent speaker across the country, sharing his experiences, and was recognized with numerous awards including the Congressional Gold Medal, presented to the Little Rock Nine by President Bill Clinton in 1999, and the NAACP's Spingarn Award, also in 1999. The state of Arkansas honored the Little Rock Nine with statues on the Capitol grounds in 2005. He retired in 2004 after 27 years as a civil servant with the Defense Finance and Accounting Service. Jefferson Thomas passed away in 2010 from pancreatic cancer, becoming the first member of the Little Rock Nine to die. He was interred in Forest Lawn Memorial Park in Glendale, California.

title: G. Fowler Stewart
text:
George Fowler Stewart was born in 1861, the youngest son of Charles Stewart, a manufacturer from Kirkcaldy, Scotland. He received his education at a college in Edinburgh before beginning his career with D. & J. Fowler, a company founded by his uncles, David, James, and George Fowler. He initially worked in the firm’s London office starting in 1879. 

In 1881, Stewart was dispatched to Adelaide, South Australia, to gain experience in the business operations there. He proved capable, and in 1887, he was entrusted with managing the branch of D & J Fowler in Fremantle, Western Australia. Following several years of international travel, he returned to Adelaide in 1889 and married Laura Hill, the youngest daughter of William Hill, in 1890. Laura was also the granddaughter of John Dunn of Mount Barker.

Stewart’s role within D & J Fowler evolved when the company transitioned into a public entity, leading to his appointment as a Director based in London. He eventually returned to Adelaide in 1901 and continued working with the company until his retirement in 1914. He passed away unexpectedly at his home on January 3, 1917, due to a heart attack.

Beyond his business pursuits, Stewart was deeply involved in public life in South Australia. He played a significant role in the formation of the Australian Dried Fruit Association, serving as its first secretary. He was also a founding member of the Federation League, actively advocating for the Federation of Australia. Furthermore, he held leadership positions within various political organizations, including chairing the joint council of the Australasian National League and Farmers' and Producers' Political Union, and later becoming president of the Torrens electoral committee and the Glenelg branch of the Liberal Union, as well as serving on the Liberal Union’s State executive. 

Stewart also participated in cultural and community organizations. He was an active member of the South Australian Caledonian Society and served as its Chief in 1902. He was a member of the Glenelg Town Council in 1905 and contributed to the South Australian Literary Societies' Union, serving as its president in 1906 and previously as treasurer of its associated Union Parliament. 

George and Laura Stewart had three children: Helen Fowler Stewart, born in 1891, who later married Valentine Zerbini Alderman; William Hill Dunn Stewart, born in 1895; and Charles Gordon Stewart, born in 1903, who married Mary Frewin Hancock and lived in Langkoop, Victoria. The family resided at “Waldo” in Glenelg, and later moved to “Waldo” in Kensington Gardens.

title: Sérgio Moraes
text:
Sérgio Moraes, born July 23, 1982, is a Brazilian former mixed martial artist who competed in the welterweight and middleweight divisions, notably within the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). Known as “O Orgulho da Cohab” – “The Pride of Cohab” – he hails from that area of Brazil. Before transitioning to MMA, Moraes was a highly accomplished Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu practitioner, earning four World Championships, with a particularly celebrated victory over Kron Gracie in 2008. He is affiliated with the Alliance Jiu-Jitsu Team and currently works as a Jiu-Jitsu instructor, at Evolução Thai in Curitiba, Brazil and Reza Martial Arts Center in Bahrain.

Moraes began his professional MMA career in Brazil in October 2006, quickly building a record of six wins and one loss, largely defined by submission victories. He made his US debut in 2009 with Bellator Fighting Championships, winning his first fight via triangle choke. In 2012, he appeared on *The Ultimate Fighter: Brazil*, winning his opening fight against Thiago Rela via heel hook and advancing to the house. He then defeated Delson Heleno but was knocked out by Daniel Sarafian in the semi-finals.

This led to a UFC contract and a fight against Cezar Ferreira in June 2012, stepping in as a replacement for Sarafian. He lost this bout by unanimous decision.  His UFC career saw a mix of wins and losses. He secured victories over Renée Forte, Neil Magny (earning a Submission of the Night bonus for a triangle choke), and Mickaël Lebout, as well as Zak Ottow and Davi Ramos. However, he faced defeats against opponents including Ferreira, Sarafian, Anthony Rocco Martin, and Warlley Alves. A fight with Kamaru Usman saw two attempts, first ending in a draw and the second in a knockout loss for Moraes. 

Throughout his UFC tenure, numerous scheduled fights were altered due to injuries of either himself or his opponents.  In 2017, he signed a new six-fight contract with the UFC, but was eventually released following a knockout loss to James Krause in November 2019. Following his release, Moraes signed with Taura MMA in 2020, but lost his debut fight against Jared Revel by unanimous decision.  He was recognized by UFC.com and Fight Matrix for his performances, receiving a ranking for Submission of the Year in 2013 and being named Comeback Fighter of the Year in 2015.

title: Diego Godín
text:
Diego Godín, born in 1986 in Rosario, Uruguay, was a professional footballer renowned as one of the best defenders of his generation. He began his career at Cerro before moving to Nacional, where his maturity quickly led to a captaincy. In 2007, he transferred to Villarreal in Spain, establishing himself as a key player and participating in their most successful La Liga season, finishing second. 

Godín then joined Atlético Madrid in 2010, where he spent nine years, becoming a club icon. He won eight titles with Atlético, including the La Liga championship in 2014, scoring a crucial equalizing goal against Barcelona on the final matchday to secure the victory. He also reached two Champions League finals with the club, scoring in the 2014 final against Real Madrid, though they ultimately lost. He rejected a move to Manchester City in 2015 and became the foreign player with the most appearances for Atlético, earning Ballon d'Or nominations in 2016 and 2018.

Following his time in Madrid, Godín played for Inter Milan, Cagliari, Atlético Mineiro, and Vélez Sarsfield before retiring in 2023, briefly coming out of retirement in 2024 to play for Uruguayan amateurs Porongos. At Inter Milan, he won the Europa League runner-up medal in 2020, and with Atlético Mineiro, he won the Supercopa do Brasil and Campeonato Mineiro in 2022.

Internationally, Godín is Uruguay’s all-time most-capped player, earning 161 appearances. He represented his country at four World Cups and six Copa América tournaments, winning the Copa América in 2011. He captained Uruguay in several major tournaments, including the 2014 World Cup, where he scored the winning goal against Italy.

Despite lacking exceptional pace, Godín was praised for his intelligence, leadership, positioning, aerial ability, and composure. He was known for his ability to read the game, anticipate plays, and organize his defense. He was also capable of contributing in attack with his technique and ability to play the ball out from the back. 

Beyond football, Godín is married to the daughter of a former Uruguayan international and is close friends with Antoine Griezmann, with whom he played at Atlético Madrid. He is also Griezmann's daughter's godfather. Throughout his career, Godín accumulated numerous individual accolades, including La Liga Player of the Month awards, selections to various Teams of the Season, and recognition as one of the world's best defenders.

title: Trevor Noah
text:
Trevor Noah, born in Johannesburg, South Africa on February 20, 1984, is a multi-talented entertainer working as a comedian, writer, producer, political commentator, actor, and television host. He is best known as the former host of *The Daily Show* on Comedy Central, a position he held from 2015 to 2022, earning him two Primetime Emmy Awards and recognition as a prominent figure in New York media and globally.

Noah’s early life was shaped by the apartheid laws in South Africa. His father is Swiss-German and his mother, Patricia, is Xhosa. Because of apartheid, his parents’ relationship was illegal at the time of his birth, and he was classified as “Coloured.” He was raised by his mother and grandmother in Soweto. He was educated at Maryvale College and grew up in a household that blended Christian beliefs with exposure to Jewish traditions through his mother’s conversion.

He began his career in South Africa in 2008, taking on various hosting roles with the South African Broadcasting Corporation and appearing as a contestant on *Strictly Come Dancing*. He also created and hosted his own late-night talk show, *Tonight with Trevor Noah*, from 2010 to 2011. His breakthrough came in 2014 when he became a Senior International Correspondent for *The Daily Show*, ultimately leading to his succession of Jon Stewart as host in 2015.

Beyond television, Noah is a published author, releasing his autobiographical comedy book *Born a Crime* in 2016, which became a New York Times Bestseller. He has also been a frequent host of major events, including the Grammy Awards from 2021-2025 and the 2022 White House Correspondents Dinner.

Throughout his career, Noah’s comedy often draws from his unique upbringing and observations on race and culture. He gained recognition performing at comedy clubs in South Africa and later in the United States, appearing on shows like *The Tonight Show* and *Late Show with David Letterman*. He has faced some controversy over past jokes that were deemed insensitive. 

Following his departure from *The Daily Show* in December 2022, Noah has continued to pursue various projects, including hosting the Grammy Awards, launching a Spotify podcast titled *What Now? with Trevor Noah*, and acting in films. He has cited comedians like Richard Pryor, Eddie Murphy, Chris Rock, and Dave Chappelle as major influences, as well as his predecessor, Jon Stewart, whom he views as a mentor. He currently resides in New York City and speaks multiple languages. His mother’s resilience, marked by surviving a shooting incident by her former husband, is a significant theme in his life and work.

title: Abdullahi Mohammad Ahmad Hassan
text:
Abdullahi Mohammad Ahmad Hassan was born in Sudan in January 1928, in Barah, North Kurdufan, though his family later settled in Al-Ubayyid. He received an education beginning with Koranic school before attending Hantoub Secondary School and then graduating from the Faculty of Arts at the University College of Khartoum in 1955. He initially worked as a history teacher in Tonj and later at Khour Taqatt Secondary School, but resigned in 1958 to pursue business and journalism in Khartoum.

Early in his life, Abdullahi became involved in Sudanese politics, opposing the military government of General Aboud after the 1958 coup. He was a founding member of the Islamic Liberation Movement in 1949, joining while a student and playing a key role in recruiting future prominent figures like Hassan Al-Turabi. This movement aimed to liberate Sudan from British occupation and establish an Islamic state. He was involved in student politics at the University of Khartoum, helping the Islamic Liberation Movement gain control of the student union. 

Throughout the following decades, Abdullahi navigated a turbulent political landscape. He was elected as a Member of Parliament twice during the second Sudanese democracy, and a third time following elections in 1986. He actively participated in opposition movements following coups in 1958 and 1969, experiencing exile in Saudi Arabia before relocating to the United Kingdom. Following a national reconciliation in 1979, he returned to Sudan and was appointed to oversee the affairs of the Ansar. 

Abdullahi held several ministerial positions. He served as Minister of Culture and Information, then Minister of Foreign Trade, and later as Councilor and Advisor to the Prime Minister under Sadiq al-Mahdi. After a coup in 1989, he was initially arrested but later surprisingly appointed by Omar Al-Bashir as Minister of Education, Culture and Information, and eventually as Sudan’s ambassador to Italy, Spain, Greece and San Marino. However, his disagreements with the government led to his recall from his ambassadorial post in 1995. He spent much of his later life between Sudan and the United Kingdom, continuing to work as a political observer, analyst, lecturer, author and columnist. Abdullahi Mohammad Ahmad Hassan died in the United Kingdom on 22 June 2022, at the age of 94.

title: Lunay (singer)
text:
Jefnier Osorio Moreno, professionally known as Lunay, is a Puerto Rican singer and songwriter born on October 4, 2000. He gained prominence in the Latin urban music scene through a series of successful songs including “Soltera”, “No Te Quieren Conmigo”, “La Cama”, “A Solas”, and “Aventura”. His debut studio album, *Épico*, was released on October 25, 2019.

Before focusing on music, Lunay’s childhood passions were playing the drums and soccer. It was through soccer that he discovered his interest in a music career, inspired by the success of other Latin American urban artists. He began recording freestyle raps around the age of twelve, posting them to Facebook where several clips gained viral attention, particularly amongst his soccer teammates. These videos eventually caught the eye of producers Chris Jedi and Gaby Music. 

Lunay began uploading musical projects to SoundCloud in 2017 under his given name, Jefnier. His track "Aparentas" garnered significant attention on the platform, leading to contact from Chris Jedi and Gaby Music, who offered him a record deal. Upon signing, he adopted the stage name Lunay in May 2018. He quickly released singles like “Si Te Vas Conmigo” and “Dejame Saber,” followed by collaborations with Lyanno on “A Solas” and Amarion on “Como La Primera Vez.” 

Early collaborations proved successful, notably “Luz Apaga” featuring Ozuna, Rauw Alejandro, and Lyanno, which amassed millions of views on YouTube. Later in 2018, a remix of “A Solas” featuring Anuel AA, Brytiago, and Alex Rose trended on YouTube for several days. His single “Soltera,” released in March 2019, quickly achieved over five million views in just five days and was later remixed with Daddy Yankee and Bad Bunny. In 2020, he collaborated with American rapper Lil Mosey on the single “Top Gone”, which appeared on the deluxe edition of Lil Mosey’s album *Certified Hitmaker*.

Lunay distinguishes his musical style by intentionally avoiding themes of violence or the degradation of women. He has stated that being involved in urban music doesn’t necessitate promoting negativity, and that his work aligns with his personal faith. In 2019, he was recognized with the “artist on the rise” award at the Premios Juventud. His discography includes studio albums, EPs, numerous singles as a lead artist, and appearances as a featured artist on other songs.

title: Adel Emam
text:
Adel Emam, born on May 17, 1940, is a highly celebrated Egyptian actor with a career spanning over 150 films, plays, and television series. Considered a leading figure of the second generation of comedic artists in the Arab world, he is known for his versatility, moving between comedy, social commentary, and drama. While initially appearing in supporting roles alongside stars like Salah Zulfikar in films such as *My Wife, the Director General* and *My Wife's Goblin*, he rose to prominence in the 1960s and became a dominant force in Egyptian and Arab cinema. He holds a bachelor's degree in Agriculture from Cairo University, where he began his acting journey in university theatre alongside future notables like Salah El-Saadany.

Emam’s contributions to the film industry are marked by his willingness to tackle social and political issues, earning him a cult following and establishing him as an influential public figure in the 1980s and 90s. He is viewed as a cultural icon in modern Egypt, receiving numerous accolades including Lifetime Achievement Awards. In 2000, he was appointed a Goodwill Ambassador for UNHCR by the United Nations. 

Born into a modest family in Cairo, with roots in the Dakahlia Governorate, Emam experienced a mobile childhood, moving between several districts. His father, a police officer, passed away in 1997 after a long battle with Alzheimer’s. He is married to Hala El-Shalaqani, a union that began in the mid-1960s despite initial resistance from her family due to his profession. They have three children: Ramy, a director; Sarah; and Mohamed, an actor who appeared in *The Yacoubian Building*. He now enjoys spending time with his eight grandchildren and cultivating his passion for gardening, a reflection of his agricultural background. While specific figures remain unconfirmed, reports suggest a net worth in the millions of dollars.

Emam’s career began in the early 1960s with small roles, developing his skills in theatre with productions like *Ana Wa Howa Wa Heya*. He quickly gained recognition with roles in films such as *My Wife's Dignity* and *Virgo*, and his talent was recognized by writer Mahmud Sadani. The 1970s saw him rise to fame with films like *Bahibek Ya Helwa* and *Madraset El Moshaghbeen*, solidifying his comedic talent. The 1980s marked a period of diverse roles, including the action-oriented *The Suspect*, and collaborations with Soad Hosny, consistently earning high box office numbers. His 1990s were considered his peak, with critically acclaimed and commercially successful films like *Terrorism and Kebab*, *Al-La'ib Ma'a Al-Kibar*, and *The Terrorist*, often characterized by social and political satire. Throughout his career, Emam maintained a prolific output, frequently appearing in multiple films per year alongside his stage work.

title: Rosé (singer)
text:
Rosé, born Roseanne Park on February 11, 1997, is a New Zealand and South Korean singer and songwriter. She was born in Auckland, New Zealand, and spent her childhood in Melbourne, Australia before moving to Seoul, South Korea in 2012. After successfully auditioning for YG Entertainment in Sydney, she trained for four years and ultimately debuted as a member of the girl group Blackpink in August 2016. 

Before her official debut, Rosé was featured on a song by labelmate G-Dragon in 2012, though her contribution wasn’t publicly credited at the time. As a member of Blackpink, she achieved significant success, including a global partnership with Interscope Records in 2018. Rosé also appeared on Korean broadcast programs, showcasing her vocal ability and gaining positive reception from audiences. 

In March 2021, Rosé embarked on her solo career with the release of her debut single album, *R*. This album broke records, achieving the highest first-week sales for a Korean female soloist, selling 448,089 copies. The lead single, “On the Ground,” further cemented her success, topping the Billboard Global 200 chart – a first for a Korean soloist, as well as a group member - and charting in the UK Singles Chart. She gained six Guinness World Records for this success. 

Following Blackpink's activities, Rosé signed with The Black Label and Atlantic Records in 2024. This led to the release of “Apt.” featuring Bruno Mars, which became another number-one hit on the Billboard Global 200 and topped charts in multiple countries, including Australia, marking the first time a Korean female soloist achieved this in Australia. “Apt.” also reached the top three on both the US Billboard Hot 100 and the UK Singles Chart, breaking records for Korean female soloists on both charts. Her debut studio album *Rosie*, released in December 2024, continued this success, charting highly in the US and the UK.

Throughout her career, Rosé has received awards including two MAMA Awards and the Asia Artist Award for Song of the Year. She is highly influential on social media, ranking as the second-most followed Korean individual on Instagram, and has been featured on both *Time’s* list of the 100 most influential people and *Rolling Stone’s* list of living icons from Australia and New Zealand. 

Beyond music, Rosé has established herself as a fashion icon, serving as a global ambassador for Yves Saint Laurent and Tiffany & Co., and appearing on numerous magazine covers. Her voice has been widely praised for its unique timbre, earning her the nickname "the golden voice" among fans. She has cited artists like Taeyang and Tori Kelly as musical inspirations.

title: Samir Kochhar
text:
Samir Kochhar, born on May 23, 1980, is an Indian actor and television presenter who has become a recognizable face in Indian entertainment. He is particularly well-known for his role as the host of *Extraaa Innings T20*, the pre-match show for the Indian Premier League. More recently, he has gained prominence for his acting role in the Netflix India series *Sacred Games*.

Kochhar’s career began with television, specifically with *Haath Se Haath Mila*, a Doordarshan program focused on AIDS awareness, presented in a travel show format. He co-anchored this show with Sugandha Garg. He then transitioned into film with a debut in the 2003 bilingual movie *Valentine Days*, directed by Sumeer Sabharwal. Following this, he returned to television with *Dangerous*, a talk show centered around the topic of sex, which aired on Zoom. 

His work in television continued with a role in the soap opera *Bade Acche Lagte Hain*, where he portrayed the character of Rajat Kapur. He also expanded his film credits with appearances in *Zeher* in 2005, directed by Mohit Suri, and the thriller *Jannat* in 2008, where he played a police inspector. He later reprised his role in *Jannat 3*, slated for release in 2025.

Beyond mainstream television and film, Kochhar participated in independent cinema, being a part of *Island City*, a film directed by Ruchika Oberoi which garnered positive reviews at both the Venice International Film Festival and the JIO MAMI Film Festival in Mumbai in 2015. He also has a role in *Mango Dreams*, a feature film set in India directed by American director John Unchurch. In 2016, Kochhar appeared in two commercially released films: *Housefull 3*, alongside Akshay Kumar, and *Mango Dreams*. He was also involved in *Hume Tumse Pyaar Kitna*, directed by Lalit Mohan and featuring Karanvir Bohra, which was scheduled for release in 2018.

Outside of acting and presenting, Kochhar is also involved in the Celebrity Cricket League, playing for the Mumbai Heroes team. 

On a personal note, Samir Kochhar married his longtime girlfriend Radhika on January 9, 2010. They have two children: a son named Kabir, born in April 2015, and a daughter named Sara, born in October 2017.

title: Arif Mohammad Khan
text:
Arif Mohammad Khan was born on November 18, 1951, in Bulandshahr, and is currently serving as the Governor of Bihar, a position he assumed in January 2025. Prior to this, he served as the Governor of Kerala from September 2019 to December 2024. He is a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), having joined in 2004, though his political career began much earlier.

Khan’s early political life involved student leadership; he was President of the Aligarh Muslim University Students' Union in 1972-73 and its Honorary Secretary the year before. He first entered the legislative assembly in 1977, representing the Siyana constituency, after an initial unsuccessful contest. He was subsequently elected to the Lok Sabha in 1980 and 1984 as a member of the Indian National Congress. 

A significant turning point in his career came in 1986 when he resigned from the Congress due to disagreements over the Muslim Personal Law Bill, specifically objecting to provisions allowing divorced men to avoid maintenance payments to their wives. He then joined the Janata Dal and was re-elected to the Lok Sabha in 1989, serving as Union Minister of Civil Aviation during that period.
