He later switched to the Bahujan Samaj Party, winning a Lok Sabha seat in 1998, and held ministerial responsibilities between 1984 and 1990. Despite unsuccessfully contesting the 2004 Lok Sabha election, he was later appointed Governor by the BJP. 

Khan has been a vocal advocate for reform within the Muslim community, defending the Supreme Court’s judgement in the Shah Bano case and opposing the practice of triple talaq, advocating for it to be a punishable offense. He has also expressed controversial views on religious education, suggesting a review of madrasa teachings regarding blasphemy, following the murder of Kanhaiya Lal in Udaipur. He supports the idea that the hijab is not essential to Islam, as demonstrated by his stance during the 2022 Karnataka hijab row.

Beyond politics, Khan is an author, having penned "Text and Context: Quran and Contemporary Challenges" in 2010, and continues to write on Islam and Sufism. He has also advocated for the abolishment of the All India Muslim Personal Law Board. 

During his time as Governor of Kerala, he faced controversy surrounding the appointment of vice-chancellors with connections to the SFI/CPIM, and his departure was marked by a lack of official farewell from the state government. He was also implicated in the Jain Hawala case, being accused of receiving funds as a minister, though he was later acquitted.

title: Billy Conigliaro
text:
William “Billy” Conigliaro was a professional baseball outfielder who played in Major League Baseball for five seasons between 1969 and 1973, appearing for the Boston Red Sox, Milwaukee Brewers, and Oakland Athletics. Born in Revere, Massachusetts in 1947, he followed in the footsteps of his older brother, Tony Conigliaro, also a major league player, with whom he briefly played as teammates on the Red Sox. Their parents, Sal and Teresa, encouraged both sons to pursue baseball.

Billy Conigliaro was a three-sport athlete at Swampscott High School, where he pitched a no-hitter in 1964 shortly after his brother debuted in the majors. He was drafted by the Red Sox in the first round of the inaugural MLB draft in 1965 and spent the next four years honing his skills in the minor leagues. He made his MLB debut in April 1969, stealing a base as a pinch runner, and quickly demonstrated offensive potential with two home runs in his first start a few days later. He finished his rookie year with a .288 batting average in 32 games.

His most productive season came in 1970, where he recorded career highs in several categories, including 108 hits, 59 runs scored, 18 home runs, and 58 RBIs across 114 games. That year, the Red Sox even shifted Carl Yastrzemski to first base to accommodate Conigliaro in the lineup. He was notably upset when his brother Tony was traded to the California Angels at the end of the season. In 1971, he hit 11 home runs and finished eighth in the American League in doubles with 26.

In October 1971, Conigliaro was traded to the Milwaukee Brewers in a ten-player deal. However, he became dissatisfied and retired mid-season in 1972. He sought reinstatement and was sold to the Oakland Athletics in 1973, appearing in both the American League Championship Series and the World Series, though he did not achieve any hits in seven at-bats. Following knee surgery, he was waived by the Athletics in 1974 and briefly attempted a comeback in 1977, ultimately declining a minor league assignment. Throughout his career, he maintained a .256 batting average with 40 home runs and 128 RBIs in 347 games. 

Beyond baseball, Conigliaro studied Shotokan karate under Kazumi Tabata, who acknowledged him in one of his books. He married Keisha in 2002 and passed away on February 10, 2021, from a heart attack at his home in Beverly, Massachusetts.

title: Nikole Hannah-Jones
text:
Nikole Hannah-Jones, born in 1976 in Waterloo, Iowa, is an American investigative journalist recognized for her reporting on civil rights in the United States. She joined *The New York Times* in 2015 and achieved significant acclaim, including a 2017 MacArthur Fellowship and the 2020 Pulitzer Prize for Commentary, both awarded for her work on *The 1619 Project*. She is currently the inaugural Knight Chair in Race and Journalism at Howard University, where she also founded the Center for Journalism and Democracy.

Hannah-Jones’s upbringing was shaped by her biracial identity – her father is African-American and her mother is of Czech and English descent – and by attending predominantly white schools through a desegregation program. She earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in history and African-American studies from the University of Notre Dame in 1998, where she publicly challenged what she perceived as racist rhetoric in the student newspaper. She later received a master's degree in journalism from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in 2003.

Her journalism career began with coverage of education at the *Raleigh News & Observer* and continued at *The Oregonian* for six years, where she covered various beats including demographics and government. She received a fellowship from the Institute for Advanced Journalism Studies in 2008-2009, allowing her to study healthcare and education in Cuba.  In 2011, she joined ProPublica, focusing on civil rights, redlining, and the enforcement of fair housing laws. At *The New York Times*, she has focused on racial segregation and discrimination in schools and housing, exposing systemic racism perpetuated by laws and institutions. She also authored *The Problem We All Live With*, a book exploring school segregation.

Hannah-Jones is most prominently known for *The 1619 Project*, launched in 2019 to commemorate the 400th anniversary of the arrival of enslaved Africans in Virginia. The project reframes American history by centering the consequences of slavery and the contributions of Black Americans.  It evolved from a special issue of *The New York Times Magazine* into a multifaceted initiative including essays, poetry, fiction, a podcast, and live events. While widely praised, *The 1619 Project* faced criticism from historians regarding some of its interpretations, specifically regarding the motivations behind the American Revolution, leading to clarifications in some articles.

A planned professorship at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill became controversial, with the university initially offering a fixed contract rather than tenure following criticism of the project. Hannah-Jones ultimately declined the position and accepted a tenured position at Howard University, accompanied by $20 million in funding for her work. 

Beyond her reporting and academic roles, Hannah-Jones co-founded the Ida B. Wells Society for Investigative Reporting in 2016, aiming to increase diversity in investigative journalism. She has received numerous awards and accolades throughout her career, recognizing her impactful work and contributions to the field. She has also faced some controversy, including apologizing for sharing a conspiracy theory about fireworks and a dispute over a story regarding Chick-fil-A.

title: Sergei Bodrov
text:
Sergei Vladimirovich Bodrov, born in Khabarovsk, Russia in 1948, is a prominent Russian film director, screenwriter, and producer. He gained recognition as one of the first directors to benefit from the increased creative freedom during the Glasnost period in the Soviet Union, allowing him to explore previously restricted topics in his films. Following the collapse of the Soviet Union, Bodrov emigrated to the United States, currently residing in Los Angeles with a ranch also in Arizona, and is married to American film consultant Carolyn Cavallaro.

Bodrov’s early life included being raised by his grandparents, with his background marked by a diverse heritage: a Buryat grandmother, a Tatar mother, and a Russian grandfather. He initially pursued engineering, studying spaceship design, but abandoned his studies after developing a gambling addiction that led to a deeply regretted act of stealing from his grandmother. This prompted him to cease gambling altogether. He then found employment as an electrician at Mosfilm, the government film studio, where he eventually transitioned into scriptwriting for comedies.

His directorial debut came in 1985 with *Sweet Juice of the Grass*, which was screened at the Locarno Film Festival. *The Non-Professionals*, released in 1987, faced censorship in the USSR due to its depiction of the Soviet-Afghan War, only being shown after changes during Perestroika allowed for the ‘de-shelving’ of banned films. This film explored the “spiritual malaise” of a generation and drew comparisons to the New Wave cinema of the 1960s. *Freedom Is Paradise* (1989), set in Kazakhstan, continued his focus on social realism and his talent for incorporating non-actors into his productions, even intervening to secure the parole of one young actor after filming. 

Bodrov achieved international acclaim with *Prisoner of the Mountains* (1996), a film about the First Chechen War which received nominations for both an Academy Award and a Golden Globe for Best Foreign Language Film. Notably, the film deliberately avoided explicit political stances, focusing instead on humanist themes and portraying compassion on both sides of the conflict. It also marked the acting debut of his son, Sergei Bodrov Jr., who tragically died in an avalanche in 2002 while filming *The Messenger*. Bodrov has directed a total of fourteen feature films, writing or co-writing the scripts for all but two. He received an International Achievement Award in Filmmaking at CinemaCon in 2008, coinciding with the U.S. release of *Mongol*, which also garnered Academy Award and Golden Globe nominations. He has won the Nika Award for Best Picture and Best Director for both *Prisoner of the Mountains* and *Mongol*.

title: Jake Tilson
text:
Jake Tilson, born in London in 1958, is a multifaceted English artist working across disciplines including graphic design, writing, and publishing. He comes from a creative family; his father is artist Joe Tilson, his mother Joslyn Tilson (née Morton), and his grandfather was Alastair Morton, who supported numerous artists through the Edinburgh Weavers business. Tilson studied painting at Chelsea School of Art (1976-1979) and continued at the Royal College of Art (1980-1983), winning a Major Travelling scholarship that allowed him to exhibit in Paris.

Throughout his career, Tilson has been involved in publishing, beginning with the establishment of The Woolley Dale Press in 1979 to produce limited edition book works and the arts magazine *Cipher*. He continued publishing with *Atlas*, a trilingual arts magazine that gained international distribution in 15 countries, eventually evolving into his second independent press, Atlas, which released his audio works and publications like *3 Found Fonts* (2003). He exhibited extensively during the 1990s, represented by the Nigel Greenwood Gallery, and his work during this period focused on collage and sculptural dioramas. 

Tilson’s professional design work includes commissions for well-known organizations such as Paul Smith, the Royal National Theatre, Haworth Tompkins, and Warehouse plc. He also embraced new technologies early on, creating the website *TheCooker* in 1994 and designing websites for institutions including the Royal Institute of International Affairs and the Royal College of Art. More recently, he contributed to the Venice Architecture Biennale in 2012 with a commission from Haworth Tompkins Architects.

Beyond his artistic and design pursuits, Tilson has also been involved in education, teaching in the Communication Design department at the Royal College of Art from 1987 to 1999. He was also an artist in residence at the Ruskin School of Drawing and Fine Art at Oxford University. He is a trustee of the Oxford Symposium on Food & Cookery and has authored *A Tale of 12 Kitchens* (2006) and numerous bookworks like *Light & Dark* (1979) and *Breakfast Special* (1989). He has also produced several audio works released via Atlas, including *City Sounds of the Everyday* (2012) and *Foundsounds* (1993). His work is held in public collections including the Tate Gallery, Chase Manhattan Bank and the BBC World Service.

title: Robert Whittaker (fighter)
text:
Robert Whittaker, born in 1990 in Auckland, New Zealand, is a professional mixed martial artist currently competing in the Middleweight division of the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC). He is a former UFC Middleweight Champion and holds the distinction of being the first Australian to win a UFC championship. As of July 2025, he is ranked #7 in the UFC middleweight division. His professional MMA career began in 2009, and he first gained prominence as a contestant and eventual winner of the welterweight tournament on the first series of *The Ultimate Fighter: The Smashes*. He later became the interim middleweight champion at UFC 213 and was elevated to undisputed champion when Georges St-Pierre relinquished the title in 2017.

Whittaker’s upbringing involved martial arts from a young age. His father, of European descent, and mother, of Samoan and Māori ancestry, enrolled him and his brother in Goju-ryu karate at age seven. After eight years and achieving a black belt, Whittaker switched to hapkido, which eventually transitioned into MMA when the gym’s focus shifted. He had also been a talented rugby league player, even reaching the development academy of the Cronulla Sharks, but ultimately chose MMA as his primary sport. Known for his sportsmanlike conduct, Whittaker avoids trash talk, preferring to focus on the athletic aspect of competition.

Early in his MMA career, Whittaker competed in Australian promotions like Xtreme Fighting Championships and Cage Fighting Championships, building a 6-0 record before a loss in Macau in 2011. He continued to fight, experiencing both wins and losses, before entering *The Ultimate Fighter*. His time on the show was marked by impressive knockouts, including a victory earning him $25,000 for "Knockout of the Season", and ultimately led to him winning the entire welterweight tournament at “The Ultimate Fighter: The Smashes Finale” in 2012.

After transitioning to the middleweight division, Whittaker achieved significant success in the UFC. He secured notable wins over fighters like Clint Hester, Brad Tavares, Uriah Hall, Rafael Natal, Derek Brunson, and Ronaldo Souza, earning multiple “Fight of the Night” and “Performance of the Night” bonuses. His championship reign included a unanimous decision victory over Yoel Romero to claim the interim title, and later being crowned the undisputed champion after St-Pierre’s title vacancy. Despite facing challenges including injuries and a loss to Israel Adesanya for the championship in 2019, Whittaker continued to compete at a high level, securing victories over Darren Till, Jared Cannonier, and Kelvin Gastelum. He has consistently remained a top contender in the division, with recent fights showcasing his resilience and skill.

Beyond MMA, Whittaker has also pursued a career in freestyle wrestling, winning the Australia Cup and Australian National Wrestling Championships in the 97 kg division and qualifying for the 2018 Commonwealth Games, though he ultimately withdrew to protect his UFC commitments. He is married to Sofia, and they have three sons and a daughter, and he is also the legal guardian of his younger half-siblings. Whittaker proudly acknowledges his Māori heritage and has a tattoo as a mark of respect for his ancestry.

title: María José (singer)
text:
María José, born on January 12, 1976, is a multifaceted Mexican artist known for her work as a singer, ballerina, flamenco dancer, athlete, and television personality. Her career began at age 15 with the popular band Kabah in the 1990s, where she gained recognition as a vocalist. She pursued a solo career after leaving Kabah in 2006 and has since released six studio albums. Prior to her musical career, she earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in communications and received early stage experience as a flamenco dancer with the Spanish Dance Company led by Maria Elena Anaya.

Her first solo album, *María José*, was released in 2007, featuring the single “Quien Eres Tu?” with Trey Songz. Although it reached number 84 in the Mexican charts, she left Warner Music shortly after its release, continuing as an independent artist. She followed this with *Amante de lo ajeno* in 2009, a collection of covers of 1980s pop hits, which included the successful single “No soy una señora.”  *Amante de lo Bueno* followed in 2010, also featuring reinterpretations of 80s songs, with “La Ocasión Para Amarnos” becoming a hit. 

María José continued to release albums, including *De Noche* in 2012, her second album of original material, and *Habla Ahora* in 2016, her third.  She’s demonstrated a talent for both performing original songs and revitalizing classic hits. In 2019, she released *Conexión*, a live album celebrating ten years of her solo work, featuring collaborations with artists like Ha*Ash and Yuri. 

Throughout her career, María José has also taken on opportunities outside of album releases. She opened for Gwen Stefani’s tour in Mexico and participated in the musical *Hoy No Me Puedo Levantar*, based on the songs of Mecano. She was nominated for Best New Artist at the Premios Oye! and appeared on the reality show *El Show de los Sueños*. More recently, she has expanded into television, becoming a judge on *México tiene talento* and a host/actress on *Esta historia me suena*. She also served as a coach on *La Voz* for two seasons. She was honored in San Francisco with a day declared in her name, February 6th, by the Board of Supervisors. 

María José cites a diverse range of artists as influences, including Mariah Carey, Rocío Dúrcal, Mecano, Celine Dion, and Boyz II Men, reflecting her broad musical taste and shaping her own distinctive style.

title: Zeca Pagodinho
text:
Zeca Pagodinho, whose real name is Jessé Gomes da Silva Filho, is a Brazilian singer-songwriter born on February 4, 1959, specializing in samba and pagode music. He was raised in Irajá, Rio de Janeiro, immersed in the traditions of samba, and began writing his own verses while involved with the GRES Portela samba school. During the 1970s, he became a regular at the Carnival Block of Cacique de Ramos, a significant hub for the development of pagode. 

His career took off after samba singer Beth Carvalho recognized his talent and invited him to record "Camarão Que Dorme a Onda Leva" in 1983. This led to the release of fifteen studio albums and three DVDs throughout his career. Zeca Pagodinho’s songs are known for their creative, joyful, and often playful lyrics that reflect the everyday life of the typical resident of Rio de Janeiro, contributing to his widespread popularity in Brazil. He is considered one of the country’s best-selling artists.

Zeca Pagodinho’s family includes his wife, Mônica Silva, and their children Eduardo, Elisa, Louis, and Maria Eduarda, as well as his grandson Noah and granddaughter Catarina. His daughter-in-law is Thalita. He currently resides in Barra da Tijuca with his family.

His music has reached a global audience, notably with the inclusion of his song "Deixa a Vida Me Levar" in the video game FIFA 2004. In 2015, his album *Ser Humano* received a nomination for Best Samba/Pagode Album at the 16th Latin Grammy Awards. 

Throughout his career, Zeca Pagodinho has received numerous awards, including three consecutive Troféu Imprensa awards for Best Singer from 2003 to 2005. He was also recognized at the 2009 VMB – Video Music Brasil awards for Best Samba, and earned three awards at the 2009 Prêmio da Música Brasileira for Best Singer, Best Album, and Best Song, as well as the 2008 Prêmio BRA GA de música for Best Singer. His discography includes albums released from 1986 through 2019, showcasing a consistent output of music over several decades.

title: Marcel Hernández
text:
Marcel Hernández Campanioni, born on July 11, 1989, is a Cuban professional footballer currently playing as a centre-forward for Herediano in Costa Rica, while also representing the Cuba national team. His club career has involved stints in the Dominican Republic and a complicated attempt to play in Kosovo. He began with Barcelona Atlético in the Dominican Republic on January 10, 2017, before moving to Cibao. A transfer to the Kosovan side Trepça’89 was announced on December 23, 2017, but ultimately failed to materialize due to bureaucratic issues, despite his registration with the Football Federation of Kosovo. It was anticipated he would join the team during a future transfer window, but this is not detailed further in the available information.

Hernández’s international career began with the Cuba under-23 team, where he made his debut on June 25, 2011, in a CONCACAF Men’s Pre-Olympic Tournament qualification match against Aruba U23. He started the game and scored two goals in a decisive 7-0 victory for Cuba. He progressed to the senior national team, making his debut on November 10, 2010, in a Caribbean Cup qualification match against Dominica. He also scored on his debut, contributing one goal to a 4-2 win. Throughout his time with the national team, he participated in 4 FIFA World Cup qualification matches.

However, Hernández surprisingly announced his retirement from international football on November 6, 2013, following his omission from the Cuban squad for the 2013 CONCACAF Gold Cup. The article does not provide any further details regarding the reasons for his retirement. 

Throughout his career, Hernández has achieved team and individual accolades. He was part of the Alajuelense team that won the CONCACAF League in 2020. He also celebrated victory with the Cuban national team, winning the Caribbean Cup in 2012. Individually, he was recognized as the Liga FPD Top Scorer during the Apertura 2020 season, demonstrating his goal-scoring ability. Further information about his career can be found at National-Football-Teams.com.

title: Bob Marley
text:
Robert Nesta Marley, born in Nine Mile, Jamaica, in 1945, was a singer, songwriter, and guitarist who became a pioneer of reggae music and a global cultural icon. He blended reggae with ska and rocksteady, creating a distinctive style and significantly increasing the visibility of Jamaican music internationally. Marley was deeply spiritual, becoming a prominent figure in the Rastafari movement and incorporating its themes into his work. He also became known for his advocacy of Pan-Africanism and the legalization of cannabis, often taking controversial stances on democratic social reforms.

Marley’s musical journey began in 1963 with the formation of the group Teenagers, alongside Peter Tosh and Bunny Wailer, which eventually evolved into the Wailers. Their debut album, *The Wailing Wailers* (1965), featured the song “One Love” and marked their initial rise within the reggae scene. The Wailers released eleven more albums before signing with Island Records and rebranding as Bob Marley and the Wailers. During this period, influenced by Marley’s conversion to Rastafari, their music shifted towards a more rhythmically focused style. A relocation to London followed, coinciding with the release of *The Best of The Wailers* in 1971.

The band gained international recognition after signing with Island Records and touring in support of *Catch a Fire* and *Burnin’* (both 1973). Following the group’s disbandment in 1974, Marley continued to record and perform under the name Bob Marley and the Wailers, assembling a new backing band and vocalists known as the “I Threes”. *Natty Dread* (1974) was well-received, but his international breakthrough came with a live version of “No Woman, No Cry” from the *Live!* album in 1975, and subsequently with *Rastaman Vibration* (1976), which charted in the US. 

In December 1976, Marley survived an assassination attempt at his home in Jamaica, believed to be politically motivated. He subsequently moved to London, where he recorded *Exodus*, an album that blended reggae with elements of blues, soul, and British rock, achieving both critical and commercial success. Tragically, in 1977, Marley was diagnosed with acral lentiginous melanoma, a form of skin cancer, and he died in May 1981 after being baptized into the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. His death prompted widespread grief and a state funeral in Jamaica.

Posthumously, Marley’s legacy has continued to grow. *Legend* (1984), a greatest hits compilation, became the best-selling reggae album of all time. He is estimated to have sold over 75 million records worldwide and has been honored with numerous accolades, including Jamaica’s Order of Merit, induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, and a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. *Rolling Stone* magazine ranked him among the greatest artists and singers of all time. His early life saw a somewhat distant relationship with his white Jamaican father, Norval Marley, and a strong influence from his maternal grandfather, a Myal man. His musical development began in childhood with friend Bunny Wailer and was fostered by local musicians like Joe Higgs, who helped develop their vocal harmonies.

title: Michael H. Schneider Sr.
text:
Michael H. Schneider Sr., born in 1943, dedicated his career to the legal system in Texas and at the federal level, culminating in his service as a United States District Judge. His educational background began with an Associate of Arts degree from Lon Morris College in 1963, followed by a Bachelor of Science from Stephen F. Austin State University in 1965. He completed his legal training at the University of Houston Law Center, earning a Juris Doctor in 1970.

Schneider’s early career involved public service as an assistant district attorney in Harris County, Texas, a position he held from 1971 to 1975. He then transitioned into private practice for a year before becoming a general attorney for Dresser Industries from 1976 to 1980. During this period, he also served part-time as a municipal judge for the City of West University Place, Texas, for twelve years, from 1978 to 1990. He continued his work as a general attorney, first with Bawden Drilling, Inc. from 1980 to 1986, and later as a general solicitor for the Union Pacific Railroad Company from 1986 to 1989, before briefly returning to private practice in 1989 and 1990.

Schneider's career then shifted toward judicial roles within the Texas state court system. He served as the presiding judge of the 157th District Court in Harris County from 1990 to 1996. He was subsequently appointed as chief justice of the First Court of Appeals of Texas in Houston, a position he held from 1996 to 2002. While serving on the Court of Appeals, he pursued further education, earning a Master of Laws degree from the University of Virginia Law School in 2001. In 2002, he reached the highest level of the Texas state judiciary, becoming a justice on the Supreme Court of Texas, a role he fulfilled until 2004.

In 2004, President George W. Bush nominated Schneider to the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Texas, filling the vacancy left by John H. Hannah Jr. The Senate confirmed his appointment on September 7, 2004, and he received his commission a few days later, on September 10, 2004. He served as a district judge for over eleven years, assuming senior status on January 7, 2016, before ultimately retiring from the bench on October 1, 2016.

title: Dana Ashbrook
text:
Dana Ashbrook is an American actor born on May 24, 1967, in San Diego, California. He comes from a theatrical family; his mother, D’Ann Paton, is a teacher, and his father, Vernon L. “Buddy” Ashbrook, directed the drama department at Palomar College. He has two siblings, writer Taylor Ashbrook and actress Daphne Ashbrook.

Ashbrook’s acting career began in 1978 with an uncredited role in *Attack of the Killer Tomatoes!*. After a period away from acting, he returned to the screen with guest appearances on television shows like *Cagney & Lacey*, *Knots Landing*, and *ABC Afterschool Special*. He then landed a role in the 1988 horror film *Return of the Living Dead Part II*, and also appeared in *Waxwork* and an episode of *21 Jump Street* the same year. He was initially set to star in a film called *A Place to Hide* in 1988, but the project was delayed and ultimately made in 1990 as *Night of the Warrior* with a different cast.

He gained significant recognition in 1989 for his portrayal of Joey in *She's Out of Control*, and then from 1990 to 1991 for his role as Bobby Briggs on the television series *Twin Peaks*. During his time on *Twin Peaks*, he also appeared in several films, including *Sundown: The Vampire in Retreat*, *Ghost Dad*, *Girlfriend from Hell*, and *The Willies*, as well as an episode of *The Hidden Room*. 

Ashbrook reprised his role as Bobby Briggs in the 1992 *Twin Peaks* prequel film, *Fire Walk with Me*. That same year, he played Clyde Barrow in the television film *Bonnie & Clyde: The True Story*. Throughout the 1990s, he continued to work steadily, appearing in the short film *The Coriolis Effect* (with Jennifer Rubin and Quentin Tarantino), *Cityscrapes: Los Angeles* (1994), the science fiction pilot *W.E.I.R.D. World* (1995), and the film *Comfortably Numb* (1995). He also had guest roles on *The Outer Limits* in both 1996 and later, and was cast as Gary McDermott in the short-lived series *Crisis Center* in 1997.

Into the 2000s, Ashbrook’s television work included appearances on *Charmed*, *The Pretender*, and *Law & Order: Special Victims Unit*. He had a recurring role as Rich Rinaldi on *Dawson’s Creek* from 2002 to 2003 and joined the cast of *Crash* in 2009 as Jimmy. He revisited the world of *Twin Peaks* in 2010 with a guest appearance on *Psych* alongside other members of the original cast. More recent film appearances include *The Aggression Scale* (2012) and the werewolf horror film *Late Phases* (2014). In 2017, he once again took on the role of Bobby Briggs in David Lynch’s revival of *Twin Peaks*, titled *The Return*.

title: Maggie Cogan
text:
Maggie Cogan is a New York City resident best known for being the first female coachman in Central Park, employed by the Plaza Hotel. Her pioneering role garnered media attention, including a 1967 appearance in a Universal newsreel and a 1968 spot on the quiz show *What’s My Line?* where panelists attempted to identify her profession. She famously voiced her opposition to a proposal to install meters on the horse-drawn carriages, believing it would cheapen the experience.

Cogan’s early life included cheerleading and dance in high school in New Hyde Park, Long Island, followed by attendance at several colleges, though she did not earn a degree. She began her career with the Plaza Hotel at the age of 19. However, her life began to experience difficulties in the late 1960s. She endured two unsuccessful marriages and had two sons, whom she ultimately relinquished to her parents after struggling with the aftermath of her failed relationships and being unable to reclaim them upon returning to New York from a four-year stay in Texas.

The 1970s saw a decline in Cogan’s mental health. While living with Lisa Ryan, the daughter of actor Robert Ryan, she developed intense infatuations, first with Robert Ryan, sending him unusual gifts, and later with serial killer David Berkowitz. She also suffered a violent mugging that resulted in facial slashes, and experienced a separate, unspecified sexual assault. These events led to a severe emotional breakdown, culminating in her parents committing her to a mental hospital in 1977.

Following her release and the loss of her job, Cogan became homeless and spent approximately fifteen years living in Central Park. During this time, she created elaborate stories about her life, claiming to be Robert Ryan's daughter and possessing extrasensory perception. Despite her hardships, she maintained friendships and relied on the kindness of others for food and clothing, and found companionship with several dogs she adopted.

Her story came to the attention of filmmaker Michel Negroponte in 1989 while he was working on a different documentary. He shifted his focus to Cogan and created *Jupiter's Wife*, a film documenting her life in the park. The film captured her daily routines and interactions, and ultimately led to public assistance being granted, allowing Cogan to secure an apartment, though this housing was later lost in a 1995 eviction. She briefly lived with a friend at a pet shelter, but returned to Central Park after five weeks. The film received a special jury prize at the Sundance Film Festival.

title: Ryan Brasier
text:
Ryan Brasier, born August 26, 1987, is a professional baseball pitcher currently with the Chicago Cubs, having previously played for the Los Angeles Angels, Boston Red Sox, and Los Angeles Dodgers, as well as the Hiroshima Toyo Carp in Japan. He has won two World Series championships, one with the Red Sox in 2018 and another with the Dodgers in 2024. He stands 6 feet tall, weighs 225 pounds, and is a right-handed pitcher and batter.

Brasier initially played catcher at S.H. Rider High School in Texas, but switched to pitching in college at Weatherford College. He was drafted by the Los Angeles Angels in the sixth round of the 2007 MLB draft and spent six years working his way through their minor league system, reaching Triple-A. He made his major league debut with the Angels in 2013, appearing in seven games with a 2.00 ERA. A Tommy John surgery sidelined him for the entire 2014 season, and he was later released by the Angels. 

After a brief stint with the Oakland Athletics organization in 2015-2016, and a period of rehabilitation, Brasier chose to play professionally in Japan with the Hiroshima Toyo Carp in 2017. He credits his time in Japan with helping him refine his pitching mechanics. Returning to the United States, he signed a minor league contract with the Boston Red Sox in 2018. 

Brasier quickly rose through the Red Sox system, earning a spot on the major league roster mid-season and contributing to their 2018 World Series victory. He continued with the Red Sox through 2022, earning a save in 2019 and navigating injury setbacks, including a calf injury and being hit by a line drive in 2021. He experienced varying levels of success with the Red Sox, with some seasons marked by strong performance and others by struggles. 

In May 2023, after a difficult start to the season, the Red Sox designated Brasier for assignment and later released him. He quickly signed a minor league deal with the Los Angeles Dodgers, where he impressed and was called up to the majors, playing a key role in their postseason run and ultimately winning the 2024 World Series. He signed a two-year contract with the Dodgers but was designated for assignment in January 2025 before being traded to the Chicago Cubs a few days later.

title: Cha Eun-woo
text:
Lee Dong-min, professionally known as Cha Eun-woo, was born on March 30, 1997, in Gunpo, South Korea, and is a singer and actor. He debuted as a member of the boy band Astro in 2016, releasing their first EP, *Spring Up*. He also began his acting career in 2014 with a small role in the film *My Brilliant Life*, which led to a modeling contract with Shara Shara cosmetics. 

Before his entertainment career took off, Cha attended Nungnae Elementary School, Suri Middle School, and Suri High School, eventually graduating from Hanlim Multi Art School in 2016 with a focus on broadcasting and acting. He continued his education at Sungkyunkwan University, majoring in performing arts. His initial foray into acting came after a talent scout approached him during a middle school festival, leading to training throughout high school. In 2015, he starred in the web drama *To Be Continued* alongside Kim Sae-ron.

Following Astro’s debut, Cha engaged in a variety of activities, including appearances on reality shows like *Law of the Jungle* and hosting *Show! Music Core* alongside other idols. He continued to take on acting roles, with notable appearances in web dramas like *My Romantic Some Recipe* and *Sweet Revenge*. His first leading television role came in 2018 with *Gangnam Beauty*, which significantly boosted his popularity and earned him recognition in GQ Korea’s “Men of the Year.”

He continued to build his acting portfolio with roles in *Rookie Historian Goo Hae-ryung* (2019), where he won acting awards, *True Beauty* (2020-2021), *Island* (2022-2023) and *A Good Day to Be a Dog* (2023-2024). In 2024, he premiered in *Wonderful World* alongside veteran actress Kim Nam-joo. In January 2024, he debuted as a soloist with the EP *Entity*, featuring the single “Stay,” and embarked on a fan concert tour across Asia.

Throughout his career, Cha has become a highly sought-after model, representing numerous brands including Tommy Hilfiger, Dior, Samsonite, and more recently, Calvin Klein and Chaumet. He also actively participates in philanthropic endeavors, donating to causes like ALS research, victims of the Sokcho Fire, and student scholarships at his alma mater. He’s also supported COVID-19 relief efforts and initiatives promoting Korean language education.  In 2025, he is leading an effort to create a tribute song for his late Astro bandmate, Moonbin, and will star in his first leading film role, *First Ride*.

title: Ricky Martin
text:
Ricky Martin, born Enrique José Martín Morales in San Juan, Puerto Rico in 1971, is a globally recognized singer, songwriter, and actor celebrated for his versatility across numerous musical genres including Latin pop, dance, reggaeton, and salsa. He began his career remarkably early, appearing in television commercials at age nine and joining the popular Puerto Rican boy band Menudo at twelve. He remained with Menudo until 1989, navigating a rigorous schedule and acknowledging the sacrifices it made to his childhood, but also appreciating the opportunities it provided.

Following his departure from Menudo, Martin pursued both acting and a solo music career. He initially found work in Mexican television, starring in soap operas and a related film, which led to a recording contract with Sony Discos. His first two solo albums, *Ricky Martin* (1991) and *Me Amaras* (1993), primarily focused on ballads and established him within Latin America. He then transitioned towards a broader sound with his 1995 album, *A Medio Vivir*, which propelled him to prominence in Europe and featured the breakthrough hit “María.” This song, a fusion of Latin musical styles, became his first international success, selling over five million copies and topping charts in numerous countries.

The success of “María” paved the way for *Vuelve* (1998), an album that earned Martin his first Grammy Award and included hits like "Vuelve" and "La Copa de la Vida," which he performed at the Grammy Awards. His 1999 self-titled English album solidified his international stardom, debuting at number one on the US Billboard 200 chart with the smash single "Livin' la Vida Loca" also topping charts in the US and UK. This period is widely considered the beginning of the “Latin explosion,” with Martin credited with bringing Latin pop into the mainstream and opening doors for other Latin artists.

Throughout the 2000s and 2010s, Martin continued to release successful albums, including *Almas del Silencio* (2003), *MTV Unplugged* (2006), and *A Quien Quiera Escuchar* (2015), which won a Grammy. He also pursued acting roles, appearing in the soap opera *General Hospital* and receiving an Emmy nomination for his portrayal of Antonio D’Amico in *The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story*. He also starred as Ché in a Broadway revival of *Evita*. 

Over his career, Ricky Martin has sold over 70 million records worldwide, earning numerous awards including two Grammys, five Latin Grammys, and multiple awards from MTV, the American Music Awards, Billboard, and World Music Awards. Beyond his artistic achievements, Martin is a dedicated philanthropist, founding The Ricky Martin Foundation in 2004 to fight human trafficking and advocate for LGBT rights. His early life was marked by a stable upbringing despite his parents’ divorce, with strong family connections and a musical upbringing influencing his future career.

title: Irina Shayk
text:
Irina Shaykhlislamova, known professionally as Irina Shayk, is a Russian fashion model who rose to international prominence after becoming the first Russian model to appear on the cover of the 2011 *Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue*. Born in 1986 in Yemanzhelinsk, Russia, she comes from a family with a Volga Tatar father who was a coal miner and a Russian mother who was a music teacher. She credits her father with her physical appearance, noting that people frequently assume she is South American due to his heritage. She has a sister, Tatiana, and is an aunt to her three children, one of whom is also named Irina.

Shayk’s early life included seven years of musical training, playing piano and singing in a choir at her mother's insistence. Her father’s death from pneumonia when she was fourteen created financial hardship for her family. After high school, she initially studied marketing before attending beauty school with her sister. It was there that she was discovered by a local modeling agency and encouraged to enter the “Miss Chelyabinsk 2004” contest, which she won, though she characterized it as less prestigious than similar contests in larger cities. 

Her modeling career began in 2007 when she replaced Ana Beatriz Barros as the face of Intimissimi and debuted in *Sports Illustrated*. She became the official ambassador for Intimissimi in 2010 and also worked with brands like Beach Bunny Swimwear, Guess, Victoria’s Secret, Lacoste and others.  She signed with IMG Models in 2009.  Shayk transitioned from swimwear to high fashion, appearing in magazines such as *Harper’s Bazaar* and *Elle Spain*, and was named “Best International Model of 2010” by *Glamour Spain*.  A nude photoshoot for *GQ Spain* in 2010 sparked controversy, with the magazine claiming digital alteration to remove lingerie, a claim she disputed. 

The 2011 *Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue* cover proved to be a breakthrough moment, and she continued to appear on the covers of numerous international magazines including *Tatler Russia*, *Cosmopolitan Spain*, and *Glamour Spain*.  Throughout the early 2010s she worked with brands like Rampage, Replay and XTI.  She walked runways for designers like Jeremy Scott and Givenchy, and continued to feature in major fashion publications like *Vogue* and *Vanity Fair*. In 2014, she served as the placard bearer for the Russian team during the opening ceremony of the 2014 Winter Olympics.

More recently, in 2016, she walked in the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show while pregnant with her daughter, Lea de Seine Shayk Cooper.  She became a L'Oréal Paris International Spokesperson in 2015. In 2022, Models.com included her on their list of the “New Supers.” She also made her acting debut in the 2014 film *Hercules*.

Shayk was engaged to footballer Cristiano Ronaldo from 2009 to 2015, and later had a relationship with actor Bradley Cooper from 2015 to 2019, with whom she shares a daughter.

title: Kathinka Pasveer
text:
Kathinka Pasveer, born June 11, 1959, in Zaandam, Netherlands, is a flautist renowned for her close collaboration with composer Karlheinz Stockhausen. Her father, Jan Pasveer, was a conductor and taught at the Amsterdam Conservatory. She received her performer’s diploma from the Royal Conservatory of The Hague in 1983, winning the Nicolai Prize, and served as principal flutist of the Gewestelijk Orkest Zuid-Holland during her final year of studies. 

Her defining artistic relationship began in December 1982 when Stockhausen invited her to work with him on compositions including *Zeitmaße*, *Amour*, and *In Freundschaft*. This led to her involvement in the creation and premiere of *Kathinkas Gesang*, the second scene of Stockhausen’s opera *Samstag aus Licht* in 1983, a performance that required six months of rehearsal. She subsequently performed the role at the staged premiere of *Samstag* at La Scala in Milan in 1984. Stockhausen then created a version of the piece for flute and six-channel electronic music, premiered by Pasveer at Ircam in Paris in 1985.

This initial connection sparked a twenty-five-year collaboration with Stockhausen until his death in 2007. He composed numerous works specifically for her, all of which she premiered, and many were dedicated to her. These include parts in *Montag aus Licht* (1988), *Dienstag aus Licht* (1993), and *Freitag aus Licht* (1996), as well as concert premieres of *Orchester-Finalisten* (1996), *Michaelion* (1998), and *Licht-Bilder* (2004). Later works included flute versions of *Harmonien* (2006) and *Paradies* (2007), both part of the chamber-music cycle *Klang*.

Beyond performing Stockhausen’s flute compositions, Pasveer embraced diverse roles within his work. She learned and performed the solo dancer-mime part for *Inori* in 1989, a piece she considers deeply personal and frequently practices as a meditative exercise. She also memorized and performs the 83-minute *Vortrag über HU*, a sung and mimed lecture accompanying *Inori*, in both German and English. Additionally, she has performed the dancer-mime role in *Vision*. Her versatility extended to vocal performance, recording soprano parts for works such as *Dienstag aus Licht*, *Freitag aus Licht*, and *Die sieben Lieder der Tage*.

Since 1998, Pasveer has taught the interpretation of Stockhausen’s works at the annual Stockhausen Courses for New Music in Kürten. She assisted Stockhausen with recordings beginning in 1983, learning his techniques for sound projection, and after his death, she continued as a sound projectionist and became instrumental in producing and mixing the recordings for the *Stockhausen Complete Edition*, alongside Antonio Pérez-Abellán. She also contributed to the creation of the sound loops for *Cosmic Pulses*.  Currently, she co-directs the Stockhausen Foundation for Music with Suzanne Stephens. Her niece is harpist Marianne Smit.

title: Worranit Thawornwong
text:
Worranit Thawornwong, also known as Mook, is a Thai actress and singer born on October 9, 1996, in Bangkok. She is the second child in her family and has an actor brother, Jirakit Thawornwong. Worranit completed her secondary education at Satriwitthaya 2 School and later graduated from the Faculty of Humanities at Kasetsart University. 

Her career in acting began in 2014 with roles in the Channel Bang dramas *Rukjing Pinker*, where she played Bew, and *Room Alone 401–410*, as Snow. However, she gained significant recognition in 2015 with her portrayal of Junior in the popular television series *Ugly Duckling Series: Perfect Match*, alongside Puttichai Kasetsin. As part of this role, she also contributed vocally, performing a song for the series.

Following this success, Worranit continued to appear in a string of television series, often paired with different co-stars. In 2016, she starred in *Kiss The Series* with Sattaphong Phiangphor and took on a role in *U-Prince* alongside March Chutavuth Pattarakampol, specifically in the segment titled “Ambitious Boss.” The following year, she appeared in *My Dear Loser* with Thanat Lowkhunsombat, in the segment “Monster Romance.” 

This pattern of appearing in various series segments continued in subsequent years. She was paired with Perawat Sangpotirat in *Mint To Be* (2018), and with Yuke Songpaisan in *Love At First Hate* (2018). In 2019, she featured in *Mia Noi* with Krissada Pornweroj and *Plara Song Krueng* with Oil Thana Suttikamol. More recently, in 2020, she acted in *Girl Next Room* alongside Pathompong Reonchaidee, in the segment “Motorbike Baby”, and also appeared in *Ban Sao Sod* with Jirayu La-ongmanee.

Beyond her acting roles, Worranit has contributed to several drama soundtracks, singing songs such as "Mah Tun Welah Por Dee" and "Kon Jao Choo" ("Bee Dup Bee Doo") for *Ugly Duckling: Perfect Match*, and "Poot Wah Ruk Nai Jai" for *Roon Pee Secret Love*. She has also participated in the singing competition show *The Mask Singer Thailand*. In 2025, she made the decision not to renew her contract with GMMTV, marking a potential shift in her career path.

title: Carl Braun (obstetrician)
text:
Carl Braun, born in Zistersdorf, Austria, in 1822, was a prominent Austrian obstetrician who significantly contributed to the development of both obstetrics and gynecology as distinct medical fields. He was the son of physician Carl August Braun and received his medical education in Vienna, beginning in 1841. He initially served as an assistant doctor at the Vienna General Hospital in 1847, and in 1849, he succeeded Ignaz Semmelweis as an assistant to Professor Johann Klein at the hospital’s maternity clinic, a position he held for four years.

In 1853, Braun was appointed professor of obstetrics in Trient and also became vice-director of the Tiroler Landes-Gebär- und Findelanstalt. He returned to Vienna in 1856 to take over from Johann Klein as professor of obstetrics. A pivotal achievement was his recommendation and subsequent establishment of the hospital’s first gynaecology clinic in 1858, which he directed, effectively solidifying gynecology as a separate area of medical study. 

Throughout his career, Braun held several administrative roles at the University of Vienna, serving as dean of the medical faculty from 1867 to 1871 and as rector during the 1868-1869 academic year. He was recognized for his contributions with a knighthood in 1872, becoming Carl Ritter von Fernwald Braun, and later achieved the title of Hofrat in 1877, an honor bestowed upon highly respected professors.

Despite differing in opinion with Ignaz Semmelweis regarding the cause of puerperal fever – Braun identified 30 potential causes while Semmelweis focused on ‘cadaverous poisoning’ – Braun consistently achieved low mortality rates in his division, comparable to those attained by Semmelweis, indicating he continued to enforce hand disinfection practices. He is also associated with the “Braun-Fernwald sign,” an asymmetrical enlargement and softening of the uterine fundus detectable during early pregnancy, specifically between four and five weeks of gestation.

Braun authored several important medical texts, including *Klinik der Geburtshilfe und Gynäkologie* (1855), co-authored with Chiari and Spaeth, *Lehrbuch der Geburtshilfe* (1857), a textbook on obstetrics, and a second edition of *Lehrbuch der gesammten Gynäkologie* in 1881. He also published a study on caesarean sections and hysterectomies performed on patients with narrow pelves. Carl Braun died in 1891.

title: Shawn Ashmore
text:
Shawn Ashmore, born October 7, 1979, in Richmond, British Columbia, is a Canadian actor with a diverse career spanning film, television, and video games. He began acting as a child, landing his first role after his twin brother Aaron was initially cast in a commercial but became ill. The brothers were sometimes chosen for parts by a coin flip early in their careers. Ashmore received a Gemini Award nomination at age 14 for his leading role in the TV film *Guitarman* (1994).

He gained prominence in the late 1990s and early 2000s with roles in television series like *Animorphs* (1998-1999) and *In a Heartbeat* (2000-2001), and the Disney Channel Original Movie *Cadet Kelly* (2002). However, international recognition came with his portrayal of Bobby Drake / Iceman in the *X-Men* film franchise, beginning in 2000 and continuing through 2014. He won an MTV Movie Award for Breakthrough Male Performance for *X2* (2003).

Beyond the *X-Men* films, Ashmore took on leading roles in movies like *Terry* (2005), a biopic about Terry Fox, and horror films *The Ruins* (2008) and *Frozen* (2010). On television, he played FBI agent Mike Weston in *The Following* (2013–2015) and currently stars as attorney Wesley Evers in the police procedural *The Rookie* (2018–present), becoming a series regular in the third season. 

Ashmore has also made significant inroads into the video game industry, providing voice and performance capture for characters in *Quantum Break* (2016), *The Dark Pictures Anthology: Man of Medan* (2019), and *Alan Wake II* (2023). His work in *Quantum Break* was particularly lauded, with critics praising his nuanced performance.

Throughout his career, Ashmore has received a Leo Award for *Legend of Earthsea* (2004) and multiple Gemini and Saturn Award nominations. He often works alongside his identical twin brother, Aaron Ashmore, with whom he shared a scene in the *Fringe* episode “Amber 31422” after fifteen years of not acting together. 

Ashmore married Dana Renee Wasdin in 2012, whom he met on the set of *Frozen*. They have one son, Oliver, born in 2017. Both brothers have matching “GMA” tattoos honoring their step-grandfather, Gangu Jagtiani. He has also used his platform to support breast cancer awareness causes, participating in fundraising events.

title: Abdul Halik Hudu
text:
Abdul Halik Hudu, nicknamed Rooney, is a Ghanaian professional footballer born on March 19, 2000, who currently plays as a midfielder for Al-Wehdat SC in the Jordanian Pro League. He began his career with Inter Allies in the Ghana Premier League, having progressed from their youth system at Accra Youth FC. He quickly became a regular starter, appearing in 19 games during his debut season in 2016, and was recognized for his talent by winning both the “Most Promising Player of the Year” award and the “Fans' Player of the Season” award for Inter Allies that same year. 

In 2017, Hudu had a trial period with Swedish club Hammarby IF, participating in friendly matches. He returned to Inter Allies before the season began, and continued to impress, earning “Man of the Match” honors in three league games throughout the year. Over two seasons with Inter Allies, he made a total of 37 competitive appearances and scored two goals.

Hudu eventually secured a permanent move to Hammarby IF in early January 2018, signing a three-and-a-half-year contract shortly after turning 18. He scored on his competitive debut for the club on August 23rd in a 3–0 win against Carlstad United in the Svenska Cupen. Following a season with Hammarby, he was loaned to IK Frej in the Superettan in 2019, playing 26 games and scoring twice, though the club was relegated during his time there. He then spent the latter part of 2020 on loan at GIF Sundsvall, simultaneously extending his contract with Hammarby for another year. 

A significant achievement in his career came on May 30, 2021, when he won the Svenska Cupen with Hammarby IF, defeating BK Häcken in a penalty shootout after a 0–0 draw. Later in 2021, on July 16th, Hudu moved to Lyngby in Denmark, signing a two-year contract and making his debut as a substitute in a 2–1 win over Jammerbugt. In March 2022, he returned to Sweden, joining AFC Eskilstuna on another two-year deal. Most recently, in December 2023, he signed a three-season contract with GIF Sundsvall before moving to Al-Wehdat SC in January 2025.

Internationally, Hudu has represented Ghana at the under-17 level, even captaining the team to an 8–0 victory over Namibia in March 2016. He also received a call-up to the Ghana under-20 team in 2018 for a match against Algeria. He has received individual recognition for his play, earning the "Most Promising Player of the Year" award in the Ghanaian Premier League in 2016.

title: Pratibha Patil
text:
Pratibha Patil, born on December 19, 1934, in Nadgaon, Maharashtra, is an Indian politician and lawyer who notably served as the President of India from 2007 to 2012, becoming the first woman to hold the office. She is associated with the Indian National Congress and previously served as the Governor of Rajasthan from 2004 to 2007, and as a Member of Parliament in both the Lok Sabha (1991-1996) and Rajya Sabha (1985-1990).

Patil’s early life involved education at R. R. Vidyalaya and then earning master's degrees in Political Science and Economics from Mooljee Jetha College, followed by a law degree from Government Law College, Bombay. She began her career practicing law in Jalgaon while also focusing on social issues related to women. She married Devisingh Ramsingh Shekhawat in 1965 and they have a daughter, Jyoti Rathore, and a son, Raosaheb Shekhawat, who is also a politician.

Her political career began in 1962 with election to the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly, representing Jalgaon, and continued with four consecutive wins in the Muktainagar constituency until 1985. Beyond her legislative roles, Patil held various cabinet positions in Maharashtra and served in leadership roles within the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha. She also held positions with national co-operative organizations. In 2004, she became the first woman Governor of Rajasthan.

In 2007, Patil was nominated as the United Progressive Alliance’s (UPA) presidential candidate, emerging as a compromise choice. Her candidacy was not without controversy; she faced accusations of shielding her brother in a murder case, a claim that was initially rejected by the courts but later led to charges against her brother in 2015. The presidential election, unlike the usual consensus-based selection, became a contested race against Bhairon Singh Shekhawat, the incumbent vice-president. Opponents criticized her experience, charisma, and questioned her beliefs, including references to a spiritual guru and a past comment on sterilization. Allegations also surfaced regarding misappropriation of funds during her time as a Member of Parliament. 

Despite these challenges, Patil won the election and became India's 12th President, taking office on July 25, 2007. Her presidency was marked by controversies, including a record number of death sentence commutations and significant spending on foreign travel, often accompanied by family members. 

After leaving office in 2012, further scrutiny arose regarding the construction of a retirement mansion using public funds on military land and questions about her use of official allowances. Patil also has business interests, including the Vidya Bharati Shikshan Prasarak Mandal educational institute and the Shram Sadhana Trust, which supports working women. She was also involved with a cooperative sugar factory and, significantly, a cooperative bank, Pratibha Mahila Sahakari Bank, which ultimately failed due to alleged illegal loans to relatives and was forced into liquidation. She received the Mexican Order of the Aztec Eagle in 2018.

title: Shane Fontayne
text:
Shane Fontayne, born Michael Barakan on April 29, 1954, is an English rock guitarist with a career spanning several decades, beginning in the 1970s. He is perhaps best known for his work as Bruce Springsteen’s guitarist during the 1992-1993 “Other Band” Tour, a period when Springsteen was performing without his regular E Street Band. 

Fontayne’s musical journey began with the bands Ora and later Byzantium, an English psychedelic music group. Throughout his career, he has collaborated with a diverse array of prominent musicians. In the early 1980s, he worked with Steve Forbert on the album *Little Stevie Orbit*. He also contributed to albums by Lone Justice (*Shelter*, 1986) and Maria McKee (*Maria McKee*, 1989). Later collaborations included work with Joe Cocker on *Heart & Soul* in 2004, and Richard Marx’s *My Own Best Enemy*, also released in 2004.

Beyond these artists, Fontayne has toured and recorded with a significant number of well-known names in the music industry. He served as the guitarist for French rock icon Johnny Hallyday during the “Lorada tour” in 1995 and a 1996 concert in Las Vegas. He has been a touring guitarist for singer-songwriter Marc Cohn since 1998. More recently, he has worked with Crosby, Stills & Nash, and Graham Nash, touring with both and also producing Nash’s 2016 album *This Path Tonight*.

A notable performance in Fontayne’s career occurred in 2012 at the Kennedy Center Honors. He played lead electric guitar on Ann and Nancy Wilson's rendition of “Stairway to Heaven,” alongside Jason Bonham on drums, in a tribute to Led Zeppelin.

On a personal note, Fontayne was married to actress Mackenzie Phillips from 1986 until 2000, and they have one son, Shane, born in 1987. His brother, Peter Barakan, is a music critic based in Japan. 

As a solo artist, Fontayne has released three albums: *Merchants of Venus* in 1991, *What Nature Intended* in 2003, and *Voodoo at the Mint* in 2006. Further information about his work can be found on his official website, as well as on CD Baby, AllMusic, and Discogs. An interview with Fontayne is also available through the NAMM Oral History Library from 2017.

title: Lodewicus du Plessis
text:
Lodewicus Johannes du Plessis was a South African academic and political thinker born in Burgersdorp, Cape Colony, on February 10, 1897. He was the son of Jacobus Albertus du Plessis and Laurika Postma, and married Engela Susanna van der Merwe in 1926. He passed away on February 19, 1968, in Potchefstroom, Transvaal. Du Plessis enjoyed a lengthy and varied educational path, beginning with his matriculation from Potchefstroom Gimnasium in 1912. He then attended the University of Pretoria, where he earned a Bachelor of Arts degree, followed by Bachelor of Arts Honours and a Master of Arts degree, all focusing on Classical languages. He further expanded his academic credentials by obtaining a master’s degree in Economics and ultimately qualifying as a lawyer with an LL.B. degree.

Du Plessis began his professional life in 1918 as a senior lecturer in Classical languages at the Theological Seminar of the Reformed Church in Potchefstroom. Capitalizing on his later qualifications in economics and law, he transitioned into a professorship at the Potchefstroom University for Christian Higher Education, teaching economics, political science, and ethics before concentrating his efforts on law in his later career. Beyond his academic role, he contributed significantly to the Afrikaans community as secretary to the commission responsible for translating the Bible into Afrikaans, and also served as an advisor to the influential figure, Totius.

His theological stance was characterized by an open-minded approach to Calvinism. While deeply rooted in the tradition, Du Plessis didn't view it as the sole path to truth, and was receptive to integrating elements from other belief systems, including Marxism. Politically, he was involved in Afrikaner politics but never sought elected office. He held the position of chairman of the Afrikaner Broederbond from 1930 to 1932, a position of influence within the Afrikaner community. 

Du Plessis was known for his independent thinking and willingness to publicly disagree with prominent political leaders of the time, including J.B.M. Hertzog, DF Malan, and J.G. Strijdom. His most significant political conflict arose with H.F. Verwoerd, ultimately leading to his expulsion from the National Party and his decision to resign from the Afrikaner Broederbond. This was due to his opposition to Verwoerd's racial policies and his restrictive definition of who qualified as an Afrikaner, demonstrating a divergence in their ideologies regarding the future of South Africa.

title: Francisco Urroz (footballer)
text:
Francisco Urroz Martínez, born on December 14, 1920, and passing away on January 22, 1992, was a Chilean footballer who excelled as a defender. Though born in Higuerote, Venezuela, he became a significant figure in Chilean football, enjoying a successful club and international career. He died at the age of 71 in Concón, Chile.

Urroz’s introduction to football came early, joining Unión Deportiva Española in 1931 alongside his brothers, Guillermo and Gilberto. This was facilitated by their uncle, Simón Martínez, who was a prominent leader within the sport. He quickly progressed through the ranks and became a key member of the first team by 1940, eventually earning the position of team captain. His leadership and skill culminated in a significant achievement for the club: winning the 1943 Primera División de Chile, marking Unión Española’s first-ever league title.

Following his success with Unión Española, Urroz transferred to Colo-Colo, another leading Chilean club. This move proved equally fruitful, as he again secured a Primera División title, this time with Colo-Colo in 1947. This demonstrates his ability to contribute to winning teams across different clubs, solidifying his reputation as a talented and consistent player.

Beyond his club achievements, Urroz also represented his adopted nation on the international stage. He earned 11 caps for the Chile national team and participated in the 1950 FIFA World Cup, a prestigious event showcasing his abilities against some of the world’s best players. The article does not detail his specific contributions during the World Cup, but his selection signifies his importance to the Chilean national squad at the time.

Details about his personal life reveal a difficult early experience with the loss of his father, Francisco Sr., a fruits and vegetables seller, when Urroz was just thirteen years old. He later became a father himself, with his daughter Silvana Urroz becoming a noted tennis player. His legacy extended further through his grandchildren, including Manuela Urroz, a field hockey player who also briefly played football for Unión Española in her youth, and Francisco Urroz, a rugby union player who also pursued a career as a doctor. Thus, sporting talent and a dedication to professional life ran through multiple generations of the Urroz family.

title: Sila María Calderón
text:
Sila María Calderón Serra, born in San Juan, Puerto Rico in 1942, is a prominent figure in Puerto Rican politics and business, best known as the island’s first elected female governor, serving from 2001 to 2005. Her lineage includes a maternal grandfather who emigrated from Mallorca, Spain, which later granted her Spanish citizenship in 2012. She received a Bachelor of Arts degree in Government from Manhattanville College in 1964 and furthered her education at the University of Puerto Rico’s Graduate School of Public Administration.

Calderón’s career began in 1973 as an aide to the Labor Secretary, followed by a role as a special aide to Governor Rafael Hernández Colón. After a period in the private sector at Citibank, where she successfully developed new consumer products, she became president of Commonwealth Investment Company, a family-owned real estate business. She re-entered government service in 1984 as Chief of Staff to Hernández Colón, becoming the first woman to hold that position, and later served as the 12th Secretary of State of Puerto Rico in 1988. During these roles, she also participated in economic advisory councils and boards related to government development and the Fifth Centenary of the Discovery of the Americas.

Returning to the private sector in 1989, Calderón served on the boards of several major Puerto Rican corporations, including BanPonce and Banco Popular, and held leadership positions within organizations focused on economic development and public broadcasting. She re-entered political life in 1995, winning the mayoral election for San Juan in 1996, becoming only the second woman to hold that office. As mayor, she initiated extensive urban redevelopment projects across the city, focusing on revitalizing deteriorated areas and assisting impoverished communities.

In 2000, Calderón was elected Governor of Puerto Rico, leading the Popular Democratic Party to victory in a closely contested election. During her term, she prioritized aid to disadvantaged communities, establishing the Puerto Rico Office for Socioeconomic and Community Development with a significant investment of $1 billion, though the program faced criticism for incomplete projects and potential fund diversion. She chose to appoint her daughters, Sila Mari and María Elena, as joint First Ladies. She also strengthened ties with Latin American nations, receiving honors from the Dominican Republic, Panama, and Costa Rica for her efforts. 

Calderón did not seek re-election in 2004, and after leaving office, she became a partner in Inter-American Global Links, Inc., a consulting firm. She also chairs a philanthropic foundation dedicated to addressing issues like poverty, women’s rights, and urban revitalization. Throughout her career, she has received numerous awards and honorary degrees recognizing her contributions to public service and leadership. She has been married three times, first to Francisco Xavier González Goenaga, then to Adolfo Krans, and finally to Ramón Cantero Frau, all of which ended in divorce.

title: Ameyaw Debrah
text:
Ameyaw Debrah is a Ghanaian celebrity blogger, journalist, and reporter who is widely known for founding the entertainment website AmeyawDebrah.com. He earned a bachelor’s degree in publishing from Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), where he was recognized as the Best Publishing Student in 2005. His career in media began during his time at Adisadel College, where he served as an editor for the school magazine in 1999.

After graduating from KNUST, Debrah completed his National Service Secretariat (NSS) program at Ovation International Magazine in Accra, focusing on coverage of the Ghanaian entertainment scene for an international audience. He then became a columnist for the Star newspaper before contributing to several pan-African websites – Jamati.com, Orijin-ent.com, and ModernGhana.com – in 2007. He also worked with the Netherlands-based media project Voices of Africa, providing content for Africanews.com.

In 2008, Debrah joined GhanaWeb.com as its entertainment editor and simultaneously launched his own blog, AmeyawDebrah.com. He eventually left Ghanaweb in 2012 to dedicate himself fully to his blog. He continues to contribute to other platforms, including the entertainment segment StarGist on Africa Magic, EbonyLife TV, and Glitz Africa Magazine. He has also served as an ambassador for the Malta Guinness Africa Rising Campaign. 

AmeyawDebrah.com gained traction with the help of a friend who assisted with hosting and domain acquisition. The site launched an iPhone app in 2010 and hosted an online talent competition in 2012 to promote emerging Ghanaian musicians, as well as the My Ghana Campaign, inviting video submissions on relevant national issues. 

Debrah’s career also includes leadership roles at Ringier Ghana, where he launched and managed Pulse Ghana in late 2014 before moving to Genesis Technology in 2015. He then served as editor-in-chief of Yen.com.gh from September 2015 to September 2017. Beyond journalism, he has worked in artist management, first with music producer Coptic, handling his affairs in Ghana and scouting talent for his Rebel Musik label, and later with Pappy Kojo in 2014.

In 2018, Debrah launched Ameyaw TV, a web portal showcasing various video formats, and subsequently debuted shows like Daily Buzz, News in One, and Trend Mill, with further programming planned. On a personal note, Ameyaw Debrah married Elsie Darkoa on March 6, 2018, and they have two sons: Nathan and Samuel Amo-Ameyaw, who plays for Southampton FC.

title: Ana Cláudia Bolzan
text:
Ana Cláudia Bolzan e Silva, born on July 15, 1996, is a professional handball player representing both Sport Lisboa e Benfica and the Brazilian national handball team. Her primary position is left wing. While the article provides limited biographical detail, it highlights her accomplishments within the sport at both the club and international levels.

Bolzan has achieved success in club competitions, notably winning the Pan American Women's Club Handball Championship in 2017. This victory demonstrates her skill and contribution to a winning team on a continental scale. More recently, in 2022, she again demonstrated her competitive prowess by securing another championship title, this time at the South and Central American Women's Club Handball Championship. 

Her performance in the 2022 South and Central American Women's Club Handball Championship was particularly recognized. Beyond the team’s overall win, Bolzan was individually honored with selection to the All-Star team as the left wing, acknowledging her as one of the top players in that position throughout the tournament. This award signifies her consistently high level of play and impact on the game.

The article also points to Bolzan’s participation in major international events. Links are provided to profiles on the International Handball Federation website, Olympedia, and Olympics.com, and the Paris 2024 Summer Olympics website, indicating her involvement and recognition within the Olympic movement. The inclusion of a link to her Instagram profile suggests a degree of public profile and engagement. 

Although specific details about her career trajectory or personal life are not included in this brief overview, the provided information firmly establishes Ana Cláudia Bolzan e Silva as a significant figure in Brazilian handball, with a track record of success at both the club and potentially international level, and with ongoing participation in high-profile competitions such as the Olympics. Her achievements demonstrate a dedication to the sport and a consistent ability to perform at a high level, earning her both team victories and individual accolades.

title: Charles Allen (jurist)
text:
Charles Allen, born in Greenfield, Massachusetts on April 17, 1827, was a prominent American jurist with a long and distinguished legal career. He was the son of Sylvester and Harriet (Ripley) Allen, and his educational foundation began with attendance at Harvard University, from which he graduated in 1847. Following his university studies, Allen pursued a legal education and was admitted to the bar in 1850.

For the next twelve years, he practiced law in his hometown of Greenfield, establishing himself within the legal community. This period of private practice was followed by a move into public service, as he was appointed Attorney General of Massachusetts, a position he held from 1867 until 1872. This role marked a significant step in his career, demonstrating a growing recognition of his legal abilities and trustworthiness.

The most substantial portion of Allen’s career was spent on the Massachusetts Supreme Judicial Court, where he served for sixteen years, from 1882 to 1898. During this time, he gained a reputation as one of the most respected and influential judges of his era. The article notes that he became known as one of the most eminent jurists of his day, suggesting a profound impact on legal thought and practice within Massachusetts and potentially beyond.

Beyond his judicial duties, Allen also contributed to legal scholarship through his publications. He compiled *Allen's Reports*, a fourteen-volume collection spanning from 1861 to 1867. Later in his career, he published *Telegraph Cases* in 1900, and also ventured into a different field of study with *Notes on the Bacon-Shakespeare Question*, also published in 1900. These writings demonstrate a broad intellectual curiosity alongside his dedication to the law. 

Allen received an honorary degree, a Doctor of Laws (LL.D.), from Harvard University in 1892, acknowledging his contributions to the field. He passed away on January 13, 1913, leaving behind a legacy as a respected attorney general and a highly regarded justice. Sources documenting his life and career include biographical dictionaries and records from the Massachusetts General Court.

title: Cleopatra
text:
Cleopatra VII, the last active ruler of the Ptolemaic Kingdom of Egypt, reigned from 51 to 30 BC. Descended from Ptolemy I Soter, a companion of Alexander the Great, she was uniquely among her dynasty in learning the Egyptian language alongside Koine Greek and several others, including Latin, Hebrew, and Arabic. Her reign marked the end of the Hellenistic period, initiated by Alexander, as Egypt subsequently became a Roman province.

Born in Alexandria around 70/69 BC, Cleopatra inherited the throne alongside her brother Ptolemy XIII following their father Ptolemy XII Auletes’ death in 51 BC. A power struggle quickly erupted between them, leading to civil war. This conflict was dramatically impacted by the Roman civil war between Julius Caesar and Pompey. Pompey, having been defeated by Caesar at Pharsalus in 48 BC, fled to Egypt seeking refuge, but was betrayed and murdered by Ptolemy XIII’s forces. 

Caesar arrived in Alexandria and attempted to reconcile Cleopatra and Ptolemy XIII, but she was besieged in the palace by her brother’s troops.  After reinforcements arrived, Ptolemy XIII was defeated and killed in battle. Caesar then installed Cleopatra and her younger brother Ptolemy XIV as joint rulers, beginning a personal affair with Cleopatra that resulted in a son, Caesarion. Cleopatra visited Rome in 46 and 44 BC, residing in Caesar’s villa. Following Caesar’s assassination and the subsequent death of Ptolemy XIV – potentially orchestrated by Cleopatra – she named Caesarion as her co-ruler, Ptolemy XV.

During the ensuing power struggles in Rome, Cleopatra aligned herself with the Second Triumvirate consisting of Octavian, Mark Antony, and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus. A romantic relationship with Antony blossomed after their meeting in Tarsos in 41 BC, producing three children. Antony increasingly depended on Cleopatra for financial and military support in his campaigns, and he granted territories under his control to Cleopatra and their children in the Donations of Alexandria. 

Octavian used this as propaganda, accusing Antony of treason and declaring war on Cleopatra in 32 BC.  The conflict culminated in the Battle of Actium in 31 BC, where Octavian’s forces defeated Antony and Cleopatra’s fleet.  Octavian invaded Egypt in 30 BC, leading to Antony’s suicide.  Shortly after, Cleopatra reportedly took her own life, likely through poisoning, to avoid being paraded as a prisoner in Octavian’s Roman triumph.

Cleopatra’s legacy endures through art and literature, though early Roman accounts often portrayed her negatively.  She has been a subject of artistic representation throughout history, from Roman busts and coins to Renaissance paintings and modern films, becoming a prominent symbol of Egyptomania and enduring fascination. Her name, meaning “glory of her father,” was a common one in the Ptolemaic dynasty and Greek mythology.

title: Evgeny Shalunov
text:
Evgeny Vladimirovich Shalunov, born on January 8, 1992, is a retired professional bicycle racer from Russia, competing in both road and track cycling. He began his professional career mid-way through the 2011 season, initially joining Team RadioShack as a *stagiaire* – a temporary rider assessing a potential full contract – in July of that year. 

Prior to his signing with RadioShack, Shalunov had a successful run competing domestically with Lokomotiv–Urbycolan, achieving victory in eight national events throughout 2011. This success led to a contract with the Lokosphinx team for the 2012 season. His performance continued to improve, and in March 2012, he finished fourth in the French race, La Roue Tourangelle.

April 2012 marked a significant milestone in Shalunov’s career with his first victory in a UCI Europe Tour race: the Vuelta a La Rioja in Spain. The race saw him launch a solo attack approximately 30 kilometers from the finish line.
