Following a failed 1959 uprising, he fled to India and established a government-in-exile, the Central Tibetan Administration, initially in Mussoorie and later in Dharamsala, where he resided until relinquishing political leadership in 2011 in favor of a democratically elected government.

Central to the belief surrounding the Dalai Lamas is the concept of reincarnation as a Bodhisattva, specifically an emanation of Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva of Compassion. He is known by many names including Gyalwa Rinpoche, Kundun, and Yizhin Norbu, and is revered by followers as “His Holiness.” He belongs to the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism.

Born to a farming family in the Amdo region of Tibet, the search for his reincarnation began after the death of the 13th Dalai Lama. The process involved visions, omens, and the investigation of potential candidates, including a complex series of tests involving personal belongings of his predecessor. The search was complicated by political factors, particularly the involvement of the Chinese Nationalist government and the Hui Muslim warlord Ma Bufang, who controlled the region where the young Tenzin Gyatso was found.  Significant ransoms had to be paid to secure his journey to Lhasa. The Golden Urn selection process, typically used for confirming reincarnations, was waived with approval from the Nationalist government.

After assuming temporal duties at age 15 following the Battle of Chamdo and the annexation of Central Tibet, the Dalai Lama lived in Lhasa until his exile. Since the early 1970s, he has advocated for a “Middle Way Approach” to resolve the Tibetan issue with China, seeking autonomy within China rather than full independence, a policy democratically supported by Tibetans. He has openly criticized past CIA involvement in Tibet, stating it served American interests rather than Tibetan ones.

Throughout his life, the Dalai Lama travelled extensively, sharing Buddhist teachings and engaging in discussions with world leaders, scientists, and religious figures. While reducing travel since 2018, he continues to teach and address audiences remotely, focusing on issues like environmentalism, women’s rights, nonviolence, interfaith dialogue, and the intersection of Buddhism and science.

He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1989 and was hailed by *Time* magazine as the “spiritual heir to Gandhi.” The Asian Buddhist Conference for Peace also recognized his contributions, declaring July 6th as Universal Day of Compassion.  He passed his final Buddhist examinations in 1959, earning the highest academic degree in Buddhist philosophy. His early education included tutelage from prominent Tibetan lamas and, later, a friendship with Austrian mountaineer Heinrich Harrer, who served as a tutor and documented his life.

title: Christian Almeida
text:
Christian Almeida, born on December 25, 1989, is a Uruguayan professional footballer who currently plays as a left-back for River Plate. He began his senior career with Liverpool in Uruguay, playing for the club for six years. His first appearance for Liverpool came on August 13, 2011, in a match against Racing Club (M), and he went on to make four appearances during the 2011–12 Uruguayan Primera División season. 

Almeida remained with Liverpool for several years, accumulating a total of fifty-four appearances before finally scoring his first goal for the club in March 2015. This goal came in a 5–2 victory over Cerrito, but it was during a period where Liverpool was competing in the Uruguayan Segunda División, having been relegated from the Primera División in the 2013–14 season. Despite this relegation, Liverpool achieved success in the following season, winning the Segunda División championship in 2014–15 and securing immediate promotion back to the Primera División. Almeida also experienced continental competition with Liverpool, making his debut in the Copa Sudamericana in 2017 against Fluminense.

In January 2018, Almeida moved to Argentina to join Defensa y Justicia, a team in the Argentine Primera División. During his time there, he played in sixteen matches and scored two goals – one against Racing Club (A) and another against Mitre in a cup game. He left Defensa y Justicia in January 2019, signing with Belgrano. However, his time at Belgrano was marked by the team’s relegation to Primera B Nacional, and he departed after twelve months, in January 2020, to join Godoy Cruz.

Almeida then experienced a return to his former club, Liverpool, in October 2020, though this stint was brief, ending at the close of the year. He subsequently signed with Nacional on April 9, 2021. 

Throughout his career with Liverpool, Almeida achieved success, notably contributing to their championship win in the Segunda División during the 2014–15 season, earning the club promotion. As of July 6, 2020, detailed career statistics are available, though the article does not specify these numbers.

title: Vicente Carrillo Fuentes
text:
Vicente Carrillo Fuentes, known as El Viceroy, was a prominent Mexican drug lord and the former head of the Juárez Cartel, a major organization responsible for transporting drugs into the United States. Born in Sinaloa, Mexico in 1962, he was one of eight children, including brothers who played key roles in the cartel’s development. His uncle was also a significant figure in the drug trade. The Juárez Cartel was founded by his brother, Amado Carrillo Fuentes, and Vicente rose to leadership after Amado’s death in 1997 following a power struggle.

During his time leading the cartel, Vicente formed alliances with various individuals including Juan José Esparragoza Moreno, his brother Rodolfo, his nephew Vicente Carrillo Leyva, and the Beltrán Leyva brothers. He navigated a complex landscape of rival cartels, particularly the Arellano Félix organization and, later, the Sinaloa Cartel led by Joaquín Guzmán Loera. A period of conflict with the Sinaloa Cartel ensued, including retaliatory assassinations, but was temporarily paused due to the Sinaloa Cartel’s war with the Gulf Cartel. Internal divisions also plagued the Juárez Cartel, separating those loyal to the Carrillo family from those aligning with Esparragoza Moreno and the Sinaloa Cartel. 

The cartel experienced significant pressure from law enforcement, particularly with the “House of Death” case, though it was hampered by corruption within the investigating teams. By the late 2000s, the Juárez Cartel had diminished in power, and in 2008, escalating violence prompted military intervention in Ciudad Juárez. 

Carrillo Fuentes faced a 46-count indictment in the United States, including charges of drug trafficking, money laundering, and ordering murders. A reward of up to $5 million was offered for information leading to his arrest. In 2000, he was sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department under the Kingpin Act, freezing his assets and prohibiting U.S. businesses from interacting with him.

He was ultimately arrested in 2014 in Torreón, Coahuila, Mexico and sentenced to 28 years in prison by a Mexican court in 2021. Finally, on February 27, 2025, he was extradited to the United States, where he pleaded not guilty to charges of running a criminal enterprise the following day. His life and the activities of the Juárez Cartel have been depicted in television series like "El Chapo" and "Narcos: Mexico".

title: Hu Qili
text:
Hu Qili, born in 1929 in Shaanxi Province, is a former high-ranking official of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) who rose to prominence as a proponent of economic reform in the 1980s. He joined the CCP in 1948 and initially focused on political studies after the founding of the People’s Republic of China in 1949, having begun his education in physics. His early career involved significant roles within the Communist Youth League, serving as secretary of its Peking University Committee and later as president of the All-China Students’ Federation. He even had an audience with Mao Zedong in 1958.

During the Cultural Revolution, Hu was sent to work at the lower levels of May Seventh Cadre Schools. Following this period, he held various leadership positions, including deputy president of Tsinghua University and party secretary and mayor of Tianjin between 1980 and 1982. He steadily climbed the ranks of the CCP, becoming a member of the Politburo and Secretariat in 1982, and a leading member of the CCP Secretariat from 1985 to 1989.  His ascent culminated in a position on the Politburo Standing Committee from 1987 to 1989, positioning him as a potential future General Secretary.

Hu’s political career was dramatically impacted by the Tiananmen Square protests of 1989.  Aligned with General Secretary Zhao Ziyang, he advocated for dialogue with the student protestors and a policy of openness and tolerance in reporting on the movement. He publicly expressed belief that the students were acting reasonably and that accurate information should be provided to them.  He and Zhao Ziyang were the only two members of the Politburo Standing Committee to oppose the implementation of martial law. This opposition led to his purge from the party following the June 1989 plenum, where he and several others were stripped of their posts.

However, Hu made a return to government in 1991, serving as vice minister of the Ministry of the Machine-Building and Electronics Industry. He later became Minister of the same ministry from 1993 to 1998. He was then elected vice chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference in 1998, tasked with restoring political treatment for party and state leaders.  Finally, he became chairman of the Soong Ching-ling Foundation in 2001, a role he held until his retirement in 2016, focusing on Chinese charities and welfare projects. As of April 2024, Hu Qili is the sole surviving member of the 13th Politburo Standing Committee from the first three plenary sessions.

title: Arthur Wakefield
text:
Arthur Wakefield was born in Essex, England, in 1799, the son of a surveyor and land agent and part of a large family. He began his career in the Royal Navy at the age of eleven, serving extensively throughout the following decades. He participated in conflicts in the Dutch East Indies and during the War of 1812, including the capture of Washington D.C., and was involved in the bombardment of Algiers and anti-slavery patrols off West Africa. He eventually commanded his own steam frigate, the Rhadamanthus, but resigned from the Navy in 1841 after being passed over for promotion.

Following his naval career, Wakefield was recruited by his brother, Edward Gibbon Wakefield, to join the New Zealand Company. He was tasked with selecting settlers, escorting them to New Zealand, and overseeing the development of a new settlement named Nelson. He arrived in Wellington in September 1841, with the first immigrant ships reaching Nelson in February 1842. The initial stages of the settlement were successful, with over 3,000 colonists arriving within the first two years. Wakefield worked to promote the colony's orderly growth, earning respect from many of the settlers.

However, the Nelson settlement soon faced substantial difficulties, primarily due to a severe shortage of arable land. The New Zealand Company had promised settlers generous land allocations – including urban, suburban, and rural plots – but lacked the ability to deliver on these promises.  Negotiations with the Māori, the native inhabitants, for land purchases proved difficult, as they were reluctant to sell and distrustful of the company. The colonial government, under Governor Hobson, also offered little support.  This conflict arose from differing views on land ownership, with some colonists believing they were entitled to the land and dismissing Māori claims.

These tensions culminated in the Wairau Affray in 1843.  A dispute arose over the Wairau Plains, which the Māori chiefs Te Rauparaha and Te Rangihaeata had made clear they would not allow settlers to occupy. Despite this, Wakefield and the Chief Magistrate, Henry Thompson, sent out surveyors, who were peacefully escorted off the land by Māori and their hut burned. Thompson then issued an arrest warrant for the two chiefs, and, along with Wakefield, led a group to execute it.  The resulting confrontation led to the deaths of Wakefield and 21 others. It is believed Thompson instigated the arrest, but Wakefield was in command and failed to heed his brother's warnings about the invalid land claim.  Following a clash and surrender, Wakefield and others were executed by Te Rangihaeata, reportedly in revenge for the death of his daughter.

A subsequent government inquiry found the expedition illegal and cleared the Māori of wrongdoing, a decision that angered the colonists and contributed to the recall of Governor FitzRoy.  Today, Fort Arthur, once located where Nelson’s cathedral now stands, commemorates the period. The town of Wakefield, located south of Nelson, was renamed shortly before his death, and the Arthur Range in Kahurangi National Park is named in his honor.

title: Sheldon T. Mills
text:
Sheldon Tibbetts Mills, born in Seattle, Washington on August 13, 1904, and passing away in Santa Barbara, California on July 15, 1988, dedicated his life to a career in the United States Foreign Service. He served as a diplomat with the U.S. Department of State for 32 years, from 1928 until his retirement in 1961. His path to this career began with a Bachelor of Arts degree from Reed College in Portland, Oregon, in 1927, followed by preparation for the rigorous Foreign Service exams under the tutelage of Angus Crawford, a prominent instructor of the time. He successfully passed the exams and was commissioned as a Foreign Service Officer in December 1928. He furthered his education with a detail to Harvard University from 1939 to 1940 to study Economics.

Throughout his career, Mills held postings in a variety of countries, including Bolivia, Panama, Romania, Chile, India, and Brazil. He reached the level of United States Ambassador on three occasions. First, he served as Ambassador to Ecuador from 1954 to 1956. He then moved to Afghanistan, holding the ambassadorship there from 1956 to 1959, where he cultivated a strong rapport with King Mohammad Zahir. This relationship proved valuable to both nations, and the King was later able to return to Afghanistan after years in exile. Notably, during Mills’ time in Afghanistan, the country uniquely received economic development support from both the United States and the Soviet Union, despite the prevailing Cold War tensions. Finally, Mills was appointed as the United States Ambassador to Jordan from 1959 to 1961. 

In Jordan, he established a positive connection with King Hussein, strengthening the relationship between the two countries. A significant moment during his tenure involved a conversation with King Hussein in early 1960, where the King expressed his belief that the long-held Arab aspiration to eliminate Israel should be abandoned, advocating for a pragmatic approach to a final settlement between Israel and the Arab nations.

Mills came from a family with deep roots in American history and prominent figures. His father, Harry Edward Mills, was a Protestant minister and poet, while his mother, Mary Brewster Tibbetts Mills, was a descendant of William Brewster, a passenger on the Mayflower. He married Francesca Dekum in 1932, the daughter of a hardware businessman and a woman whose family also boasted a long American lineage. They had three daughters together. Following his retirement from the Foreign Service, Mills remained engaged in international affairs, becoming an active member of several organizations, including the Channel City Club, the Cosmopolitan Club, the Council on Foreign Relations, the American Foreign Service Association, and Diplomatic and Consular Officials, Retired. He also continued to share his insights through op-ed articles published in local newspapers.

title: Joseph A. Lopez
text:
José Antonio López, later known as Joseph Anton Lopez, was born in Cotija, Michoacán, Mexico in 1779 and died in St. Inigoes, Maryland in 1841. He was a Catholic priest and Jesuit who lived a life deeply intertwined with the political upheaval of early 19th-century Mexico and later, the development of American higher education. He received a bachelor’s degree in canon law from the Royal and Pontifical University of Mexico after studying at the Colegio de San Nicolás. Early in his career, he served as a local priest in Peribán, Michoacán, and even attempted to arrest Miguel Hidalgo during the Mexican War of Independence, an effort that ultimately led him to flee.

López became closely associated with Agustín de Iturbide, initially through his connection to Iturbide’s wife, Ana María Huarte. He served as chaplain to Iturbide’s army and later as a tutor to his children, eventually being placed in charge of the education of all the Mexican princes. He developed a curriculum for their education, reflecting a preference for a strong monarchy. Following Iturbide’s downfall and subsequent exile, López remained a loyal ally, accompanying the former emperor and his family to Italy and England. He even participated in a failed attempt to restore Iturbide to power in Mexico in 1824.

After Iturbide's execution, López accompanied the Empress consort and her children to the United States, settling in Washington, D.C. He became chaplain at the Georgetown Visitation Monastery and, in 1833, joined the Society of Jesus, working as a novice and minister at Georgetown College. He anglicized his name to Joseph Anton Lopez during this time. He held several positions at Georgetown, including librarian, and in 1840, he was appointed acting president, becoming the first Latin American to lead a university in the United States. He was known for his strict disciplinary approach. 

His presidency was short-lived, lasting only a few months before illness forced him to seek recuperation in St. Inigoes, Maryland, where he died in October 1841. He famously predicted the day of his death, and was buried in Chapel Field before being reinterred in the cemetery adjoining St. Ignatius Church in the same village. His life represents a bridge between the political turmoil of post-colonial Mexico and the burgeoning American educational landscape.

title: Vishal (actor)
text:
Vishal Krishna Reddy, known professionally as Vishal, is a prominent Indian actor and film producer working primarily in the Tamil film industry. Born on August 29, 1977, in Chennai, he comes from a family with a background in the film industry; his parents are businesspeople and film producers, and his elder brother is also involved in film production. He holds a degree in visual communications from Loyola College, Chennai.

Vishal began his career as an assistant director to Arjun, and transitioned into acting with his debut role in the 2004 romantic thriller *Chellamae*. He quickly gained recognition through action films like *Sandakozhi*, *Thimiru*, *Thaamirabharani*, and *Malaikottai*, establishing himself as a rising action hero. Recognizing a need for creative control, he founded Vishal Film Factory, his own production company, and has since produced films like *Pandiya Naadu*, *Naan Sigappu Manithan*, and *Poojai*, often starring in them as well.

Throughout his career, Vishal has taken on diverse roles. He portrayed a village stage actor in *Avan Ivan* (2011), a performance praised for its depth, and frequently played police officers, such as in *Sathyam* and *Vedi*. While some of his films garnered significant commercial success, like *Thaamirabharani* and *Thupparivaalan*, others, like *Sathyam* and *Thoranai*, underperformed. He ventured into Malayalam cinema with a villainous role in *Villain* (2017).

Beyond acting and producing, Vishal has been involved in industry organizations, serving as General Secretary of the Nadigar Sangam and later as President of the Tamil Film Producers Council. He's also a vocal advocate against online piracy, having established an anti-piracy cell in 2014. His recent projects include *Mark Antony* (2023), which became his highest-grossing film to date, surpassing 100 crore worldwide, and *Rathnam* (2024). 

In his personal life, Vishal announced his relationship with actress Sai Dhanshika and plans to marry her on his 48th birthday in 2025. He has faced legal issues, including an arrest for attempting to enter the Tamil Film Producers Council office. He has received the Kalaimamani award for his contributions to Tamil cinema and won the SIIMA Best Debutant Producer Award for *Pandiya Naadu*. He also ventured into television hosting with *Sun Naam Oruvar* in 2018.

title: Andry Rajoelina
text:
Andry Rajoelina, born in 1974 in Antsirabe, Madagascar, is a politician and businessman who has twice served as President of Madagascar, first in a transitional role from 2009 to 2014 and again since 2019. Before entering politics, Rajoelina developed a career in the private sector, founding a printing and advertising company, Injet, in 1999 and later acquiring the Viva radio and television networks in 2007. He entered politics by forming the political association Tanora malaGasy Vonona (TGV) and was elected Mayor of Antananarivo in 2007, capitalizing on a desire for younger leaders.

His mayoral term was marked by conflict with then-President Marc Ravalomanana, stemming from issues like advertising regulations and escalating with controversies surrounding large-scale land leases and the purchase of a presidential jet. Rajoelina led an opposition movement, and in 2009, following a series of protests and a military intervention after violence resulting in multiple deaths, he was installed as President of the High Transitional Authority (HTA) by the military, a move widely condemned internationally as a coup d'état. As President of the HTA, he dissolved the Senate and National Assembly and implemented governance through decrees and new structures.

During his transitional leadership, Rajoelina faced international isolation, including frozen aid and sanctions. He oversaw a constitutional referendum in 2010, which established the Fourth Republic and altered presidential eligibility requirements. Following elections in 2013 – in which neither he nor Ravalomanana were permitted to run – he stepped down in 2014. He subsequently won the 2018 presidential election and was inaugurated in January 2019. 

His more recent presidency has included navigating the COVID-19 pandemic, during which he promoted unproven treatments, and responding to a food security crisis and Cyclone Batsirai. He was re-elected in the 2023 presidential election. Throughout his career, Rajoelina has faced accusations of authoritarian tendencies, including dissolving legislative bodies and pursuing legal action against political opponents. His family background includes a father who served in the French army, and he married Mialy Razakandisa in 2000, with whom he has three children. His rise to power represents a trend toward younger leadership in Madagascar, though it has been consistently accompanied by political turmoil and international scrutiny.

title: James Franco
text:
James Franco, born in Palo Alto, California in 1978, is an American actor and filmmaker who rose to prominence through a diverse career spanning television and film. His parents, Betsy Lou Verne, a children’s book author, and Douglas Eugene Franco, a business owner, fostered an academic and largely secular upbringing for Franco and his two younger brothers, both of whom became actors. Despite early struggles with the law, including arrests for underage drinking and theft, Franco excelled academically and briefly interned at Lockheed Martin. He initially considered marine zoology but ultimately pursued acting, dropping out of UCLA after a year to dedicate himself to the craft. He supported himself with a job at McDonald’s while training with Robert Carnegie.

Franco’s breakthrough role came with the short-lived but critically acclaimed television series *Freaks and Geeks* in 1999. He followed this with the title role in the 2001 biographical film *James Dean*, winning a Golden Globe Award for his performance. He gained wider recognition in 2002 with his portrayal of Harry Osborn in Sam Raimi’s *Spider-Man*, a role he reprised in two sequels. 

Throughout the 2000s and 2010s, Franco appeared in a prolific number of films, including *Milk* (2008), *Eat Pray Love* (2010), *Rise of the Planet of the Apes* (2011), *Spring Breakers* (2012), and *Oz the Great and Powerful* (2013). He frequently collaborated with Seth Rogen, starring together in films like *Pineapple Express* (2008), *This Is the End* (2013), and *The Disaster Artist* (2017), for which Franco won another Golden Globe. His performance in *127 Hours* (2010) garnered him an Academy Award nomination. He also took on recurring television roles in *General Hospital* (2009-2012) and *The Deuce* (2017-2019).

However, Franco’s career was significantly impacted by allegations of sexual misconduct. In 2014, screenshots of messages surfaced showing Franco attempting to meet a 17-year-old girl, and in 2018, *The Los Angeles Times* reported accusations from five women alleging inappropriate behavior during his time as an acting teacher or mentor. A subsequent lawsuit filed by former students alleging sexual harassment and fraud was settled in 2021 for $2.2 million.

title: George VI
text:
George VI, born Albert Frederick Arthur George in 1895, became King of the United Kingdom and the Dominions of the British Commonwealth in December 1936, and remained so until his death in 1952. He was also the last Emperor of India until 1947 and the first Head of the Commonwealth in 1949. Named after his great-grandfather Prince Albert, he was known as “Bertie” within the family. As the second son of George V, he wasn’t initially expected to become king, living in the shadow of his elder brother, Edward.

Albert received a naval education and served in both the Royal Navy and Royal Air Force during World War I, later becoming Duke of York in 1920. He married Lady Elizabeth Bowes-Lyon in 1923, with whom he had two daughters, Elizabeth and Margaret. He notably worked to overcome a lifelong stutter with the help of speech therapist Lionel Logue. The unexpected abdication of his brother, Edward VIII, in 1936, following a desire to marry Wallis Simpson, thrust Albert onto the throne, at which point he chose the regnal name George VI.

George VI’s reign coincided with World War II, beginning in 1939. He became a symbol of national resilience during the conflict, sharing in the hardships of the British people, even as Buckingham Palace was bombed. His younger brother, the Duke of Kent, was also killed during the war. Britain’s victory in 1945 was followed by a period of significant imperial decline, with Ireland largely breaking away and India and Pakistan gaining independence in 1947. This led to George relinquishing the title of Emperor of India and becoming Head of the Commonwealth. 

Throughout his life, George faced various challenges. As a child, he was often unwell and prone to shyness. His education included overcoming a natural left-handedness and dealing with physical ailments. Though he enjoyed sports like tennis, his stutter and lack of confidence initially hindered his public appearances. He and Elizabeth toured extensively throughout the Commonwealth, including a visit to Australia and New Zealand where he demonstrated a progressive attitude by playing tennis with a Black man.

His accession to the throne was unexpected and initially met with some doubt. He navigated the complex situation surrounding his brother’s abdication, including settling his titles and purchasing royal residences. His coronation in 1937 was a significant event, supported by his mother, Queen Mary. Ultimately, George VI’s reign was marked by duty and dedication, guiding Britain through wartime and the beginnings of a changing world. He died in 1952 at Sandringham House, aged 56, from a coronary thrombosis, and was succeeded by his elder daughter, Elizabeth II.

title: Lisa Ling
text:
Lisa Ling is an American journalist and television personality born in Sacramento, California, in 1973. Her mother is a Taiwanese immigrant and her father is from Hong Kong, with familial roots tracing back to Guangzhou, China and Malaysia. Ling’s father opened the first Chinese restaurant in Folsom, California after facing difficulties finding work upon immigrating to the United States. She admired journalist Connie Chung from a young age and aspired to a career in journalism. Following her parents’ divorce when she was seven, Ling was raised in Carmichael, California, with her sister Laura. She attended the University of Southern California but left before graduating to begin her career. She is fluent in Spanish.

Ling began her television career on a teen magazine show and quickly rose to prominence as a reporter and anchor for Channel One News, covering assignments including the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan. In 1999, she joined the daytime talk show *The View*, landing the position after auditioning against 12,000 other candidates. While on the show, she notably got a navel piercing which one of the hosts disapproved of, and aimed to provoke thought with her commentary, even after the September 11th attacks, where she questioned the motivations behind the attacks. She left *The View* after three and a half years to return to international reporting.

From 2003 to 2010, Ling hosted *National Geographic Explorer*, covering topics such as the drug war in Colombia, the MS-13 gang, and the culture of U.S. prisons. She also gained rare access to North Korea with a medical missionary group, which she documented in a National Geographic documentary. Following this, she became a special correspondent for *The Oprah Winfrey Show*, reporting on a wide range of investigative pieces, including issues in India, the Congo, and Uganda, as well as domestic stories like the Virginia Tech Massacre and Hurricane Katrina.

Ling later hosted *Our America with Lisa Ling* on the Oprah Winfrey Network from 2011 to 2014, winning an Emmy Award for the show. She then hosted the CNN documentary series *This Is Life with Lisa Ling* from 2014 to 2022, until the series was cancelled. In 2019, she signed an overall deal with HBO Max, with her first project being a documentary series called *Take Out* exploring Asian American takeout restaurants. Currently, as of 2023, Ling is a news contributor for CBS News. 

Ling is also a published author, co-writing *Somewhere Inside* with her sister Laura, detailing Laura’s detention in North Korea. Her sister Laura is also a journalist, and the pair experienced a harrowing ordeal when Laura and a colleague were detained in North Korea in 2009, eventually being released after a visit from Bill Clinton. Ling identifies as a feminist and was diagnosed with attention deficit disorder at age 40. She is married to radiation oncologist Paul Song, and they have two daughters and reside in Santa Monica, California.

title: Generoso Rossi
text:
Generoso Rossi, born on January 3, 1979, is an Italian former professional footballer who played as a goalkeeper throughout his career. He began his professional journey with A.S. Bari, experiencing loan spells with Serie C1 teams before returning to Bari in 2000, where he eventually made his Serie A debut against Verona on September 30th of the same year.

His career took a turn in January 2001 with a transfer to Venezia, which was quickly followed by a move to Palermo as a result of a change in ownership, with Maurizio Zamparini acquiring both clubs. Rossi then spent time on loan with U.S. Lecce and ultimately signed with A.C. Siena in the summer of 2003.

A significant setback occurred when Rossi was banned from football due to involvement in a betting scandal. After serving the ban, he resumed his career in January 2005, signing an 18-month contract with Queens Park Rangers. He then moved to Triestina in the summer of 2005. 

In January 2008, Rossi joined Calcio Catania on loan in a swap deal involving Babu. At Catania, he served as the third-choice goalkeeper, positioned behind Ciro Polito and Albano Bizarri, and ahead of Raffaele Ioime. The following season, in 2008/2009, he transferred to Gallipoli in Lega Pro Prima Divisione – B. Although Gallipoli achieved promotion to Serie B, financial difficulties within the club led to Rossi’s departure.

Rossi found a relatively stable period with Sorrento, joining them in February 2010 and remaining for two and a half seasons. He became a key player for the team, which narrowly missed promotion to Serie B on two occasions. Following the resignation of Sorrento’s president and uncertainty surrounding the club's future in the summer of 2012, Rossi left to pursue other opportunities. However, after a period without a club, he was re-signed by Sorrento on a free contract in November 2012.

Beyond his club career, Rossi also represented Italy at the youth level. He participated in the Toulon Tournament for Italy in 2000 and was selected for the under-21 squad during the 2002 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship. 

He achieved one notable honour during his time with Sorrento, winning the Lega Pro Prima Divisione title in 2009.

title: Idi Amin
text:
Idi Amin Dada Oumee, born around 1928, served as the third president of Uganda from 1971 to 1979, ruling as a brutal military dictator. His early life is shrouded in conflicting accounts, with birthdates ranging from 1925 to 1928. He was born to a Kakwa father and a Lugbara mother, and his early years were spent moving between family and various locations due to his parents’ circumstances. Amin joined the British Colonial Army’s King’s African Rifles in 1946 as a cook and steadily rose through the ranks, participating in conflicts in Kenya against Somali rebels and the Mau Mau uprising.

Following Uganda’s independence in 1962, Amin continued his military career, becoming Deputy Army Commander in 1964 and full commander two years later. He eventually launched a coup d'état in 1971, seizing power from President Milton Obote after learning of a planned arrest for misappropriating army funds. Initially presenting himself as a temporary caretaker, Amin quickly declared himself president, establishing a military government and suspending the constitution. 

Amin’s rule was marked by dramatic shifts in international alliances. He initially enjoyed support from Western nations and Israel but later aligned himself with Libya’s Muammar Gaddafi, Zaire’s Mobutu Sese Seko, and the Soviet Union. A controversial expulsion of Ugandan Asians in 1972, the majority of whom were Indian-Ugandans, led to a severing of diplomatic relations with India. Despite widespread human rights abuses, Amin briefly held the chairmanship of the Organisation of African Unity in 1975 and Uganda was a member of the United Nations Commission on Human Rights until 1979. 

The late 1970s saw increasing unrest in Uganda due to Amin’s persecution of ethnic groups and political dissidents, and his support for hijackers involved in the 1976 hijacking incidents. This culminated in Israel’s Operation Entebbe. Further escalating tensions, Amin attempted to annex Tanzania’s Kagera Region in 1978, prompting a Tanzanian invasion led by President Julius Nyerere. Tanzanian forces and Ugandan rebels successfully captured Kampala in 1979, ending Amin's rule. He fled into exile, spending time in Libya and Iraq before settling in Saudi Arabia, where he died in 2003.

Amin’s presidency was characterized by widespread human rights violations, including political repression, extrajudicial killings, nepotism, corruption, and severe economic mismanagement. Estimates of the number of people killed under his regime range from 100,000 to 500,000. His military background and athletic prowess – he was a Ugandan boxing champion – were notable, but overshadowed by the brutality and chaos of his rule. He skillfully used a blend of direct leadership and connections built during his military service to gain initial popularity, though it ultimately dissipated amidst the violence and instability of his dictatorship.

title: Mike Adenuga
text:
Michael Adenuga Jr., born April 29, 1953, is a Nigerian businessman currently ranked as the fifth richest person in Africa, with Forbes estimating his net worth at $6.7 billion as of May 2024. He is primarily known as the owner of Globacom, Nigeria’s second-largest telecommunications company, which also operates in Ghana and Benin. Beyond telecoms, Adenuga holds significant stakes in Equitorial Trust Bank and the oil exploration company, Conoil, originally known as Consolidated Oil Company.

Adenuga’s background reflects a blend of educational and entrepreneurial pursuits. His father was a schoolteacher, and his mother a businesswoman with royal lineage from the Ijebu people of Nigeria. He identifies as Yoruba. He completed his secondary education at Ibadan Grammar School and Comprehensive High School, Aiyetoro, and financed his university studies, in part, by working as a taxi driver. He ultimately earned degrees in Business Administration from Northwestern Oklahoma State University and Pace University in New York.

His entrepreneurial journey began early, achieving his first million dollars by the age of 26 in 1979 through trading lace and distributing soft drinks. A pivotal moment came in 1991 when his company, Consolidated Oil, discovered oil in commercial quantities in the shallow waters off Southwestern Ondo State, marking the first time an indigenous Nigerian company had achieved this. 

Adenuga’s entry into the telecommunications sector involved navigating regulatory hurdles. Initially granted a GSM license in 1999, it was later revoked, but he successfully re-acquired one during a subsequent government auction in 2003. This led to the establishment of Globacom as a major player in the Nigerian telecom market. His success in the industry was recognized in 2007 when he was named African Entrepreneur of the Year at the African Telecoms Awards. In 2015, he attempted to expand his telecom interests further with a $600 million bid to purchase Comium Côte d'Ivoire, a mobile operator in Ivory Coast.

Adenuga has received numerous honors acknowledging his contributions to business and society. In 2012, the Nigerian government conferred upon him the title of Grand Commander of the Order of the Niger. He also holds the Yoruba chieftaincy title of “Otunba Apesin” within the Ijebu clan. Further international recognition came in 2018 when President Emmanuel Macron of France decorated him with the insignia of a Commander of the Legion of Honour. In 2019, *New African* magazine included him in its list of the Top 100 most influential Africans.

title: Danny Almonte
text:
Danny Almonte Rojas, born in Moca, Dominican Republic on April 7, 1987, became a baseball sensation in 2001 as a Little League pitcher for a team from the Bronx, New York. He quickly gained attention for his fastball, reaching speeds of 76 mph – equivalent to a 102 mph major league pitch – and earned the nickname “Little Unit” due to his resemblance to Randy Johnson. Almonte led his team, nicknamed the “Baby Bombers,” to a third-place finish in the 2001 Little League World Series, highlighted by a perfect game against Florida. They were celebrated with honors from the New York Yankees and the city of New York.

However, questions arose regarding Almonte’s age, fueled by his size and pitching prowess. Rumors circulated that he was older than the Little League age limit of 12. Investigations by other teams and Little League officials initially found no evidence of wrongdoing, with league president Rolando Paulino vehemently defending Almonte’s birthdate. The truth emerged when *Sports Illustrated* reporters discovered a birth certificate in Moca registering Almonte’s birth in 1987, meaning he was 14 during the 2001 series. This contradicted a later-registered birth certificate claiming a 1989 birthdate, which his mother maintained was accurate.

Further investigation revealed that witnesses associated with the 1989 birth certificate denied its validity. Dominican officials ultimately confirmed Almonte’s 1987 birthdate. As a result, the Baby Bombers were forced to forfeit their wins, and Almonte was declared ineligible. His father, Felipe, was banned from Little League competition for life, and Paulino also received a lifetime ban due to his responsibility for player eligibility. Criminal charges were filed against Felipe for falsifying the birth certificate, though Danny was cleared of any wrongdoing, having been unaware of the deception.

Following the scandal, Almonte remained in New York, becoming the ward of Rolando Paulino. He continued to play baseball, appearing in a championship game for Public Schools Athletic League in 2004. He briefly played for the Southern Illinois Miners in the Frontier League in 2007, but was released after six appearances. He then attended and excelled at Western Oklahoma State College, demonstrating skill as both a pitcher and a hitter. A sore arm eventually forced him to abandon pitching, and he transitioned to playing outfield in semi-pro leagues. By 2010, he was working as a volunteer assistant baseball coach at his high school in the Bronx, acknowledging his professional baseball aspirations had diminished. 

In 2006, Almonte married Rosy Perdomo, who was 30 at the time of their wedding, when Almonte was 18. Throughout the ordeal and beyond, the controversy surrounding his age significantly impacted his baseball career and public image.

title: Balázs Bekő

Bekő’s managerial career has involved working with teams within the Hungarian football league system, specifically at the top tier level known as the Nemzeti Bajnokság I. His first documented head coaching role at this level began on June 24, 2013, when he was appointed to lead Kecskeméti TE. This marked a significant step in his career, placing him in charge of a club competing in Hungary’s highest football division. 

Following his time with Kecskeméti TE, Bekő continued to progress as a manager, securing another head coaching position within the Nemzeti Bajnokság I. title: Andy Middleton
text:
Andy Middleton, born May 22, 1962, is an American jazz saxophonist proficient in both tenor and soprano saxophone. He has collaborated with numerous prominent musicians throughout his career, including Ralph Towner, Dave Holland, Kenny Wheeler, and Renee Rosnes. His musical journey began in Harrisburg, Pennsylvania, where he started playing the alto saxophone at the age of nine, nurtured by a musical family.

Middleton’s formal education included studies at the University of Rochester (1980-1982) and the University of Miami (1982-1987). A pivotal experience was his attendance at the Banff Centre in Alberta, Canada in 1985 and 1986, where he connected with influential figures like Steve Coleman, John Abercrombie, Richie Beirach, and David Liebman. In 1987, he relocated to the New York City area and became involved with several big bands, including those led by Bob Mintzer and Lionel Hampton – the latter of which recorded a composition he co-wrote with his brother, Rob Middleton, titled “Two Brothers.” He also performed with the Maria Schneider Jazz Orchestra. 

Throughout his career, Middleton led his own quartet, which featured a rotating roster of musicians including Ben Monder, John Hollenbeck, Scott Colley, Henry Hey, and others. He released his debut album, *Acid Rain*, in 1991 on Owl Records. *Terra Infirma* followed in 1995, produced by David Liebman and released by EMI France. He also co-led the group The Fensters, recording two albums, *Jazz Music, Vol. 1* (1992) and *Jazz Music, Vol. X* (1996). Later albums as a leader included *Nomad’s Notebook* (1999) with Ralph Towner and Dave Holland, and *Reinventing the World* (2003) featuring Kenny Wheeler and Nils Wogram.

Middleton has also contributed as a sideman to recordings by artists such as Lionel Hampton, Maria Schneider, and Stefan ‘Pista’ Bartus. In 2006, he moved to Vienna, Austria, to take a teaching position at the Music and Arts University of the City of Vienna.

Throughout his career, Middleton has received several accolades, including an Outstanding Jazz Soloist award from *DownBeat* magazine in 1987, and first prize awards for both best soloist and best arranger at the 13th Europ’ Jazz Contest in Belgium in 1991. He has also been a recipient of grants from organizations like the National Endowment for the Arts, the Brooklyn Arts Council, and Chamber Music America, supporting his work and performances.

title: Anderson Silva
text:
Anderson Silva, born in São Paulo, Brazil in 1975, is a highly regarded mixed martial artist and boxer. He is best known for his reign as UFC Middleweight Champion, holding the record for the longest title defense in UFC history at 2,457 days, spanning from 2006 to 2013, during which he achieved 16 consecutive victories. He departed the UFC in 2020 and subsequently returned to professional boxing, and was inducted into the UFC Hall of Fame in July 2023.

Silva’s early life was marked by poverty, leading him to be raised primarily by his aunt and uncle in Curitiba. He began martial arts training in jiu-jitsu as a child and later expanded his skills to include taekwondo, capoeira, and muay thai. He began his professional MMA career in 1997, initially competing in the welterweight division, achieving a nine-fight winning streak after an early loss to Luiz Azeredo. He found success in Japan, becoming the Shooto Middleweight Champion in 2001 by defeating the previously undefeated Hayato Sakurai. 

Silva’s career included stints with PRIDE Fighting Championships and Cage Rage. He was originally scheduled to fight Matt Hughes in the UFC in 2002, but instead chose to compete in PRIDE. While achieving some notable wins, including a victory over Carlos Newton with a memorable flying knee, he also experienced setbacks, notably a submission loss to Daiju Takase, which initially led him to consider retirement. He later joined Brazilian Top Team and continued to compete in various promotions. In Cage Rage, he became a champion, defending the title against Curtis Stout and Tony Fryklund. A controversial disqualification loss to Yushin Okami in Hawaii, due to an illegal kick, further punctuated this period.

In 2006, Silva signed with the Ultimate Fighting Championship. He made a spectacular debut, defeating Chris Leben by knockout in under a minute. This earned him a title shot against Rich Franklin, which he won by TKO in the first round, becoming the UFC Middleweight Champion. He then embarked on a dominant championship run, defending his title multiple times against opponents like Travis Lutter, Nate Marquardt, and a rematch with Franklin. He also briefly competed in the Light Heavyweight division, defeating James Irvin and Forrest Griffin. 

Throughout his championship reign, Silva's performances were sometimes marked by periods of showboating and taunting opponents, drawing criticism from Dana White and fans alike, as seen in fights against Demian Maia. Despite these controversies, he remained a dominant force, consistently showcasing his striking prowess and finishing ability. His reign eventually ended after a loss to Chris Weidman in 2013, and a subsequent rematch also ended in defeat. He continued to fight in the UFC until 2020, experiencing mixed results, before transitioning back to boxing.

title: Phillip Gillespie
text:
Phillip J. Gillespie, born on October 23, 1975, in Frankston, Victoria, Australia, is an Australian cricket umpire who previously played the sport. He currently serves as a member of the Australian National Umpire Panel. Gillespie’s path to umpiring began after a series of injuries – to his Achilles tendon, jaw, and knee – sustained while playing for the Rowville Cricket Club in Melbourne forced him to find another way to remain involved in cricket. He started his umpiring career in the Victorian Premier Cricket competition in 2009.

His first List A match was in February 2013, officiating a game between the England Lions and Victoria, and he went on to umpire eight matches in the Matador BBQs One-Day Cup. He also officiated in women’s cricket, including two Women’s National Cricket League matches, notably the semi-final between New South Wales and Victoria in 2015. Gillespie was involved in the Big Bash League, umpiring six matches in the 2015–16 season and four more the following season. He began umpiring women’s Twenty20 matches during the 2012–13 Australian Women's Twenty20 Cup, and stood in a Women’s Big Bash League semi-final in the 2016–17 season, a match between the Sydney Sixers and the Hobart Hurricanes.

Gillespie’s first-class debut occurred on February 15, 2015, in a Sheffield Shield match between New South Wales and Victoria, a game remembered for Doug Bollinger’s hat-trick from Gillespie’s end of the pitch. He subsequently umpired nine further first-class matches, with his most recent being a clash between Tasmania and Queensland in March 2017. 

He made his international umpiring debut in 2014 during the West Indies women’s tour of Australia, officiating all four Women's One Day International matches. He continued to umpire in international women’s cricket, including the final two WODIs of the South Africa in Australia series in November 2016.  He also officiated matches in the 2016–17 ICC World Cricket League East Asia–Pacific Region Qualifiers in February 2017, covering fixtures involving Fiji, the Philippines, and Vanuatu.

Gillespie’s dedication to improving his skills led to his acceptance into the 2015 intake of the Australian Sports Commission National Officiating Scholarship program, designed to support the development of elite-level officials. In May 2015, he joined the 2015–16 National Umpire Panel, replacing Damien Mealey.  He further progressed his career, standing in his first Twenty20 International (T20I) match between Australia and West Indies on October 7, 2022. 

Outside of cricket, Gillespie works as a police officer in the Victorian Police Force and is a supporter of the Richmond Tigers Australian Football League team.

title: Mike Melvill
text:
Michael Winston Melvill, born in Johannesburg, South Africa on November 30, 1940, is a pilot recognized for breaking aviation records and, notably, for being the first commercial astronaut. His pioneering role came as a test pilot for SpaceShipOne, the experimental spaceplane created by Scaled Composites. He achieved this distinction on June 21, 2004, during flight 15P, becoming the 435th person to enter space. He also piloted SpaceShipOne on flight 16P, which was the first competitive flight in pursuit of the Ansari X Prize.

Melvill’s connection to Scaled Composites began in 1978 when he travelled to California to demonstrate a VariViggen aircraft he had personally built. Impressed, Burt Rutan, the founder of Scaled Composites, immediately offered him a position. He was later appointed as Rutan’s lead test pilot in 1982.

Before his historic flights on SpaceShipOne, Melvill undertook a significant aviation feat with Dick Rutan, Burt’s brother. In 1997, the two flew around the world in home-built Long-Eze aircraft, a journey dubbed "The Spirit of EAA Friendship World Tour." This trip, taking approximately 80 nights, included some extremely long flight segments exceeding 14 hours in duration. 

The success of the 2004 SpaceShipOne flights, with Melvill at the controls for the pivotal first flight to space, resulted in the team being awarded the $10 million Ansari X Prize. This achievement is widely credited with initiating the modern era of private space exploration. Following his piloting work, Melvill transitioned into a management role at Scaled Composites, becoming their Vice President/General Manager. 

Melvill possesses a comprehensive set of FAA certifications, including Commercial certificates for single and multi-engine airplanes, instrument airplane, rotorcraft-helicopter, and glider, in addition to his astronaut qualification. As of January 2020, he held or jointly held ten aviation world records recognized by the FAI. He was also honored with the Iven C. Kincheloe Award in 1999 for his work in high-altitude developmental flight-testing of the model 281 Proteus aircraft. Ultimately, he is recognized as the first pilot to fly a privately funded human spaceflight mission into space.

title: Edgar Bennett
text:
Edgar Bennett III, born February 15, 1969, is currently a wide receivers coach for the Jacksonville Jaguars, but is best known for his career as an NFL running back and fullback. He grew up in Jacksonville, Florida, where he attended Robert E. Lee High School, excelling in football, basketball, and track. As a football player, he earned All-State honors as a running back and was recognized as a SuperPrep All-Dixie selection, greatly influenced by his coach, Corky Rogers.

Bennett continued his football career at Florida State University, playing primarily as a fullback alongside several other future NFL players. He proved to be a versatile player, capable of both running and receiving, and even started at halfback in the Cotton Bowl after another running back was suspended. Throughout his college career, he accumulated over 2,300 all-purpose yards and 20 touchdowns on 389 touches, also catching 93 passes for over 1,000 yards.

He entered the NFL in 1992 when the Green Bay Packers drafted him in the fourth round. Initially a fullback for the Packers, he transitioned to the starting running back position in 1995, rushing for 1,067 yards. He also distinguished himself as a receiver, leading the team in receptions during his time with the Packers. While Dorsey Levens began to see increased playing time in 1996, Bennett remained a key player, ultimately contributing to the Packers’ Super Bowl XXXI victory. A ruptured Achilles tendon sidelined him for the entire 1997 season. His successful tenure with the Packers led to his induction into the Green Bay Packers Hall of Fame in 2005. 

Following his time in Green Bay, Bennett played two seasons with the Chicago Bears in 1998 and 1999 before retiring from professional football. He returned to the Packers organization in 2001, initially working as the director of player development. He then served as the running backs coach for six seasons, before being promoted to wide receivers coach in 2011. In 2015, he was further promoted to offensive coordinator, a position he held until 2018.

Bennett then moved to the Oakland/Las Vegas Raiders in 2018 as wide receivers coach under Jon Gruden, and was retained by Josh McDaniels in 2022. He was with the Raiders until February 2025, when he was dismissed. Shortly after, in February 2025, he accepted the position of wide receivers coach with the Jacksonville Jaguars. 

Beyond his football career, Edgar Bennett’s daughter, Elyse Bennett, was a high draft pick in the National Women’s Soccer League, selected seventh overall in the 2022 NWSL Draft by KC Current.

title: Lucas Boyé
text:
Lucas Boyé, born on February 28, 1996, is an Argentine professional footballer currently playing as a striker for Granada in the Segunda División. His football journey began with River Plate, where he was included in the first team’s pre-season squad in January 2014 by manager Ramon Diaz. He made his unofficial debut in a friendly against San Lorenzo de Almagro later that month, and followed it up with another friendly appearance against San Luis. His official debut for River Plate came in the 2013–14 Copa Argentina against Ferro, contributing to a penalty shootout victory. He then debuted in the Argentine Primera División in a 1–1 draw with Gimnasia y Esgrima, and quickly followed that with his first Primera División goal against San Lorenzo, assisted by Tomas Martinez.

In February 2016, Boyé signed a four-year contract with Italian club Torino, set to begin in July of that year. However, he spent time on loan during his time with the Italian club. His first loan move was to Spanish club Celta in January 2018. The following season, 2018–19, saw him join AEK on loan, where he scored his first goal for the club against Aris Thessaloniki in October 2018, and later secured a brace against Apollon Smyrnis – his first career brace – in February 2019.  

Another loan spell followed in August 2019, this time with English Championship side Reading. He scored his first goal for Reading in an EFL Cup match against Wolverhampton Wanderers, though the game ultimately ended in defeat after he missed a penalty during the shootout. 

In September 2020, Boyé moved to newly promoted La Liga team Elche on loan with an option to buy, which was subsequently exercised in May 2021, making his transfer permanent. Most recently, on August 30, 2023, he joined Granada, again in La Liga, for a reported fee of €7 million plus add-ons, signing a four-year contract.

Boyé is known for his physical presence and playing style, earning him nicknames like “El Tanque” (The Tank) and “El Toro” (The Bull). He is described as a technically skilled and agile centre forward, praised for his work rate and selflessness on the field. Comparisons have been drawn between him and former Roma forward Abel Balbo.

Throughout his career, Boyé has achieved success at the club level, winning the Copa Libertadores, Copa Sudamericana, Recopa Sudamericana, Suruga Bank Championship, and Copa Euroamericana all while playing for River Plate in 2015. As of May 24, 2024, detailed statistics for his club and international career are available.

title: Rosaline Elbay
text:
Rosaline Elbay is an Egyptian-born actress, producer, and writer currently working in both the United States and Egypt. She was raised in Cairo, fluent in English, Arabic, and French, and initially inspired by a childhood fascination with archaeology, even studying Classics and Archaeology at Oxford University before pursuing a Master’s in Political Science and Colonial History. She then formally trained as an actress at the Actors Studio in New York City and at LAMDA, completing a two-year MFA program.

Elbay began her acting career in UK theatre, with a foundation in Shakespearean performance. She transitioned to screen work with her first Egyptian feature film, *Diamond Dust*, in 2018, followed by *Fork & Knife*. That same year, she appeared in the music video for Massar Egbari’s “Fakra” and was named the first face of young filmmakers for the Cairo International Film Festival, a role she continued in 2019. 

Her breakthrough role came in 2019 with the part of Amani in the A24 series *Ramy*, alongside Ramy Youssef. Simultaneously, she received critical acclaim for her debut on Egyptian television as Sara in *Qabeel*, earning two Al-Wafd Critics’ Choice Awards for Best Supporting Actress and Best New Face. She also hosted the opening ceremony of the El Gouna Film Festival and had her screenplay, “Garlic,” selected for their TV Development Workshop.

Since then, Elbay's career has expanded significantly. She joined the cast of Netflix’s *Kaleidoscope* in 2021 as Judy Goodwin, a role described as a “demolitions specialist.” More recently, she portrayed Diana, Princess of Wales off-Broadway in *Dodi & Diana*, and has appeared in *Let Liv* and *Jagged Mind*. She currently stars as Nora Koriem in season two of the Netflix series *The Diplomat*, with a commitment to appear in seasons three and four. Upcoming projects include roles in *Do No Harm* and *A Better Place*. 

Beyond acting, Elbay is a passionate advocate for several causes. She actively supports the UNHCR and has used her platform to advocate for refugee women. She co-produced a fundraising album, "The Olive Tape," to benefit Anera, and is a vocal advocate for women's rights and diversity in the film industry. She contributed to the cancellation of a concert by Saad Lamjarred due to allegations of sexual assault and publicly shared her personal experience with domestic violence in an op-ed for *Mada Masr* during the Egyptian MeToo movement. She also supports the rights of performers, publicly stating her support for the 2023 SAG-AFTRA strike. 

Currently residing in New York, Elbay maintains a connection to her archaeological roots and enjoys painting in her free time. She temporarily withdrew from a role in the MBC Masr series *Forgetfulness* due to health concerns related to the Covid-19 pandemic, but expressed support for her replacement.

title: Abraham Ancer
text:
Abraham Ancer, born in 1991 with dual citizenship in the United States and Mexico, is a professional golfer currently competing on the LIV Golf tour, having previously played on the PGA Tour. He achieved his first significant victory at the 2018 Emirates Australian Open, and followed it up with his first PGA Tour win at the 2021 WGC-FedEx St. Jude Invitational, becoming the fourth Mexican golfer to achieve this feat. More recently, in 2024, he won the LIV Golf Hong Kong tournament for his first individual LIV Golf victory.

Ancer’s golf journey began in McAllen, Texas, with formative years also spent in Reynosa, Mexico. He attended Sharyland High School in Texas and pursued higher education at Odessa College and the University of Oklahoma, graduating with a degree in General Studies in 2013. He excelled in college golf, achieving All-American honors at Odessa College and maintaining one of the lowest scoring averages in Oklahoma Sooners history.

Turning professional in 2013, Ancer initially competed on the Web.com Tour, securing his PGA Tour card for the 2016 season after finishing 11th on the regular season money list. His early years on the PGA Tour were marked by inconsistency, leading to a return to the Web.com Tour in 2017. He successfully regained his PGA Tour card for 2018, finishing 3rd on the Web.com Tour money list with multiple top-5 finishes. 

The 2018-2019 seasons saw Ancer consistently contend, with several top-10 finishes and a breakthrough victory at the Australian Open, which also earned him entry into the 2019 Open Championship. He represented the International team at the 2019 Presidents Cup, where he posted a strong 3-1-1 record, including a highly anticipated match against Tiger Woods, who was captaining the U.S. team. Ancer also achieved a runner-up finish at the 2020 RBC Heritage. 

In 2021, he continued to perform well, finishing second at the Wells Fargo Championship and tying for 14th at the Tokyo Olympics. His first PGA Tour victory came at the 2021 WGC-FedEx St. Jude Invitational, winning in a sudden-death playoff.  He made the move to LIV Golf in June 2022, resulting in suspension from the PGA Tour. Since joining LIV Golf, he has secured one individual victory at the 2024 LIV Golf Hong Kong event and contributed to a team victory in Bangkok. He also won the PIF Saudi International on the Asian Tour in February 2023.

title: Jackson Martínez
text:
Jackson Martínez, born in Quibdó, Colombia in 1986, was a professional footballer who primarily played as a striker. He began his career with Independiente Medellín in 2004, quickly establishing himself as a promising talent and becoming the league’s top scorer in 2009. This performance led to a move to Chiapas in Mexico in January 2010, where he spent three years. 

His time in Mexico saw periods of strong form, including a nine-goal season in 2010 and key contributions in the Copa Libertadores, despite struggling with injuries.  He attracted interest from several clubs before ultimately transferring to Porto in Portugal in 2012. At Porto, Martínez reached the peak of his career, becoming the Primeira Liga’s top scorer in each of his three seasons. He secured two Portuguese Super Cups, and consistently performed well in both domestic and European competitions, including the Champions League, earning recognition as one of the best signings of the 2012-13 season.

In July 2015, Atlético Madrid paid €35 million for his services, but his time in Spain was largely unsuccessful. He struggled to adapt to the team’s style of play and faced criticism for his lack of goals, alongside injury problems. After just six months, he moved to Guangzhou Evergrande in China for a then-record Asian transfer fee of €42 million. 

His stint in China was cut short by a serious ankle injury sustained in 2016, sidelining him for almost two years and ultimately leading to his contract termination in 2018. He attempted a comeback by returning to Portugal with Portimonense in 2018, initially on loan and then permanently, and served as captain during his time there. He scored some important goals, earning a warm reception upon his return to his former club, Porto, but ultimately retired after a final appearance with Portimonense in July 2020.

Throughout his international career, Martínez represented Colombia 40 times between 2009 and 2015, scoring nine goals. He participated in the Copa América in 2011 and 2015, and was part of the Colombian squad at the 2014 FIFA World Cup, where he scored twice against Japan. He suffered a significant ankle injury while playing for Colombia in 2015 which contributed to his struggles at Atletico Madrid.

title: Margaret Rose Vendryes
text:
Margaret Rose Vendryes, born in Kingston, Jamaica on March 16, 1955, was a multifaceted artist, curator, and art historian who spent her career based in New York. Her academic journey began with studies in costume design before she earned a Bachelor's degree from Amherst College in 1984. She continued her education, receiving an MA in Art History from Tulane University in 1992 and ultimately becoming the first Black woman to earn a PhD in Art History from Princeton University in 1997. Her doctoral work focused on African American art history, and centered on the sculptor Richmond Barthé, a topic she later expanded upon in her 2008 book, *Barthé, A Life in Sculpture*.

Vendryes dedicated herself to both academia and the art world. She held positions as Chair of the Department of Performing and Fine Arts and Director of the Fine Arts Gallery at York College in New York, beginning in 2000, and later returned to the college as Distinguished Lecturer in Fine Arts and Director of the Fine Arts Gallery in 2013. She also served as a visiting lecturer at Princeton University and an associate professor at the City University of New York. Further lecturing roles included positions at Boston University and Wellesley College.  She was selected to be the Dean of the School of the Museum of Fine Arts at Tufts University, a role she was slated to begin in June 2022, but unfortunately did not live to fulfill. 

Her curatorial work included the 2010 exhibition *Richmond Barthé: The Seeker* at the Ohr-O’Keefe Museum of Art, and *Beyond the Blues* at the New Orleans Museum of Art the same year. She also contributed significantly to art discourse by cautioning against what she termed “the race-centered approach” to interpreting art, advocating for broader context and assessment of an artist’s impact beyond their racial identity. 

Vendryes was also a practicing visual artist, best known for *The African Diva Project*, a series of multimedia works begun in 2005. These pieces combine portraits of prominent Black American women – including Donna Summer, Aretha Franklin, Grace Jones, and Whitney Houston – with traditional African masks, traditionally worn by men, to explore themes of power, race, gender, and beauty. In 2014, she created “My spirit is too ancient to understand the separation of soul & gender - Guro Ntozake” for the Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture, celebrating the 40th anniversary of Ntozake Shange’s play. 

Margaret Rose Vendryes passed away on March 29, 2022, from respiratory failure. She was a longtime board member of the Leslie Lohman Museum and was remembered with a memorial exhibit at Childs Gallery in Boston from November 2022 to January 2023. Throughout her career, she authored and contributed to numerous publications on art and art history, including *The Visual Blues* and *In Search of Missing Masters: The Lewis Tanner Moore Collection of African American Art*.

title: Kaoru Kuroki
text:
Kaoru Kuroki, born in 1965, was a Japanese performer who transitioned from adult videos to become a significant media personality known for her candid discussions about sex and society. Often compared to figures like Cicciolina and Dr. Ruth, Kuroki began her career after leaving art college and Yokohama National University, initially viewing adult video (AV) work as a form of artistic expression. She admired filmmakers like Nagisa Oshima and Ingmar Bergman, but found the AV world to be more primal than artistic, likening it to a simple craving satisfied by readily available content.

Kuroki debuted in the AV industry in 1986 with *SM Poi no suki*, working with director Toru Muranishi, who was known for a documentary style in his films. She continued collaborating with Muranishi after he founded Diamond Visual, and their videos typically featured Kuroki delivering spoken-word introductions on topics of sexual liberation, followed by nude or swimsuit modeling, and then explicit performances often involving S&M. Her work was noted for its stark contrast between vulnerability and assertiveness, and she believed it could be liberating for both men and women, forcing them to confront their own desires and expectations.

Kuroki achieved mainstream recognition in 1988 when she publicly stopped shaving her underarm hair as a protest against Japanese censorship of pubic hair depictions. This act gained media attention and led to appearances on talk shows and commercials, appealing to both male fans of her AV work and female viewers who appreciated her feminist perspectives. She even had a role in a television drama. Kuroki felt a social need for someone to openly discuss sex, and saw herself fulfilling that role. 

During her career, Kuroki formed a connection with Cicciolina in Italy, finding common ground but also experiencing differences in their views on S&M. She argued that S&M did not equate to submissiveness and, alongside Kimiko Matsuzaka, helped to establish the topic as a feminist issue in Japan. She collaborated with Matsuzaka on several projects, including instructional sex videos and a pink film.

Kuroki retired from public life in 1994, following allegations of physical violence from Muranishi. Later, she successfully sued a magazine for invasion of privacy after they published details of her personal life without consent, winning a substantial settlement in 2007. At the peak of her career, her videos sold exceptionally well, reaching 17,000 units each, and she is credited with changing the public perception of AV actresses, presenting them as individuals making informed choices rather than being forced into the industry. Her impact was so significant that she is described as "the first high-profile AV actress," and her life story was recently depicted in the Netflix series *The Naked Director*.

title: G. Venugopal
text:
G. Venugopal, born on December 10, 1960, is a prominent Indian playback singer primarily known for his extensive work in Malayalam cinema. He began his career in 1984 with the film *Odaruthammava Aalariyam* and has since contributed to over 400 films, alongside a remarkable catalog of more than 500 private albums.

Venugopal’s roots are in Thattathumala, near Kilimanoor, where he was raised as the eldest of two children. His father, Gopinathan Nair, was from Thattathumala, while his mother, Sarojini, held the position of head of the music department at Government College for Women in Thiruvananthapuram. He comes from a deeply musical family; the renowned Parur sisters, K. Sharadamani and K. Radhamani, were his maternal aunts. This musical lineage extends to his cousins, singers Sujatha Mohan and Radhika Thilak, and his niece, Shweta Mohan, all of whom are established figures in the Indian music industry.

In his personal life, Venugopal married Reshmi on April 8, 1990, and they have two children, Arvind and Anupallavi. Continuing the family tradition, his son, Arvind, also pursues a career as a playback singer.

Throughout his career, Venugopal has received significant recognition for his vocal contributions. He has been honored with multiple Kerala State Film Awards for Best Male Playback Singer, winning in 1988 for “Unarumee Gaanam” from *Moonnam Pakkam*, in 1990 for “Thaane Poovitta Moham” from *Sasneham*, and again in 2004 for “Aadadi Aadaadadi” from *Ullam*. The Kerala Film Critics Association has also acknowledged his talent, awarding him Best Male Playback Singer in 1987 for “Onnam Ragam Paadi” from *Thoovanathumbikal* and in 1989 for “Mainaka Ponmudiyil” from *Mazhavilkavadi*. More recently, he received the Asianet Film Award for Best Playback Singer (Male) in 2006 for “Kainiraye” from *Baba Kalyani*. 

In 2022, Venugopal was awarded the Janmashtami Award by Balagokulam, recognizing his contributions to the art and culture of Kairali, and notably, he was the youngest recipient of this award. He has also appeared as a judge on the television series *Shyamambaram* which aired on Zee Keralam in 2023.

title: Henry VII of England
text:
Henry VII, born in 1457, was the first monarch of the House of Tudor, ascending the throne in 1485 after defeating Richard III at the Battle of Bosworth Field. His claim to the throne stemmed from his mother, Margaret Beaufort, a descendant of John of Gaunt, and his father, Edmund Tudor, a half-brother of the Lancastrian King Henry VI. Henry’s early life was marked by the Wars of the Roses, spent largely in exile in Brittany after Edward IV regained the throne in 1471. He finally secured the crown through military victory, becoming the last English king to win it on the battlefield, and solidified his position by defeating further rebellions, most notably at the Battle of Stoke Field in 1487, effectively ending the Wars of the Roses.

To further stabilize his rule, Henry married Elizabeth of York, daughter of Edward IV, uniting the warring houses of Lancaster and York. He repealed the *Titulus Regius*, legitimizing Elizabeth and potentially hinting at doubts surrounding the fate of the Princes in the Tower. He ruled for nearly 24 years, focusing on consolidating royal power by weakening the nobility through measures like bonds and recognizances and restricting their ability to maintain private armies. Several Yorkist pretenders, including Lambert Simnel and Perkin Warbeck, challenged his reign, but were ultimately defeated, demonstrating his resolve to maintain control. 

Henry’s reign was characterized by a meticulous attention to financial detail and a focus on increasing royal revenues. Unlike previous monarchs, he prioritized accumulating wealth over lavish spending, employing efficient yet often ruthless tax collection methods. Archbishop John Morton’s “Morton’s Fork” exemplifies this approach, ensuring the nobility contributed to the crown’s coffers. He also utilized acts of resumption to reclaim lands, significantly increasing royal holdings. While these measures brought financial stability, they were accompanied by widespread abuses that were investigated and addressed after his death, with some of his tax collectors being executed by his son, Henry VIII. 

His ancestry also played a role in securing support; he leveraged his Welsh heritage to rally troops during campaigns. He adopted the red dragon as a symbol alongside the standard of St. George, recognizing the importance of appealing to Welsh national identity.  He was succeeded peacefully by his son, Henry VIII, marking a period of relative stability after decades of civil war.  His policies and administrative initiatives laid the foundation for the Tudor dynasty's long and prosperous reign.

title: Terrence Romeo
text:
Terrence Bill Vitanzos Romeo, born March 16, 1992, is a Filipino professional basketball player currently with the Terrafirma Dyip of the Philippine Basketball Association (PBA). He is a versatile player, capable of playing both point guard and shooting guard. His professional career began after being drafted fifth overall by Barako Bull in the 2013 PBA draft, following a highly decorated amateur career.

Romeo's basketball journey started with the Letran Squires before he was recruited by Far Eastern University (FEU). He quickly made an impact, setting a UAAP Juniors basketball record by scoring 83 points in a single game, surpassing the previous record of 69. This performance earned him the UAAP Juniors' Most Valuable Player award in 2009, alongside averages of 37.1 points, 4.1 assists, and 4.0 steals per game. 

His collegiate career at FEU saw initial challenges adapting to a role secondary to UAAP MVP RR Garcia. While named Rookie of the Year, his shooting percentage was initially low at 32%, averaging 9.9 points. He steadily improved, averaging 11.4 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 3.2 assists in his sophomore year, helping FEU reach the UAAP Finals.  In his final two years, Romeo blossomed into a dominant force, earning spots on the UAAP Mythical Team and culminating in being named the 2013 UAAP Men's Basketball Most Valuable Player. He became only the third guard to win the award. During this period, he consistently scored 30+ points in multiple games, a feat only matched by a few players since 2003. He also played in the PBA D-League for the Big Chill Super Chargers while still in college.

Romeo’s PBA career began with GlobalPort Batang Pier in 2013, where he quickly showcased his scoring ability, including a 34-point performance in just his second professional game. He drew comparisons to PBA legend Mark Caguioa, who himself recognized Romeo’s potential. His sophomore year saw him lose weight to improve his agility and quickness, becoming a key component of a talented GlobalPort backcourt. He continued to develop, earning recognition at the 2015 PBA All-Star Weekend, winning the Three-Point Shootout and being named All-Star Game MVP. He was awarded the PBA Most Improved Player after leading GlobalPort to their best finish in the 2015 Governors' Cup and becoming the league's top local scorer.  He formed a potent offensive duo with Stanley Pringle, dubbed the "Slash Brothers".

He was later traded to TNT KaTropa in 2018, following disagreements with his coach, and then to San Miguel Beermen in December of the same year. With San Miguel, he contributed to their championship runs, including a significant 29-point performance in Game 2 of the 2019 Commissioner's Cup Finals. In November 2024, he was traded to Terrafirma Dyip, a move he described as difficult, but to which he committed.

Beyond the PBA, Romeo has represented the Philippines in 3x3 basketball, leading Manila West to victory at the 2014 FIBA 3x3 World Tour Manila Masters and earning individual accolades. He has also been a member of the Gilas Pilipinas national team, participating in tournaments like the William Jones Cup and the 2015 FIBA Asia Championship.  Recently, in January 2025, he began his coaching career as the head coach of the PSP Gymers in the Women's Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League.

title: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva
text:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, known simply as Lula, is a Brazilian politician and former trade unionist who currently serves as the 39th president of Brazil, a position he previously held from 2003 to 2011. Born in 1945 in Pernambuco, Lula experienced a difficult childhood marked by poverty and limited education, not learning to read until age ten.
