He began working at a young age, eventually becoming a metalworker and a prominent trade union leader, leading strikes in the ABC region during Brazil’s military dictatorship. He was a key figure in the movement for Brazil’s redemocratization, helping found the Workers’ Party (PT) in 1980 and participating in the Diretas Já campaign for direct elections.

Lula ran for president multiple times, unsuccessfully in 1989, 1994, and 1998, before finally winning in 2002 and being re-elected in 2006. His presidencies coincided with a period of economic growth in South America, and he implemented social welfare programs like Bolsa Família, contributing to a reduction in poverty and external debt. He also engaged in foreign policy initiatives, focusing on regional integration and global trade. Despite his popularity, his first terms were shadowed by corruption scandals, including the Mensalão vote-buying affair.

Following his second term, Lula remained active in politics. However, in 2017, he was convicted on charges of money laundering and corruption as part of the Operation Car Wash investigation, leading to 580 days in prison. He was disqualified from running in the 2018 presidential election.  Further convictions followed in 2019, but in 2021, the Supreme Federal Court annulled his convictions, citing procedural errors and bias. 

Legally able to run again, Lula campaigned in 2022 and defeated incumbent Jair Bolsonaro in a runoff election. He was inaugurated in January 2023 as the oldest person to assume the Brazilian presidency and the first to win a third non-consecutive term, and the first to defeat an incumbent president.

Lula’s early life was characterized by hardship; his family moved to São Paulo in search of better opportunities, but faced financial struggles and family division. He worked various jobs from a young age, including street vending and as a shoeshiner, before securing a position in a metallurgical company where he later suffered an accident that cost him a finger. This experience fuelled his involvement in union activities. Inspired by his brother’s political leanings, he rose through the ranks of the labor movement, becoming president of the Steel Workers' Union.

Throughout his political career, Lula has been described as left-wing. As president, he oversaw the implementation of social programs aimed at reducing hunger and poverty, like the expansion of Bolsa Escola into Bolsa Família. He also launched initiatives focused on education, housing, and infrastructure. His economic policies benefited from a boom in commodity prices, allowing for debt reduction and investment in social programs. While his presidency saw economic progress, it also faced criticism regarding the slow pace of educational improvements and the challenges of implementing social programs effectively.

title: Pablo Zabaleta
text:
Pablo Zabaleta, born in Buenos Aires, Argentina in 1985, was a professional footballer who primarily played as a right-back. He began his career at San Lorenzo in 2002, progressing through their youth system after joining at age 12, initially as a defensive midfielder before shifting to the right side of the field. In 2005, he transferred to Espanyol in Spain, where he won the Copa del Rey in 2006, playing the entire match in the final against Real Zaragoza. A shoulder injury sidelined him for three months in 2007, but he also featured in the 2007 UEFA Cup final, which Espanyol lost on penalties.

Zabaleta moved to Manchester City in 2008, rejecting an offer from Juventus. He quickly became a key player, debuting against Chelsea and scoring his first goal for the club against Wigan Athletic in 2009. He was a consistent presence in the team as Manchester City underwent significant investment under new ownership. He amassed over 300 appearances for City, winning a comprehensive set of English honors: the Premier League in 2012 and 2014, the FA Cup in 2011, the League Cup in 2014 and 2016, and the Community Shield in 2012. He became a cult hero among City fans due to his dedication and tenacious playing style, even serving as captain on multiple occasions. 

After nine seasons with Manchester City, Zabaleta joined West Ham United in 2017 on a free transfer, where he played for three seasons, making 80 appearances and scoring once. He was reunited with former manager Manuel Pellegrini in 2018. He retired from professional football in October 2020, having become the first Argentine and third South American to reach 300 Premier League appearances. 

On the international stage, Zabaleta represented Argentina at various youth levels, winning the FIFA U-20 World Cup in 2005 and a gold medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics. He earned over 75 caps for Argentina’s youth teams. He debuted for the senior national team in 2005 and was part of the squad that finished as runners-up in the 2014 FIFA World Cup and the 2015 Copa América. He even captained Argentina in a friendly match against Nigeria in 2011.

Following his retirement, Zabaleta worked as a football pundit for the BBC, covering the 2018 and 2022 World Cups. In January 2023, he began a coaching career as an assistant manager for the Albania national football team, working under head coach Sylvinho. He also currently works for ESPN covering La Liga. Zabaleta is of Spanish Basque descent and has a tattoo honoring his mother. Throughout his career, he received individual accolades including being named in the PFA Team of the Year and earning Manchester City’s Player of the Year award in 2013.

title: Juan Nepomucino Goetz
text:
Juan Nepomucino Goetz was an Austrian Catholic priest who became a significant, and controversial, figure in Cuban musical life in the early 19th century. Originally arriving in Cuba after fleeing Santiago de Cuba following the departure of British forces under Toussaint-Louverture – where he had celebrated their withdrawal by ringing church bells – Goetz established himself as a priest serving the foreign population due to his linguistic abilities. 

His most notable impact came in Havana when the position of choirmaster became vacant due to the illness and subsequent death of Lazo de la Vega. Four candidates applied for the role: José Francisco Rensoli, a 28-year-old violinist; Luis Lazo, a singer; Cayetano Solis, a maestro; and Cayetano Pagueras, a Catalan composer and first contralto who considered himself proficient in plainsong, organ playing, counterpoint, and composition. A competitive examination was planned to determine the successor.

However, before the examination could take place, Goetz submitted his own application for the position, arriving with a letter of intent on July 29, 1803. Following an assessment process involving observation, listening, and questioning of the existing choir members, Goetz produced a report to the town council containing blunt evaluations of the musicians. 

His assessment of Cayetano Pagueras, while acknowledging his compositional talent, was critical of his vocal ability, describing it as “terrible” and lacking expressiveness, and mentioned his near-blindness. He also dismissed Don Luis Lazo as musically inept, claiming he had fraudulently obtained his position and was “superfluous.” Goetz was particularly harsh in his judgement of Don Juan Alcayado, labeling him a disruptive presence with a “terrible voice” and deeming his tenor position entirely unnecessary, advocating for its abolition.

Based on these evaluations, Goetz proposed a restructuring of the musical ensemble. He advocated for reducing the number of positions, promoting younger, more capable singers, and requiring those demoted to re-take both theoretical and practical examinations. His proposed ensemble for 1806 consisted of a choirmaster, four sopranos, two contraltos, two tenors, one baritone, and an instrumental section featuring two clarinets, two bassoons, two horns, four violins, a bass viol, and a bass. Goetz’s actions and opinions, therefore, drastically reshaped the composition and structure of the Havana choir.

title: A. K. Ramanujan
text:
A.K. Ramanujan, born in Mysore City, Karnataka, in 1929 and passing away in Chicago in 1993, was a remarkably versatile figure – a poet, scholar, linguist, folklorist, translator, and playwright. He possessed expertise in five languages: English, Tamil, Kannada, Telugu, and Sanskrit, applying this knowledge to both classical and modern literature, and advocating for the recognition of non-standard dialects. Though prolific in multiple genres, he is best remembered for his uniquely original and artistically compelling poetry, for which he posthumously received the Sahitya Academy Award in 1999 for *The Collected Poems*.

Ramanujan’s early life was shaped by his father, an astrologer and mathematics professor with a strong interest in languages. Initially studying science at Maharaja College of Mysore, he switched to English at his father’s encouragement.  He continued his education as a Fellow at Deccan College, Pune, and later as a Fulbright Scholar at Indiana University, where he earned his PhD in Linguistics. He began his teaching career lecturing in English at Quilon and Belgaum, followed by eight years at The Maharaja Sayajirao University in Baroda before joining the University of Chicago in 1962, where he remained throughout his career. He also held visiting positions at Harvard, Wisconsin, Michigan, Berkeley, and Carleton College. At Chicago, he played a pivotal role in developing the South Asian Studies program, contributing to departments of Linguistics, South Asian Languages and Civilizations, and the Committee on Social Thought.

Throughout his career, Ramanujan was honored with awards including the Padma Shri in 1976 and a MacArthur Prize Fellowship in 1983, becoming the William E. Colvin Professor at the University of Chicago. His experiences as an Indo-American writer informed his work, notably poems like "Conventions of Despair," which explored the cultural differences between East and West.  His scholarship encompassed cultural essays, such as "Is There an Indian Way of Thinking?", which proposed a “context-sensitive” understanding of Indian psychology. He also made significant contributions to folklore studies, highlighted by works like *The Interior Landscape* and *Folktales from India,* emphasizing the interconnectedness of Indian oral and written traditions. His literary study, *Speaking Śiva*, became a foundational text for understanding the Vīraśaiva tradition. 

However, Ramanujan’s work was not without controversy. His 1991 essay, “Three Hundred Ramayanas,” which posited the existence of numerous versions of the Ramayana, including some depicting Rama and Sita as siblings, ignited protests in India. Some Hindus considered these interpretations derogatory and sought its removal from the University of Delhi’s history syllabus. Despite a committee recommending its retention, the essay was ultimately removed in 2011, sparking criticism from historians and intellectuals who accused the university of yielding to external pressure. 

Ramanujan left behind a substantial body of work, including translations of classical Tamil and Kannada texts, and numerous publications in poetry, essays, and literary studies. His translations include *The Interior Landscape* and *Folktales from India*, and his poetry collections include *The Striders*, *Relations*, and *The Collected Poems*. He also translated works from Kannada into English, including U.R. Ananthamurthy’s *Samskara*.

title: Lionel Messi
text:
Lionel Messi, born in Rosario, Argentina in 1987, is widely considered one of the greatest footballers in history. He currently plays as a forward and captains both Inter Miami in Major League Soccer and the Argentina national team. Throughout his career, Messi has amassed a record-breaking number of individual accolades, including a record eight Ballon d’Or awards, six European Golden Shoes, and has been named the world’s best player by FIFA eight times. He is the most decorated player ever, with a total of 45 team trophies. His records extend to most goals in a calendar year (91), most goals for a single club (672 for Barcelona), most goals in La Liga (474), most goal contributions in the FIFA World Cup (21), and Copa América (32). He has scored over 870 senior career goals and provided over 380 assists.

Messi began his professional career with Barcelona, making his competitive debut at age 17 in 2004. He steadily became a key player, and in the 2008–09 season, helped Barcelona achieve a historic treble – winning La Liga, the Copa del Rey, and the Champions League. This success marked the beginning of a period of dominance, earning him his first Ballon d’Or. He continued to break records, setting the European record for most goals in a season and becoming Barcelona's all-time top scorer by the 2011–12 season. A second treble followed in the 2014–15 season, leading to a fifth Ballon d’Or in 2015. He captained Barcelona from 2018, winning a sixth Ballon d’Or in 2019, and accumulated a club-record 34 trophies with the team, including ten La Liga titles and four Champions League titles. Financial difficulties at Barcelona led to his transfer to Paris Saint-Germain in 2021, where he won the Ligue 1 title for two consecutive seasons before joining Inter Miami in 2023.

Messi is also a pivotal figure for the Argentina national team, holding records for most goals scored and most appearances. He won a gold medal at the 2008 Summer Olympics and captained the team from 2011. Despite reaching three consecutive finals – the 2014 World Cup, 2015 Copa América, and Copa América Centenario – Argentina lost all three. He briefly retired from international football in 2016, but returned to help the team qualify for the 2018 World Cup. He finally led Argentina to victory in the 2021 Copa América, ending a 28-year trophy drought and securing his seventh Ballon d'Or. A year later, he captained Argentina to win the 2022 World Cup, their first in 36 years, earning him a record-extending eighth Ballon d’Or in 2023. He continued his success by winning the 2024 Copa América, his third major international title.

Beyond his playing career, Messi has been a brand ambassador for Adidas since 2006. He was consistently among the highest-paid footballers and athletes globally between 2009 and 2022, recognized by both France Football and Forbes. He has been featured in Time's list of the 100 most influential people and was named Laureus World Sportsman of the Year in 2020 and 2023. In 2020, he surpassed $1 billion in career earnings and was named Time’s Athlete of the Year in 2023, later receiving the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2025. His early life was marked by a passion for football nurtured by his family, and overcoming a growth hormone deficiency diagnosed at age 10 through therapy. He was scouted by Barcelona after trials with River Plate, and his family relocated to Spain in 2001, where he joined Barcelona’s youth academy, La Masia, and quickly rose through the ranks.

title: Ramkumar Mukhopadhyay
text:
Ramkumar Mukhopadhyay, born on March 8, 1956, is an Indian Bengali writer known for his contributions to both adult and children’s literature. He was born in Calcutta, the son of Ramangamohan Mukhopadhyay and Kanaklata Mukhopadhyay. His education began with attendance at Ramakrishna Mission Vidyamandir, a residential college in Belur, where he completed his graduation. He continued his studies at The University of Calcutta, earning a Masters degree in English, and later achieved a Ph.D from Jadavpur University.

Mukhopadhyay’s professional life has been deeply rooted in the literary world. He began his career as the Regional Secretary for East India with the Sahitya Akademi, and previously served as the Convener of the Bengali Advisory Board for the same organization. He also held the position of President of the Bharatiya Bhasha Parishad. He concluded his career as the Director of the Publishing Department at Visva-Bharati, from which he has since retired. Throughout his career, he has maintained connections with numerous Bengali Little Magazines, indicating a consistent engagement with the smaller, more experimental side of Bengali literary culture.

His published works span a variety of genres. He debuted as an author in 1984 with “Madale Natun Bol” (The New Beats on the Drum), a collection of fourteen short stories. His first novel, “Charane Prantare” (At the Grazing Ground, at the Horizon), followed in 1993. Beyond novels and short stories, Mukhopadhyay has also written travelogues, books of essays, compiled and edited works, and dedicated efforts towards juvenile literature, demonstrating a broad range of literary interests.

Over the course of his career, Mukhopadhyay has received significant recognition for his writing. He was awarded the Somenchandra Award from the Paschimbanga Bangla Akademi in 2000. This was followed by the Galpamela Puraskar in 2004, and the Katha Award in New Delhi in 2005. Further accolades include the Bankimchandra Smriti Puraskar from the Department of Higher Education, Government of West Bengal, in 2006, and the Saratchandra Smriti Puraskar from Bhagalpur in 2007. He received the Sis Puraskar in 2008, the Gajendra Kumar Mitra Birth Centenary Award in 2009, and the prestigious Ananda Puraskar from the Ananda Bazar Patrika and Desh in 2013. More recent awards include the D.L.Ray Award and the Kusumanjali Award, both in 2014, the Krititwa Samagra Puraskar from the Bharatiya Bhasha Parisad in 2016, and the Karmayogi Nanigopal Chakraborty Smriti Sahitya Puraskar in 2023. These awards reflect a sustained and highly regarded presence in Bengali literary circles.

title: Virginia Christine
text:
Virginia Christine, born Virginia Christine Ricketts in 1920 in Stanton, Iowa, was a versatile American actress who found success across stage, radio, film, and television. Though she enjoyed a long and varied career, she is most widely remembered for portraying “Mrs. Olson” in the popular Folgers Coffee commercials that aired from 1965 to 1986, appearing in over 100 installments. 

Christine’s early life included a move to California and studies at UCLA, beginning her acting career in radio while still in college. She amassed an impressive list of radio credits, including 23 appearances on the classic western *Gunsmoke*. Her film career began after being signed by Warner Bros. in 1942, following a stage debut in a Los Angeles production of *Hedda Gabler*. She subsequently moved to Universal Pictures and appeared in films like *The Mummy’s Curse* and *The Killers*, where she initially auditioned for the lead role but was cast as Lilly Harmon Lubinsky.

Throughout the 1950s and 60s, Christine worked steadily in film, often in supporting roles. She frequently collaborated with producer Stanley Kramer, appearing in films like *Cyrano de Bergerac*, *High Noon*, *Not as a Stranger*, and *Judgment at Nuremberg*. She also took on roles in films such as *Invasion of the Body Snatchers* and *Guess Who’s Coming to Dinner*, where she played a prejudiced coworker. 

Concurrent with her film work, Christine was a prolific television actress, appearing in numerous shows throughout the 1950s and 60s, including *The Abbott and Costello Show*, *Alfred Hitchcock Presents*, *Gunsmoke*, *The Twilight Zone*, and *Perry Mason*. She had a recurring role as Ovie Swenson on *Tales of Wells Fargo*. However, it was her portrayal of Mrs. Olson, the kindly coffee-serving neighbor, that cemented her place in popular culture, even inspiring parodies by well-known entertainers like Carol Burnett and Johnny Carson. In 1971, her Iowa hometown honored her by painting their water tower to resemble a coffee pot.

Christine retired from acting in 1979 and dedicated her time to volunteer work at Planned Parenthood and serving as a judge for the American College Theatre Festival. She was also appointed honorary mayor of Brentwood, Los Angeles, where she lived with her husband, character actor Fritz Feld, whom she married in 1940 and remained with until his death in 1993. Virginia Christine passed away in 1996 from cardiovascular disease and is buried at Mount Sinai Memorial Park Cemetery in Los Angeles. She and Fritz Feld had two sons, Steven and Danny.

title: Carlos Ghosn
text:
Carlos Ghosn, born in 1954, is a businessman who rose to prominence as a leading automotive executive, holding key positions at Michelin, Renault, Nissan, and Mitsubishi Motors. He began his career at Michelin in 1978, working his way up through various leadership roles over 18 years, including a successful turnaround of the company’s struggling South American operations. This experience shaped his cross-cultural management style, emphasizing diversity.

In 1999, following Renault’s investment in Nissan, Ghosn moved to Japan to revitalize the struggling automaker. As COO and later CEO, he implemented the “Nissan Revival Plan,” a drastic restructuring that involved job cuts, plant closures, and a dismantling of the traditional Japanese *keiretsu* system. This plan successfully returned Nissan to profitability within two years, exceeding ambitious targets and establishing Ghosn’s reputation as a turnaround specialist. He simultaneously became CEO of Renault in 2005, an unprecedented position leading two Fortune Global 500 companies. His influence further expanded in 2016 with his appointment as chairman of Mitsubishi Motors after Nissan gained a controlling stake.

Ghosn’s early life was marked by a nomadic upbringing. His grandfather emigrated from Lebanon to Brazil, establishing a successful entrepreneurial legacy. Ghosn himself was born in Brazil, moved to Lebanon as a child, and later completed his education in Paris, earning degrees from École Polytechnique and École des Mines de Paris. 

Throughout his career, Ghosn was known for his bold leadership style and willingness to challenge established norms. He championed the development of electric vehicles, investing heavily in the technology and positioning the Renault–Nissan Alliance as a leader in the market. He also played a role in recovery efforts after the 2011 Japanese earthquake and tsunami. However, his career took a dramatic turn in November 2018 when he was arrested in Japan on suspicion of financial misconduct at Nissan. 

He was accused of underreporting his income and misusing company funds. Following his arrest, Ghosn was detained for an extended period and subjected to intense interrogation. He maintained his innocence, claiming the allegations were part of a corporate coup.  After being released on bail under strict conditions, Ghosn dramatically escaped from Japan in December 2019, concealing himself in a large box shipped as freight on a private jet, a move that drew international attention. The legal proceedings and the circumstances surrounding his escape remain a complex and highly publicized case.

title: Mateo Correa Magallanes
text:
Mateo Correa Magallanes, born July 23, 1866, in Tepechitlán, Zacatecas, Mexico, was a Catholic priest and eventually a saint. He demonstrated early dedication to his faith, attending the seminary in Zacatecas on a scholarship beginning in 1881. He completed his studies and was ordained a priest in 1893 at the age of 27. Early in his priestly service, he administered First Communion to a young Miguel Pro, who would later also become a priest and be martyred himself. 

Correa served as a parish priest in various locations throughout his career. He was first assigned to Concepción del Oro in 1898, and later moved to Colotlán in 1908. The political climate in Mexico during this period was increasingly hostile towards the Catholic Church. Following the government’s repression of the church in 1910, Correa was forced to go into hiding to continue his ministry. He was later assigned to Valparaíso in 1926.

In 1927, during a period of continued persecution, Correa was arrested while performing his priestly duties. Specifically, he was apprehended by soldiers while bringing Viaticum – the Eucharist given to the dying – to a sick woman. He was falsely accused of involvement with the Cristero movement, a Catholic uprising formed in response to the government’s anti-church policies. He was subsequently imprisoned in both Zacatecas and Durango.

While incarcerated in Durango, Correa was approached by General Eulogio Ortiz. Ortiz requested that Correa hear the confessions of imprisoned Cristero rebels. Correa agreed to administer the Sacrament of Reconciliation, fulfilling his priestly obligation. However, following the confessions, Ortiz demanded that Correa reveal what had been said during the sacrament. Correa resolutely refused to violate the seal of confession, despite Ortiz threatening him with immediate execution, even pointing a gun to his head. He maintained his refusal, upholding the sanctity of the confessional. As a result, on February 6, 1927, Correa was taken to a cemetery outside Durango and executed by being shot in the head.

Decades later, on May 21, 2000, Pope John Paul II formally recognized Correa’s martyrdom and canonized him as a saint in a ceremony held in St. Peter's Square at the Vatican. The event drew thousands of pilgrims from Mexico and around the globe. During his homily, Pope John Paul II lauded Correa’s courageous faith and willingness to sacrifice his life for the Gospel, and encouraged all the faithful to emulate his example in their own lives, particularly when facing persecution and violence. Saint Mateo Correa Magallanes is now revered as a symbol of unwavering faith and dedication to Christ.

title: Anurag Kashyap
text:
Anurag Kashyap, born September 10, 1972, is a prominent Indian filmmaker and actor, recognized with four Filmfare Awards and the distinction of being a Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters by the French government in 2013. His entry into cinema began as a co-writer on Ram Gopal Varma’s successful crime drama *Satya* (1998), but his directorial debut, *Paanch*, faced censorship issues and never received a theatrical release. He then directed *Black Friday* (2004), a critically lauded film based on a book detailing the 1993 Bombay bombings, although its release was delayed for two years due to legal proceedings.

Kashyap’s career continued with *No Smoking* (2007), a film that garnered mixed reviews and commercial disappointment, followed by the well-received and commercially successful modern adaptation of *Devdas*, titled *Dev.D* (2009). He also directed the socio-political drama *Gulaal* (2009) and the thriller *That Girl in Yellow Boots* (2011). A significant turning point came with *Gangs of Wasseypur* (2012), a two-part crime epic that achieved international critical acclaim and has since gained cult status.

He subsequently co-produced the critically acclaimed *The Lunchbox* (2013) and *Shahid* (2012), the latter earning a BAFTA nomination. Further acclaimed works include the anthology *Bombay Talkies* (2013), the thriller *Ugly* (2014), *Raman Raghav 2.0* (2016), inspired by a notorious serial killer, and *Mukkabaaz* (2018). He also co-directed *Sacred Games*, India’s first Netflix Original series, based on Vikram Chandra’s novel, and the romantic drama *Manmarziyaan*. 

Born in Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh, Kashyap’s father was a chief engineer. He spent parts of his childhood in Dehradun and Gwalior, attending Hillgrange Preparatory School and Scindia School respectively. His family's life in Obra Thermal Power Station influenced locations used in *Gangs of Wasseypur*. He initially pursued zoology at Delhi University but became involved in street theatre with Jana Natya Manch. A film retrospective, particularly Vittorio De Sica’s *Bicycle Thieves*, ignited his passion for filmmaking.

After moving to Mumbai in 1993 with limited funds, Kashyap worked at Prithvi Theatre and gained experience through various writing assignments. He contributed to TV series like *Auto Narayan* and *Kabhie Kabhie*, and wrote screenplays for films like *Jayate* before his breakthrough with *Satya*. He continued writing for films such as *Kaun* and *Shool*.  He faced obstacles in getting his early directorial efforts, like *Paanch*, released due to censorship.  His later films, including *Bombay Velvet* (2015), though ambitious, weren’t always commercially successful, but he continued to explore diverse themes and styles, venturing into anthology films, horror with *Ghost Stories* (2020) and sci-fi thrillers like *Dobaaraa* (2022). His brother, Abhinav Kashyap, is also a filmmaker, known for *Dabangg*, and his sister, Anubhuti Kashyap, has served as his assistant and now directs independently with *Doctor G* (2022).

title: Stephanie Beatriz
text:
Stephanie Beatriz, born Stephanie Bischoff Alvizuri on February 10, 1981, is an American actress with a diverse career spanning television, film, voice work, and theatre. She was born in Neuquén, Argentina, to Colombian and Bolivian parents, and immigrated to the United States with her family at the age of two, eventually settling in Webster, Texas. She became a U.S. citizen at eighteen. Her early interest in the arts was fostered by her mother, and she discovered a passion for acting through speech and debate in high school. She pursued formal training at Stephens College in Missouri, graduating in 2002, and later moved to New York City and then Los Angeles in 2010 to further her acting career.

Beatriz gained significant recognition for her role as Detective Rosa Diaz in the comedy series *Brooklyn Nine-Nine*, which aired from 2013 to 2021. She also directed an episode of the show in its sixth season. Beyond this prominent role, she has appeared in a variety of other projects. She had recurring roles in *Modern Family* and smaller parts in shows like *The Closer* and *Southland*. She starred as Bonnie in the critically acclaimed independent film *The Light of the Moon*, earning particularly positive reviews for her performance.  She has lent her voice to several animated projects, including Gina Cazador in *BoJack Horseman*, General Sweet Mayhem in *The Lego Movie 2: The Second Part*, Mirabel Madrigal in Disney’s *Encanto*, and currently voices Vaggie in *Hazbin Hotel*.  She also voiced the lead role in the podcast *Tejana* and Ruby Ortiz in *Alpha Betas* and has been involved as an executive producer of *Tejana*, with plans to develop it into a television series.

Beatriz is also involved in other audio work, having starred in the sci-fi thriller podcast *Solar* and hosted the podcast *Twin Flames*, investigating a dating cult. In 2021, she appeared in the film adaptation of *In the Heights*.  She has also been a public figure at events such as the National Hispanic Media Coalition Impact Awards, where she co-hosted with her *Brooklyn Nine-Nine* co-star Melissa Fumero. 

On a personal level, Beatriz has spoken openly about her struggles with severe astigmatism, disordered eating, and her journey to self-acceptance as a bisexual woman, publicly coming out in 2016 after experiencing biphobia and erasure. She married actor Brad Hoss in 2018, and they welcomed their daughter in August 2021.

title: Ian Khama
text:
Ian Khama, born in 1953, served as the fourth President of Botswana from 2008 to 2018, following a distinguished career in the military. He is the son of Sir Seretse Khama, Botswana’s first president, and Lady Khama, and was born in exile in the United Kingdom due to opposition to his parents’ marriage. His lineage extends further back, tracing to prominent Bamangwato chiefs including Khama III and Sekgoma I. The name “Seretse,” meaning “the clay that binds together,” was given to his father to commemorate a family reconciliation, a legacy continued with Ian’s naming.

Khama’s education included Waterford Kamhlaba, a United World College, and the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst, where he qualified as a pilot. He rapidly rose through the ranks of the Botswana Defence Force (BDF), becoming a brigadier general at age 24 and ultimately serving as Commander of the BDF from 1989 until his retirement in 1998. During his military service he received honours including the Founder Officer Medal and the Distinguished Service Medal. 

His transition to politics began in 1998 when he was appointed Vice-President under President Festus Mogae, following both Mogae’s and Khama’s retirements from their previous positions. To take office, he won a by-election in Serowe North, simultaneously relinquishing his claim to the hereditary chieftaincy of the Bamangwato people, a position many traditionally still recognized him holding. He continued as Vice-President and Minister of Presidential Affairs and Public Administration, though he took a year’s leave in 2000 which drew criticism from opposition parties. In 2003, he became Chairman of the Botswana Democratic Party (BDP), setting the stage for his eventual succession to the presidency. 

Khama succeeded Mogae as President in 2008, initially promising continuity while also indicating a shift in style. He undertook a major cabinet reshuffle and appointed a new vice-president. Elected to a full term in 2009, his presidency saw the implementation of a controversial alcohol levy, later adjusted following industry resistance. He also oversaw the passage of The Media Practitioners Act, which garnered criticism for potentially inhibiting free speech. 

During his ten years in office, Khama pursued policies focused on diversification of the economy away from diamonds and championed conservation efforts, including a ban on elephant hunting. He also took strong diplomatic stances, particularly against Robert Mugabe’s government in Zimbabwe and the actions of Omar al-Bashir in Darfur. Khama’s presidency was also marked by controversy, including the death of John Kalifatis and a subsequent presidential pardon granted to the soldiers convicted of his murder. 

After leaving office in 2018, Khama joined the Botswana Patriotic Front (BPF) following disagreements with his successor, Mokgweetsi Masisi, and campaigned for the party in the 2019 general election. He also became a member of the Board of Directors of Conservation International. Facing legal issues, including accusations of illegal firearm possession, Khama spent time in self-imposed exile before returning to Botswana in 2024, where the charges were dropped. He has since resumed his role as Kgosikgolo of the BaNgwato people, taking the regal name Khama IV, and was sworn in as a member of the Ntlo ya Dikgosi in 2025.

title: Sam Michael
text:
Samuel David Michael, born in Western Australia in 1971 and raised in Canberra, is an Australian motorsports engineer and designer with a significant career spanning Formula One and Australian Supercars. His early involvement in motorsport began with work on Neal Bates’ rally car, a Toyota Celica GT-Four, before he pursued mechanical engineering at the University of New South Wales, focusing his thesis on data acquisition systems for racing cars. While studying, he gained practical experience working part-time with Greg Siddle on Mark Larkham’s Formula Holden car, allowing him to continue his education.

Michael’s Formula One journey commenced in 1993 with Lotus, but following the team’s bankruptcy in 1994, he joined Jordan Grand Prix under Gary Anderson. There, he was instrumental in establishing the team’s research and development department, concentrating on data acquisition and designing a seven-post rig for suspension simulation and an active differential. He progressed to the Jordan test team in 1997 and became race engineer to Ralf Schumacher in 1998. When Schumacher moved to Williams, Michael took on the role of race engineer for Heinz-Harald Frentzen, enjoying success with the driver that included victories at the French and Italian Grand Prix in 1999. 

In 2001, Sir Frank Williams recruited Michael to Williams as Senior Operations Engineer, where he managed the engineers during races and testing. He was further promoted in 2004 to Technical Director, enabling Patrick Head to concentrate on engineering strategy. Michael’s time at Williams was followed by a move to McLaren in late 2011, initially as Sporting Director within the senior technical management team. This period presented challenges, including pressure stemming from pitstop failures during the implementation of new equipment, though Martin Whitmarsh publicly supported his position and the changes eventually proved fruitful.

Michael returned to Australia at the end of 2014, having resigned from McLaren earlier that year. He became involved with motorsport safety, joining the board of the Australian Institute for Motor Sport Safety in mid-2016. He also began a part-time mentoring role with Triple Eight Race Engineering following Ludo Lacroix’s departure. His commitment to safety was further solidified with an advisory role to the FIA’s Research Working Group in 2017, which focuses on reviewing new safety devices, and a seat on the FIA Single Seater Commission. By 2022, he had risen to become President of the FIA Safety Commission.

Beyond his direct involvement in racing teams, Michael co-founded Ox Mountain in 2015, a machine learning company focused on optimizing maintenance in industries like mining and rail. He also continues to share his expertise as a part-time lecturer at the University of Western Australia.

title: Angela Bairstow
text:
Angela Bairstow, born in 1942 and passing away in 2016, was a prominent English badminton player who achieved international success throughout the 1960s. She grew up on Plough Lane in Purley and received her education at Dinorben School, a private girls’ school in Wallington. Her badminton career began to flourish in 1958 with a victory in the English National Junior singles title, a feat she repeated in both 1959 and 1960. During her junior career, she also secured four English National Junior doubles titles.

Moving into senior competition, Bairstow reached the final of the prestigious All England Badminton Championships singles event in 1963, ultimately losing to Judy Hashman. That same year, she was seeded to win in the singles, doubles, and mixed events at the All England Championships, highlighting her anticipated success. While she never secured an All England title, she established herself as a key player for England, accumulating numerous titles between 1964 and 1968. These included victories in the Scottish Open, German Open, Dutch Open, Asia Cup, Irish Open, English National Badminton Championships, and the European Badminton Championships.

A particularly successful year for Bairstow was 1965, marked by winning singles, doubles, and mixed titles at the Dutch Open – a feat she repeated at the Asian Championships held in Lucknow. Following this triumph at the Asian Championships, however, organizers implemented a rule barring non-Asian players from future participation. Bairstow was known for her deceptive playing style, specifically a sliced backhand serve and flick, which contributed to her success on the court. She holds the unique distinction of being the only player to have won medals in both Asian and European Championships. 

She further demonstrated her skill on the international stage at the 1966 British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Kingston, Jamaica, where she won two gold medals and one silver medal. In her personal life, Angela Bairstow married her coach, H. Ian Palmer, in 1970. They had three children, born in 1969, 1970 and 1972, and later welcomed four grandchildren. The article lists achievements across Commonwealth Games, Asian Championships, and European Championships, alongside a record of 12 international tournament titles and 10 runner-up positions across women’s singles, women’s doubles, and mixed doubles events.

title: R. Selvaraj (politician)
text:
R. Selvaraj is a politician from Kerala, India, who began his political career with the Communist Party of India (Marxist) but later joined the Indian National Congress. He was born on March 5, 1949, in Dhanuvachapuram, near Neyyattinkara, to Varghese Nadar and Ruthe Nadar, and has two siblings, an elder sister R.Sarojam and an elder brother R.Chinnappan. He is married to Mary Valsala, and they have two daughters, Divya.M.S and Deepthi.M.S, and reside near Dhanuvachapuram in Thiruvananthapuram.

Selvaraj’s involvement in politics started through the student wings of the CPI(M), the Student Federation of India (S.F.I) and the Kerala Students Youth Federation (K.S.Y.F). He first entered the Kerala Legislative Assembly in 2006, winning the election for the Parassala constituency in Thiruvananthapuram. He was subsequently elected to represent the Neyyattinkara constituency in the 2011 state election. 

However, in March 2012, Selvaraj resigned from his position as MLA and his membership in the CPI(M) district committee. He attributed this decision to increasing factionalism within the party and feeling targeted by certain leaders within the district organization. Shortly after, in April 2012, he joined the Indian National Congress, which was then the ruling party in Kerala.

The Congress party nominated Selvaraj to contest a by-election in Neyyattinkara, and he was successfully re-elected on June 14, 2012, defeating his opponents by a margin of 6,334 votes. This victory increased the ruling United Democratic Front’s (UDF) majority in the 140-member Kerala Assembly to 73. 

Despite his initial success as a Congress candidate, Selvaraj faced defeat in subsequent elections. He contested again from the Neyyattinkara constituency in both 2016 and 2021, losing on both occasions to K. Ansalan of the CPI(M). The margin of defeat widened from 9,543 votes in 2016 to 14,262 votes in 2021.

Prior to becoming an MLA, Selvaraj held several positions within the CPI(M), including C.P.I.(M) Area Secretary for Parassala, Vice-president of the Kollayil Panchayat, and District Joint Secretary of the Karshaka Sangham in Thiruvananthapuram. He was also a member of the C.P.I.(M) District Committee in Thiruvananthapuram.

title: Ernestine Eckstein
text:
Ernestine Eckstein, born Ernestine Delois Eppenger in Indiana in 1941, was a pivotal figure in the early United States lesbian and gay rights movement and later a dedicated activist within the Black feminist movement. She deliberately used the surname Eckstein to protect her privacy and avoid being openly identified as a lesbian in environments where it could have been dangerous. After graduating from Indiana University in 1963 with a degree in Magazine Journalism, minoring in Psychology and Russian, she moved to New York City where she embraced her lesbian identity and began her activism.

Eckstein quickly became involved with both the Mattachine Society and its sister organization, the Daughters of Bilitis (DOB). By 1965, she was actively pushing the DOB towards more direct action and public demonstration, a departure from the “old guard’s” preference for negotiating with medical professionals who then considered homosexuality a mental illness. She participated in the first Annual Reminder Day protest in Philadelphia and demonstrated in front of the White House, notably as the only person of color present. Her appointment as Vice President of the New York chapter of the DOB signaled a strategic shift towards a more activist-oriented approach, aiming to connect the gay rights struggle with broader civil rights issues. Though she recognized the need for change, Eckstein initially cautioned against civil disobedience, believing the movement wasn’t yet prepared for it. She focused on addressing government discrimination in employment and the military, and challenging rejection from religious institutions.

Eckstein’s activism was deeply informed by her understanding of the Civil Rights Movement, seeing parallels between the struggles for racial and sexual equality. She corresponded with prominent gay rights advocate Frank Kameny in 1966, hoping to bring him to speak at DOB headquarters to encourage a more activist stance, though ultimately the DOB disinvited him. After three years with the DOB, she became disillusioned with internal disagreements over strategy and moved to Northern California in the early 1970s.

In California, Eckstein joined Black Women Organized for Action (BWOA), a radical, activist group founded in 1973. Her involvement stemmed from earlier experience with organizations like CORE, which she found more progressive than the NAACP, which she perceived as catering to white liberals. BWOA was a unique organization built on principles of collective responsibility and shared leadership, with rotating coordinators serving three-month terms. Eckstein’s commitment to coalition-building was evident in her belief that progress required collaboration between different groups, stating that "Negroes need white people, and homosexuals need heterosexuals." She advocated for inclusivity, hoping to erase labels of race and sexual orientation within movements for social justice. 

Eckstein’s views were progressive for her time, emphasizing the importance of demonstrations and recognizing the need for a broad base of support. She believed in connecting struggles and building alliances, arguing for a focus on shared injustices. A significant moment in recognizing her contributions was her appearance on the cover of *The Ladder*, a landmark lesbian publication, in 1966.  She died in San Pablo, California, in 1992, leaving behind a legacy of activism and a vision for a more inclusive and equitable society.

title: George Washington
text:
George Washington, born February 22, 1732, in Westmoreland County, Virginia, was a pivotal figure in American history, serving as the first president of the United States from 1789 to 1797 and leading the Continental Army to victory during the Revolutionary War. He is widely known as the “Father of the Nation.”

Washington’s early life saw him inheriting land, including Ferry Farm and later Mount Vernon, after his father’s death. He lacked the formal education of his elder half-brothers but excelled in mathematics, surveying, and writing, developing a reputation for precision and adhering to a strict code of conduct outlined in “The Rules of Civility.” He gained valuable experience as a surveyor and later as a commander in the Virginia Regiment during the French and Indian War. This military service, though marked by early defeats like the surrender at Fort Necessity and a difficult experience under General Braddock, provided crucial leadership training and a growing understanding of British military tactics. He eventually rose to command the Virginia Regiment, defending the frontier against attacks.

Beyond his military career, Washington became a successful planter, cultivating tobacco and wheat at Mount Vernon and significantly increasing his wealth through marriage to Martha Dandridge Custis, a wealthy widow. He entered Virginia politics, serving in the House of Burgesses and increasingly opposing British policies perceived as oppressive, particularly taxation without colonial representation, like the Stamp Act. 

When the American Revolution began in 1775, Washington was appointed commander-in-chief of the Continental Army. He faced immense challenges, leading a poorly equipped and often demoralized force against the powerful British army. Despite early setbacks, including the retreat from New York City, Washington orchestrated vital victories at Trenton and Princeton, bolstering morale. The war continued with struggles such as the battles of Brandywine and Germantown, and persistent issues with supplies and troop discipline. However, with crucial assistance from France, Washington achieved a decisive victory at Yorktown in 1781, effectively securing American independence, formally recognized in the Treaty of Paris in 1783.

Following the war, Washington played a key role in shaping the new nation, presiding over the Constitutional Convention in 1787. He was unanimously elected as the first president in 1788 and again in 1792. During his presidency, he prioritized establishing a strong, financially stable national government, navigating the tensions between his cabinet members, Thomas Jefferson and Alexander Hamilton. He maintained a policy of neutrality during the French Revolution and negotiated the Jay Treaty with Britain. Washington established numerous precedents for the presidency, including the use of "Mr. President," a peaceful transfer of power, and the tradition of serving only two terms. His farewell address emphasized national unity and warned against the dangers of regionalism, partisanship, and foreign influence. 

Washington was a slave owner throughout his life, though he expressed growing opposition to the institution later and provided for the manumission of his slaves in his will. He died on December 14, 1799, leaving behind a legacy as a celebrated leader and enduring symbol of American independence and republican ideals. His image remains iconic, and he is consistently ranked among the greatest presidents in American history.

title: Nobuhiro Shimatani
text:
Nobuhiro Shimatani, born February 27, 1996, is a Japanese professional wrestler who currently performs as a freelancer, most notably recognized for his work with DDT Pro-Wrestling. He also currently wrestles for Gleat, where he is a member of the BULK Orchestra stable. Known as “Check Shimatani,” he began his career in 2016 and continues to compete as of July 2022.

Shimatani’s career includes appearances across various promotions. Early in his freelance work, he participated in tag team matches for Pro Wrestling Noah and Big Japan Pro Wrestling, sometimes experiencing losses and other times securing victories alongside partners like Takato Nakano and Kota Sekifuda. More recently, in April 2024, he competed in a soft-ground wrestling match in Uganda for Soft Ground Wrestling, defeating KY Kapeeka with Cima in his corner.

He debuted for DDT Pro-Wrestling at their 19th Anniversary show in March 2016, competing in a six-man tag team match. Throughout his time with DDT, he frequently participated in the promotion’s signature events, including Judgement, Peter Pan, Ultimate Party, and Into The Fight. These appearances often involved a variety of match types, including large battle royals and multi-team contests. He occasionally wrestled for titles, but often found himself on the losing side, such as in matches at Judgement 2020 against Eruption and at Into The Fight 2019 with his Damnation stablemates.

Within DDT, Shimatani was a member of the Damnation stable and frequently appeared in their storylines. He competed in the King of DDT tournament in both 2018 and 2020, though he was eliminated in the first round each time. He also had success in the Peter Pan branch, winning a Rumble match in 2018.

Shimatani’s accomplishments include holding championships in multiple promotions. He is a one-time BBW Tag Team Champion with Yakan Nabe in Best Body Japan Pro-Wrestling. He has also held the Ironman Heavymetalweight Championship in DDT Pro-Wrestling a total of nine times, the King of Dark Championship once, and the G-Infinity Championship in Gleat alongside Hayato Tamura.

title: Mindy Smith
text:
Mindy Smith, born Melinda Leigh Smith on June 1, 1972, is an American singer-songwriter who began her musical journey after gaining recognition for a cover song. She was adopted at birth and raised on Long Island, New York, by a Protestant minister and his wife, who was a choir director, fostering an early musical environment. Following her mother’s death from cancer in 1991, Smith attended Cincinnati Bible College for two years before moving to Knoxville, Tennessee with her father. It was in Tennessee that she developed an appreciation for folk and bluegrass music, citing artists like Alison Krauss and the Cox Family as influences.

In 1998, Smith relocated to Nashville to pursue a professional music career. After reaching the finals of a contest at the Kerrville Folk Festival in 2000, she secured a contract with Big Yellow Dog Music. A breakthrough moment came in 2003 when her rendition of Dolly Parton’s “Jolene” appeared on the tribute album *Just Because I’m a Woman*, leading to a recording contract with Vanguard Records. Her debut album, *One Moment More*, was released in 2004.

Smith’s music blends various genres, and her song “Come to Jesus” proved to be her most successful single, receiving airplay across country, Christian, adult album alternative, and adult contemporary radio stations, peaking at number 32 on Billboard’s Adult Top 40 chart. She performed at the Cambridge Folk Festival in 2004, with the performance broadcast nationally on BBC Radio. 

She continued to release albums, including *Long Island Shores* in 2006, featuring the single “Out Loud,” *My Holiday*, a Christmas album with original songs co-written with Thad Cockrell, in 2007, and *Stupid Love* in 2009, during which she publicly shared her diagnosis of obsessive-compulsive disorder on a radio show. In 2012, Smith independently released a self-titled album on her Giant Leap label, and Vanguard released a compilation album, *The Essential Mindy Smith*. She followed with a holiday EP, *Snowed In*, in 2013. 

Beyond her studio albums, Smith contributed as a songwriter to the television series *Nashville* between 2015 and 2018, with four of her songs appearing on the show’s soundtrack. She has also participated in several tribute albums, covering songs by artists like The Beatles and Olivia Newton-John. In 2013, she collaborated with Anthropologie to raise money for the Captain Planet Foundation. In 2004, she received the Americana Music Association’s award for Best New/Emerging Artist of the Year.

title: Ezekiel Elliott
text:
Ezekiel Elliott, nicknamed “Zeke,” was born in Alton, Illinois in 1995 to parents who were both college athletes. His mother was a track champion and his father played football, and a maternal grandfather was a basketball player, instilling a strong athletic background. Despite this, Elliott attended John Burroughs School, focusing on academics while excelling in football, basketball, and track and field – even competing in baseball. He quickly became a standout football player, achieving impressive rushing and receiving statistics as a junior and senior, though his team unfortunately lost three consecutive championship games. His track and field prowess was also notable, culminating in four state championships in a single day. He was a highly-rated recruit, ultimately choosing Ohio State University over his parents’ alma mater, the University of Missouri.

At Ohio State, Elliott initially served as a backup but quickly rose to prominence. He became the starting running back in 2014, earning Academic All-Big Ten honors, and led the Buckeyes to a national championship in 2015. He earned MVP honors in both the Sugar Bowl and the National Championship game that season, setting several school records in rushing yards and touchdowns. He finished his collegiate career as one of Ohio State’s all-time leading rushers, second only to Archie Griffin in career rushing yards and yards per game. He received numerous accolades, including being a Graham-George Offensive Player of the Year and finishing eighth in the Heisman Trophy voting in 2015.

Elliott was selected fourth overall by the Dallas Cowboys in the 2016 NFL draft. He immediately made an impact, becoming the starting running back and earning Pro Bowl and All-Pro selections. In his rookie season, he led the league in rushing yards with 1,631, breaking several Cowboys’ rookie records and becoming the youngest player to reach 1,600 rushing yards. His success continued in 2017 and 2018, with two more Pro Bowl selections and leading the league in rushing yards again in 2018. However, his 2017 season was marked by a six-game suspension stemming from allegations of domestic violence, a situation that involved multiple legal battles and delays before he ultimately served the suspension. 

After seven seasons with the Cowboys, Elliott was released following the 2022 season. He then signed with the New England Patriots for the 2023 season before returning to the Dallas Cowboys in 2024. Throughout his professional career, Elliott was consistently praised for his versatility, possessing a “rare combination of size, athleticism, pass-catching and blocking skills,” making him a valuable asset as a three-down back. He was considered one of the most complete running backs to enter the NFL since Adrian Peterson in 2007.

title: Raghav Juyal
text:
Raghav Juyal, born on July 10, 1991, is a multi-talented Indian performer working as an actor, dancer, choreographer, and television presenter. He initially gained widespread recognition as a contestant on the dance reality show *Dance India Dance 3* in 2012. Despite not being initially selected for the Top 18, public demand and the intervention of judge Mithun Chakraborty brought him back as a “trump card,” ultimately leading him to the second runner-up position with a significant number of votes. He became known for his unique dance style and popularized the “Slow Motion Walk” in India, a move that distinguished him from other dancers.

Following his success on *Dance India Dance*, Juyal became a skipper on *DID Li’l Masters 2*, successfully guiding both of his students to the Grand Finale. He continued in a leadership role, captaining a team to victory on *Dance Ke Superkids*.  He transitioned into acting with a role in the 2014 comedy *Sonali Cable*, where critics praised his vibrant performance and screen presence, with some stating he outshone the leads. He then appeared in the dance film *ABCD 2* in 2015.

Juyal has become a prominent television host, presenting several seasons of the dance reality show *Dance Plus* on Star Plus. He also hosted or co-hosted other shows including *Prem Ki Diwali*, *Khatron Ke Khiladi 7*, *Star Parivaar Awards*, *Colors Golden Petal Awards*, *Timeless Aisha*, *Rising Star*, *Dance Champions*, *Dil Hai Hindustani*, and *Dance Plus* seasons 4 and 5. 

His film career continued with roles in *Nawabzaade* (2018), *Street Dancer 3D* (2020), and *Bahut Hua Samman* (2020), the latter of which garnered positive reviews.  He also ventured into darker roles, appearing in the second season of the web series *Abhay* as a negative character.  He starred in the romantic movie *Wedlock* which was scheduled for release in August 2021 and was also part of the cast of *Yudhra*, a film produced by Excel Entertainment, slated for release in 2022. Most recently, in 2024, he starred in the action thriller *Kill* and won an IIFA Award in 2025 for Best Performance in a Negative Role.

Raghav Juyal was born and raised in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, to parents Deepak Juyal, a lawyer, and Alka Bakshi Juyal. He is of Garhwali Brahmin descent and attended Doon International School and DAV (PG) College. He is self-taught in dance, learning through observation of performances online and on television, and was mentored in acting by Saurabh Sachdeva.

title: Aaron Burr
text:
Aaron Burr Jr., born in Newark, New Jersey in 1756, was a prominent figure in early American history, serving as the third Vice President under Thomas Jefferson from 1801 to 1805. His life was marked by both political success and significant controversy, ultimately ending his career in public service. He came from a distinguished family; his father was a Presbyterian minister and president of Princeton University, and his maternal grandfather was the theologian Jonathan Edwards. Orphaned at a young age, Burr received an education at Princeton University, followed by legal training in Connecticut.

Burr actively participated in the American Revolutionary War, distinguishing himself with bravery and resourcefulness, notably during the campaign to Quebec and at the Battle of Monmouth. He served on George Washington’s staff but a perceived slight regarding commendation fostered a lasting resentment. Following the war, he established a successful legal practice in New York City and quickly became involved in politics, joining the emerging Jeffersonian Democratic-Republican Party. He served as a New York State Attorney General and later as a U.S. Senator from 1791 to 1797. 

The 1800 presidential election resulted in a tie between Burr and Thomas Jefferson. The decision ultimately went to the House of Representatives, where Jefferson was elected President, leaving Burr as Vice President. Though he claimed to support Jefferson, their relationship was strained, and Burr was not chosen as Jefferson's running mate in the subsequent election, largely due to the passage of the 12th Amendment. He then turned his attention to the American frontier, seeking new opportunities.

Burr’s ambitions led to accusations of treason. He was arrested in 1807 and twice put on trial for allegedly conspiring to create an independent nation, but was acquitted each time. Before and during these trials, Burr founded the Manhattan Company in 1799, initially presented as a water company but secretly chartered as a bank, a move that further damaged his reputation and fueled his rivalry with Alexander Hamilton. This conflict culminated in the infamous 1804 duel between Burr and Hamilton, in which Hamilton was mortally wounded. Though indicted for dueling, Burr escaped conviction. 

Following the duel, Burr left the United States for a period, traveling in Europe. He returned in 1812 and resumed his law practice in New York City, living a relatively quiet life until his death in 1836 at the age of 80. Despite a career filled with accomplishments, Burr remains a controversial figure, remembered as much for his ambition and the duel with Hamilton as for his contributions to the early republic.

title: Uee
text:
Kim Yu-jin, known professionally as Uee, was born on April 9, 1988, in Daejeon, South Korea. She initially aimed for an acting career but debuted as a singer, joining the girl group Five Girls in 2007. This group disbanded shortly after formation due to financial difficulties within their agency. Before her breakthrough, she gained public attention as “Mok-dong Girl” after being filmed at her baseball player father’s game, and later for her resemblance to actress Moon Geun-young.

Uee officially debuted as a member of the popular girl group After School in 2009. Simultaneously, she began her acting career with a role in the historical drama *Queen Seondeok*, which proved successful. She quickly gained recognition, also appearing in *You’re Beautiful* and as part of the project group 4Tomorrow. Her popularity continued with roles in dramas like *Birdie Buddy* and *Ojakgyo Family* in 2011, the latter earning her Best New Actress awards. She also released her first solo single, “Sok Sok Sok,” and became a co-host on the variety show *Night After Night*.

Throughout the early to mid-2010s, Uee balanced her music and acting careers. She hosted the music show *Music Bank* and took on leading roles in *Jeon Woo-chi*, *Golden Rainbow*, and *Hogu’s Love*. She participated in survival shows *Law of the Jungle* and *Barefooted Friends*, even co-writing and performing the song "Hero" for the latter. While enjoying success, she expressed a desire to be recognized solely for her acting skill and to move away from being labelled an “idol-turned-actor.”

In 2017, Uee left After School after eight years and signed with a new agency. She continued to pursue acting, with roles in *Manhole*, *My Contracted Husband, Mr. Oh*, and *My Only One*. She then signed with King Entertainment, followed by Lucky Company, appearing in shows like *Cabin Crew Season 2* and *I Live Alone*, showcasing her everyday life. She also hosted the 2020 Live in DMZ Concert and currently hosts the fitness program *Last Fit with U-ie*. 

Uee has been open about facing criticism regarding her weight and online harassment, with her agency taking legal action against malicious commenters in 2018. She has also dated actors Lee Sang-yoon and Kangnam, though both relationships ended after a period of time. Beyond her entertainment career, Uee demonstrated her philanthropic side with a significant donation to support young women’s hygiene and well-being in 2022.

title: Manny Pacquiao
text:
Emmanuel “Manny” Pacquiao, born December 17, 1978, is a Filipino professional boxer, businessman, and former politician widely considered one of the greatest boxers of all time. He achieved a remarkable career, winning twelve major world titles across eight different weight divisions – a feat unmatched in boxing history. He is also the first boxer to win titles in four of the “glamour divisions” – flyweight, featherweight, lightweight, and welterweight – and the first to hold world championships across four decades: the 1990s, 2000s, 2010s, and 2020s. His fights generated $1.2 billion in revenue by 2015, and he was ranked among the highest-paid athletes globally in 2012, 2015, and throughout the 2010s. In 2024, ESPN named him the greatest Asian athlete of the 21st century, and he is slated for induction into the International Boxing Hall of Fame in 2025.

Pacquiao’s early life was marked by poverty. Born to Rosalio and Dionisia Pacquiao, he experienced his parents’ separation during his childhood and moved to Manila at 14, working as a construction worker to support his family. Despite dropping out of high school due to financial hardship, he later obtained his high school diploma through an equivalency exam in 2007. He began boxing at age 12, inspired by a televised fight, and quickly rose through the ranks, turning professional at 16. His professional record stands at 62-8-2 with 39 knockouts, and he was hailed by boxing historian Bert Sugar as the greatest southpaw fighter ever.

Beyond boxing, Pacquiao entered politics in 2010, being elected as the representative of Sarangani province and serving until 2016. He then became a senator of the Philippines, holding office until 2022. He briefly led the PDP–Laban party, and in 2021 ran for President of the Philippines, but was unsuccessful. Following his unsuccessful Senate bid, he announced his retirement from politics and a return to boxing.

Pacquiao’s interests extend beyond sports and politics. He was a player-coach for the Philippine Basketball Association team Kia/Mahindra from 2014 to 2017, and later founded the Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League. He’s also appeared in films and hosted television shows.  A multi-talented individual, Pacquiao has released platinum-selling music albums, with a cover of “Sometimes When We Touch” reaching the Billboard Adult Contemporary chart. He is also an Evangelical Christian preacher and a philanthropist, dedicated to charitable work. 

Throughout his career, Pacquiao defeated 22 world champions, earning numerous accolades including “Fighter of the Decade” for the 2000s. He has six Guinness World Records, including the most consecutive boxing world title fight victories at different weights and the oldest welterweight boxing world champion. While he never competed in the Olympics, he served as the Philippine flag bearer in 2008, and considered competing in 2016 and 2024, though age restrictions ultimately prevented his participation. His financial success is also notable, having been listed amongst the world’s highest-paid athletes multiple times. In July 2024, he participated in an exhibition match, demonstrating his continued passion for the sport.

title: Martha Cunz
text:
Martha Cunz, born in St. Gallen, Switzerland in 1876 and passing away in 1961, was a Swiss artist primarily recognized for her work as a printmaker. She achieved prominence as one of the first European artists of the 20th century to fully embrace and master the modernist woodcut, and her techniques proved influential to other artists working in the field. 

Cunz received the majority of her artistic education at the Women’s Art School in Munich. There, she studied under Christian Landenberger, Ludwig Schmid-Reutte, and Peter Paul Müller. She furthered her studies in Paris in 1900 with Luc-Olivier Merson and Lucien Simon. Upon returning to Munich the following year, a lithography course led by Ernst Neumann ignited her passion for printmaking. She quickly transitioned to woodcuts, and by 1903, she was a founding member of the German Association of Graphics.

For a considerable period before World War I, Cunz maintained a residence in Munich, making annual visits back to Switzerland. During this time, she travelled throughout Europe, with notable periods spent in Holland in 1904 and 1911, and in Italy in 1914. In 1920, she established a studio at her parents’ home in St. Gallen, where she lived and worked for the rest of her life.

Cunz’s artistic output initially focused on lithographs and, more notably, woodcuts, particularly color woodcuts. She pioneered the use of a Japanese multi-block technique for color printing in Europe. Her style is distinguished by the use of subtly graded, contrasting colors layered to create a luminous effect on the print’s surface. Her work began to gain recognition around 1905, with inclusion in the annual Glass Palace Exhibition in Munich. Early woodcuts were also published in the journal *Deutsche Kunst und Dekoration* in April 1905, alongside pieces by artists like Wassily Kandinsky. 

She produced a total of 71 woodcuts, with the last one completed in 1927, and her final lithographs were created in 1931. Following this, Cunz shifted her focus to painting for approximately two decades, concentrating on landscapes and portraits. She influenced the work of artists like Carl Thiemann and also shared her expertise by teaching printmaking, with Rosa Paul among her students. Several sources detail her life and work, including a dissertation by Daniel Studer from the University of Zürich, and exhibition catalogs focusing on her art and the broader context of Jugendstil (Art Nouveau) printmaking.

title: Kaká
text:
Ricardo Izecson dos Santos Leite, widely known as Kaká, is a Brazilian former professional footballer celebrated as one of the greatest players of all time. Born in 1982 in Gama, Brazil, to a financially stable family, he began his football journey at age eight with São Paulo, progressing through their youth academy. He made his professional debut with São Paulo in 2001, quickly establishing himself with 23 goals in 58 appearances before attracting European attention.

In 2003, Kaká moved to AC Milan for a modest fee, where he experienced the peak of his career. He immediately contributed to a Serie A title and became a key figure, renowned for his pace, dribbling, passing, and goal-scoring ability. The 2006-07 season brought him the Champions League title, where he was a crucial part of the team, even though he didn’t score in the final. This success propelled him to individual accolades including the FIFA World Player of the Year, the Ballon d'Or, and UEFA Club Footballer of the Year. He was a consistent performer for Milan, winning the Serie A Footballer of the Year award in both 2004 and 2008, and was frequently named to the FIFA World XI and UEFA Team of the Year.

In 2009, Kaká transferred to Real Madrid for a then-second highest fee of €67 million. However, his time in Madrid was hampered by persistent injuries, impacting his previously explosive pace and overall performance. After four seasons, he returned to AC Milan for a single season in 2013 before moving to Orlando City SC in Major League Soccer. He had a brief loan spell back at São Paulo before permanently joining Orlando City, where he ultimately retired in 2017.

Alongside his club success, Kaká enjoyed a distinguished international career with Brazil. He debuted for the national team in 2002 and was part of the World Cup-winning squad that year. He also participated in the 2006 and 2010 World Cups, and was a member of Brazil's victorious 2005 and 2009 FIFA Confederations Cup teams, earning the Golden Ball award in 2009 as the tournament's best player.

Beyond his on-field achievements, Kaká was a significant figure off the pitch. He became the first sportsperson to reach 10 million followers on Twitter and was recognized for his humanitarian work as the youngest ambassador for the UN World Food Programme in 2004. His overall contributions earned him recognition from *Time* magazine as one of the world’s 100 most influential people in both 2008 and 2009. He attributes his faith as central to his full recovery from a serious spinal fracture sustained in a swimming pool accident when 18 years old.

title: Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland
text:
Prince Carl Philip, Duke of Värmland, born on May 13, 1979, is the only son and second of three children of King Carl XVI Gustaf and Queen Silvia of Sweden. He is currently fourth in the line of succession to the Swedish throne, following his sister Crown Princess Victoria, niece Princess Estelle, and nephew Prince Oscar. He resides in Villa Solbacken, Stockholm, with his wife Princess Sofia and their four children.

For a brief period, Prince Carl Philip was the heir apparent to the Swedish throne after his birth, holding the title of Crown Prince. However, a constitutional change in 1980, shifting to absolute primogeniture, changed the succession, making his sister Victoria the heir. He received his early education at Västerled parish preschool and then attended Smedslättsskolan and Ålstensskolan in Bromma, before completing his senior studies at Enskilda Gymnasiet in Stockholm. He was confirmed in 1994 and later studied at Kent School and Lundsbergs upper secondary school, graduating in 1999. Further studies included a year at the Rhode Island School of Design focusing on graphic design and completion of an Agricultural and Rural Management degree at the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences in 2011. Like his father and sister, Prince Carl Philip has dyslexia. 

The Prince has a variety of interests, including scouting and outdoor activities. He actively participates in sports such as football, swimming, sailing, and skiing, and notably completed the Vasaloppet, a challenging cross-country ski race. He shares a passion for car racing with his great-uncle, Prince Bertil, and competes in the Porsche Carrera Cup Scandinavia and the Scandinavian Touring Car Championship. He also completed his military service with the Amphibious Battalion and progressed through the ranks to Major by 2014.  He continues to pursue his interest in design, co-founding the company Bernadotte & Kylberg in 2012.

Prince Carl Philip is involved in numerous charitable and public activities. He and Princess Sofia established a foundation dedicated to combating bullying. He also founded the Prince Carl Philip Racing Cup to support young karting talents and frequently visits companies with the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences. He serves as a patron for several organizations, including The Swedish National Dyslexia Association and The International Union for Conservation of Nature.

He was in a long-term relationship with Emma Pernald from 1999 to 2009 before becoming linked to Sofia Hellqvist in 2010. They married in 2015 and have four children: Prince Alexander, Prince Gabriel, Prince Julian, and Princess Ines.  In 2019, his father rescinded the royal status of his two eldest sons to allow them greater freedom in their future choices, though they remain princes and in the line of succession. 

Prince Carl Philip holds a number of national and foreign honours, including being a Knight and Commander of the Royal Order of the Seraphim, and has received numerous commemorative medals.  His coat of arms incorporates elements of the Swedish greater coat of arms, the House of Bjälbo, and the arms of Värmland, reflecting his ducal title.

title: Tim Ferguson
text:
Tim Ferguson, born in 1963, is a multi-talented Australian entertainer working as a comedian, film director, screenwriter, author, and screenwriting teacher. He spent part of his childhood in Singapore before moving to a rural property near Perthville, New South Wales, the son of a prominent war correspondent and television executive. His education included time at All Saints College, Bathurst, followed by the alternative School Without Walls and Narrabundah College in Canberra.

Ferguson first gained recognition as a member of the musical comedy trio, Doug Anthony All Stars (DAAS), alongside Richard Fidler and Paul McDermott. The group found success on British television with shows like *Friday Night Live* and *DAAS Kapital*, and later starred in the Australian show *The Big Gig*. He continued with solo projects, appearing on *Funky Squad* and hosting the Logie Award-winning *Don't Forget Your Toothbrush*. He also published the novel *Left, Right and Centre* in 1997 and starred in commercials for the Nintendo 64. He co-created and hosted the comedy clip show *Unreal TV* for eight series, and was a co-writer and co-producer of the sitcom *Shock Jock*. Demonstrating his comedic writing skills, he penned an alternative preamble to the Australian Constitution, known for its irreverent tone.

Since 2000, Ferguson has expanded into filmmaking, co-directing the romantic comedy *Spin Out* and co-writing *The BBQ* starring Shane Jacobson and Magda Szubanski. He has also acted in films like *Fat Pizza* and *That’s Not My Dog!*. The Doug Anthony All Stars reformed in 2014, winning the Edinburgh Festival Spirit of the Fringe Award in 2016 and continuing to tour internationally. He has also performed in stage shows, including *The Rocky Horror Show* and his own stand-up shows, most notably *Fast Life On Wheels*, which raised awareness for disability employment and housing. He co-hosts the award-winning podcast *Bunga Bunga*. 

Ferguson is dedicated to teaching comedy screenwriting, having lectured at institutions including NYU Sydney, the Screen Academy Scotland, and RMIT University. He is the author of *The Cheeky Monkey – Writing Narrative Comedy*, a guide to comedic writing, and writes a satirical column, *The Ferguson Report*, for *The New Daily*. He has also been involved in producing orchestral performance pieces like *Billie & The Dinosaurs*. 

A significant part of Ferguson’s recent work involves advocacy and raising awareness for disability issues. Diagnosed with multiple sclerosis (MS) in his teens, and now a wheelchair user, he is an ambassador for several organizations including The Human Rights Commission for Disability and MS Australia. He has written an autobiography, *Carry a Big Stick*, detailing his life with MS, and launched the MS Australia Connections Hub. He campaigned successfully for mandatory accessibility standards in building codes. He also hosts a podcast featuring people with disabilities. He publicly apologized for abusive letters sent to a television critic in 1990.

Beyond his entertainment and advocacy work, Ferguson also briefly entered politics, running as an independent candidate in the 1990 and 2013 federal elections. He is also a collector of Star Wars toys, owning one of the largest collections in the southern hemisphere.

title: Kiara Advani
text:
Kiara Advani, born Alia Advani on July 31, 1991, is a leading Indian actress working in both Hindi and Telugu cinema. She is among the highest-paid actresses in India and has received an IIFA Award and two Zee Cine Awards, with nominations for two Filmfare Awards recognizing her work. Her acting journey began with the 2014 film *Fugly*, which didn’t perform well, but she persevered. A significant turning point came with *M.S. Dhoni: The Untold Story* (2016), where she portrayed cricketer MS Dhoni’s wife, Sakshi Rawat, achieving commercial success.
